article_content: An adult film actress who fractured her foot after being thrown from the roof of a Hollywood mansion by millionaire poker player Dan Bilzerian now appears determined to hold him accountable. A video captured adult film star Janice Griffith, 18, being tossed naked into a pool by Bilzerian — nicknamed 'Instagram's Biggest Playboy' — during a photo shoot at his sprawling Hollywood Hills home on Wednesday. But the stunt went awry: as Griffith descended, she allegedly grabbed onto Bilzerian’s shirt and struck the edge of the pool, fracturing her foot. Taking it easy: Griffith later posted a photo on Twitter of herself resting at home after the injury. On Friday, Griffith spoke with TMZ via Skype, saying the accident cost her several job opportunities, including a scheduled shoot for Kink.com. She expects to be sidelined for another two weeks. She tweeted to her 45,000 followers: 'I just want to get back to work... that's my only concern. Anyone trying to book a girl with a broken foot?' Griffith declined to discuss details of the rooftop stunt but admitted, 'Looking back on it, it's not the best idea we've ever had. It seemed like a good idea at the time.' She expressed surprise she didn’t land fully in the pool, noting she weighs only about 90 pounds. She emphasized that no drugs or alcohol were involved. When asked if she had hired an attorney, she replied, 'I’m still sorting everything out.' What upset her most, she said, was that Bilzerian — whom she met for the first time that day — never apologized. 'I did not ever hear sorry from him,' she said. The video, shared on LiveLeak, shows Bilzerian lifting Griffith over his shoulder and hurling her toward the pool. She can be heard screaming as she falls, striking the pool edge before hitting the water. Later, she tweeted: 'I broke my foot today.' On Thursday, she added: 'I was looking forward to shooting for @SexAndSub SO bad today, stupid broken foot.' Bilzerian, however, refused to take blame. He retweeted a post saying: 'Dan Bilzerian was almost murdered by a naked female that tried to pull him off a rooftop hahaha good thing he's part hulk.' Bilzerian is reportedly worth $100 million, having earned his fortune through high-stakes poker. He won the 2009 World Series of Poker and co-founded the online poker site Victory Poker. Before gambling, he served in the U.S. Navy and left SEAL training two days before graduation after offending an officer — he received an honorable discharge. He owns homes in Las Vegas, San Diego, and Los Angeles. His Instagram features lavish displays of cash, guns, supercars with plates reading 'SUCK IT,' and scantily clad women — many of whom appear to be fans or models. He once told MailOnline: 'Basically I didn't get a ton of attention as a kid, I guess that's why I'm such a flashy lunatic.' His lifestyle has led to serious health consequences, including a double heart attack and a pulmonary embolism. He claims he is now planning a different life path. Bilzerian has partially funded films like Lone Survivor and has small roles in The Other Woman and The Equalizer. He is also developing a horror film. In efforts to rebrand from 'playboy' to 'gentleman of poker,' he donated $100,000 to Typhoon Haiyan victims and $20,000 to a family who adopted four children with severe birth defects — though one child later developed leukemia.

article_content: In the wake of explosive revelations from The Guardian and The Washington Post, U.S. intelligence chief James R. Clapper defended two controversial surveillance programs—PRISM and the bulk collection of Verizon phone records—as vital, legal, and tightly monitored tools to protect Americans from terrorism and cyber threats. Clapper emphasized that these programs aren’t secret backdoors, but court-approved operations authorized under the Patriot Act and FISA Section 702, with oversight from Congress, the courts, and the White House. While tech giants like Google, Microsoft, and Facebook publicly denied handing over direct access to user data, the NSA clarified that it obtains information only after judicial approval—and with the providers’ awareness. A newly disclosed NSA tool, Boundless Informant, revealed the agency gathered nearly 3 billion data points from U.S. networks in just 30 days before March 2013, mapping intelligence by country. Clapper called media coverage ‘reckless’ for omitting crucial context about legal safeguards, warning that exposing operational details could help adversaries evade detection. He acknowledged that public perception has been skewed, but stressed that correcting misinformation would require revealing even more classified methods. To improve transparency, the NSA released a fact sheet clarifying that U.S. citizens’ communications can’t be targeted without a valid foreign intelligence purpose and proof the target is overseas. President Obama, speaking in California, echoed Clapper’s stance, admitting he once doubted these programs but concluded—after rigorous review—that they’re indispensable. 'You can’t have 100% security and 100% privacy,' he said. 'Society must make trade-offs.'

Clapper benadruk dat hierdie programme nie geheime agterdeure is nie, maar hofgoedgekeurde operasies wat onder die Patriot Act en FISA-seksie 702 geagtig is, met toesig deur die Kongres, die hof en die Wit Huis. Terwyl tegnologie-giants soos Google, Microsoft en Facebook openlik ontken het dat hulle direkte toegang tot gebruikersdata gegee het, het die NSA verduidelik dat dit inligting slegs verkry na regspraak en met die kennis van die diensverskaffers. 'n Nog onthulde NSA-hulpmiddel, Boundless Informant, het getoon dat die agentskap naby 3 miljard datapunte van Amerikaanse netwerke in net 30 dae voor Maart 2013 versamel het, met inligting per land gekarteer. Clapper het media-verslaggewing 'onverantwoord' genoem omdat dit kritiese konteks oor wettige veiligheidmaatreëls weglaat, en gewaarsku dat die blootlegging van operasionele detail vijanden kan help om opsporing te ontwyk. Hy het erken dat die openbare persepsie verdraai is, maar beklemtoon dat korreksie van misinligting meer geklassifiseerde inligting sou vereis. Om transparansie te verbeter, het die NSA 'n feiteblad uitgereik wat duidelik maak dat die kommunikasie van Amerikaanse burgers nie doelgerig kan word sonder 'n geldige buitelandse intelligensiedoeleindes en bewys dat die doelwit buite die VSA is nie. President Obama, wat in Kalifornië gespreek het, het Clapper se standpunt ondersteun, toegegee dat hy eers aan hierdie programme getwyfel het, maar ná grondige hersiening gevolgtrek het dat hulle onvervangbaar is. 'Jy kan nie 100% sekuriteit en 100% privaatheid hê nie,' het hy gesê. 'Sosietey moet keuses maak.'

article_content: Built to slash carbon emissions and save tens of thousands of pounds in energy costs, Scotland’s first solar meadow opened today at Edinburgh College’s Midlothian campus in Dalkeith — despite grey skies and steady rain. The five-acre site, featuring 2,500 solar panels, is one of Europe’s most northerly solar installations. Designed by SSE Energy Solutions at a cost of £1.2 million, it is projected to reduce the college’s annual carbon emissions by 300,000kg and fully meet its electricity demand. While dignitaries — including local MSP Colin Beattie, staff, students, and business leaders — walked the grounds under umbrellas and in high-vis jackets, the solar panels continued generating power, even under overcast conditions. Beyond energy production, the meadow is being cultivated with native wildflowers and grasses to enhance local biodiversity. Organizers hope it will evolve into a public attraction and educational hub. Professor Steve Tinsley, Vice-Principal of Edinburgh College and lead on the project, said: 'We believe the solar meadow not only looks great but will become a significant draw for locals and visitors alike. It’s also fantastic that this initiative has allowed us to engage schools and community groups in developing their own renewable energy projects — giving back in more ways than one.' The site will serve as an outdoor classroom for engineering students, monitoring real-time panel performance and environmental factors like weather and pollen. A research assistant from Edinburgh Napier University will join the team to analyze data on the interaction between solar technology and ecology. Student Alana Beaton, studying NC Intermediate Electrical Engineering, shared: 'I’m really interested in renewable energy, and I’m excited that Edinburgh College is leading the way. I can’t wait to use the solar meadow in my coursework — it’ll deepen my understanding of solar tech and modern engineering in Scotland.' Richard Chandler, SSE’s Head of Green Deal and Energy Solutions, added: 'The solar meadow will generate around 560,000 kWh annually — enough to power 170 homes — and stands as a powerful example of how industry and education can collaborate for lasting impact.' A 2015 Stanford University study noted that while manufacturing solar panels — especially melting silica at 3,000°F using coal-powered electricity — requires substantial energy, the industry is now on track to achieve net energy payback by 2015–2020. This means the solar meadow, once operational, will begin delivering clean energy beyond its initial carbon footprint.

Organiseerders hoop dat dit 'n publieke aantrekking en opvoedkundige sentrum sal word. Professor Steve Tinsley, Vise-Prinsipaal van Edinburgh College en leier van die projek, het gesê: 'Ons glo die sonweide lyk nie net goed nie, maar sal 'n beduidende aantrekking vir plaaslikes en besoekers wees. Dit is ook wonderlik dat hierdie initiatief ons laat betrokke raak by skole en gemeenskapsgroepe om hul eie hernubare energieprojekte te ontwikkel — en op meer as een manier terug te gee.' Student Alana Beaton, wat NC Intermediêre Elektriese Ingenieurswese studeer, het gesê: 'Ek is baie belanggesteld in hernubare energie, en ek is opgewonde dat Edinburgh College die padbreekster is. Ek kan nie wag om die sonweide in my kursus te gebruik nie — dit sal my begrip van son tegnologie en moderne ingenieurswese in Skotland verbeter.' Richard Chandler, SSE se Hoof van Groen Deal en Energietegnologie, het bygevoeg: 'Die sonweide sal ongeveer 560.000 kWh per jaar genereer — genoeg om 170 huise te voorsien — en is 'n kragtige voorbeeld van hoe industrie en opvoeding saamwerk vir duurzaamheid.' 'n 2015 Stanford-onderzoek het aangedui dat hoewel die vervaardiging van sonpanele — veral die smelt van silika by 3.000°F met koolkrag — groot hoeveelhede energie vereis, die industrie nou op pad is om sy energiedebiet te betaal tussen 2015 en 2020. Dit beteken dat die sonweide, sodra dit in werking is, skoon energie sal lewer wat verder gaan as sy oorspronklike koolstof-voetafdruk.'

article_content: A 17-year-old trainee beautician, Emily Wilding, who is blind in one eye, had a large section of her ponytail cut off when two boys approached her from behind and used scissors to sever her hair. The incident occurred around 5 p.m. as she walked home along Castle Street in Northwich, Cheshire, after finishing her shift at a restaurant. One of the suspects fled into a nearby park after the attack. Emily’s mother, Karen Wilding, said Emily returned home panicked, exclaiming, 'Mum, I think someone just cut my hair.' Initially dismissing it, Karen was shocked when a large chunk of hair came away in her hand. 'She was devastated. Her hair means so much to her, and she’s very conscious of its length. She always asks me to check it,' Karen said. According to police, Emily heard a snipping sound as the suspects passed her. She described them as wearing hoodies. One wore a grey tracksuit with white trainers; the other wore a blue tracksuit with black trainers. Both are white, under five feet tall, and had their hoods pulled up. Karen expressed relief that the attack didn’t result in more serious harm: 'It could have been much worse. She’s blind in one eye already — if she’d turned around, they could have targeted her other eye and caused permanent blindness.' The trauma has deeply affected Emily’s confidence. She has withdrawn from social activities and now fears leaving the house. As a trainee beautician at Hartford College, where appearance is central to professional credibility, the incident has been especially devastating. This is not the first time Emily has been targeted. Last year, a man approached her on the same route and asked her to accompany him before fleeing. Police were called then too. Since the attack, the local community has shown strong support. A local hairdresser has offered Emily a free haircut and hair extensions. Cheshire Constabulary has appealed for witnesses or anyone with information about the suspects to come forward. No connection between Emily and the attackers has been established. Anyone with details is urged to call 101.

article_content: In a devastating blow to wildlife conservation, 33 elephants were brutally killed in Garamba National Park, located in northeastern Congo near the borders of South Sudan and the Central African Republic. The massacre, which included ten elephants slain last Friday, has triggered renewed concern over the possible role of the Lord’s Resistance Army (LRA). Park rangers responded with force over the weekend, killing three suspected poachers in a violent clash. African Parks, the NGO managing the reserve alongside Congolese authorities, noted that the killings appear coordinated and targeted — with tusks and genitalia removed, echoing a pattern seen in a deadly 2012 attack long suspected — though never proven — to involve the LRA. Peter Fearnhead, CEO of African Parks, pointed to the Azande hunting domain as a known LRA stronghold, suggesting the group could be sourcing ivory to trade for arms and food. Yet he stressed it’s still unclear if the LRA, Sudanese criminal networks, or local poachers are behind this surge. Local voices challenge the assumption. Rev Benoit Kinalegu, a Catholic priest who tracks LRA activity from nearby Dungu, insists the killings were carried out by skilled professionals, not the ragtag rebels the world remembers. 'This area is too militarized,' he said, 'to say who did it.' Meanwhile, a 5,000-member African Union task force, backed by 100 U.S. Special Forces, continues its hunt for Joseph Kony, the LRA’s fugitive leader, wanted by the ICC for war crimes. Though Kony is believed to be hiding in a contested zone of South Sudan, his followers still roam the remote borderlands. The LRA, once a rebel force in northern Uganda, has long been accused of horrific atrocities — including child abduction, sexual slavery, and mutilation — all under Kony’s claim of divine mission. But while the group’s past ties to ivory trafficking are documented, experts warn against rushing to judgment as new actors emerge in the shadowy trade.

Die massa-moord, wat tien olifante insluit wat vrydag vermoor is, het herhaalde betrekkinge tot die moontlike rol van die Heer se Verzetleër (LRA) uitgelos. Parkeerwagters het oor die weekend met geweld gereageer en drie verdagtes vermoor in 'n gewelddadige botsing. African Parks, die NGK wat die reservaat bestuur saam met Kongolese owerhede, het opgemerk dat die moorde geïnstrueerd en doelgerig lyk — met sterte en geslagsdele verwyder, wat 'n patroon nagemaak wat gesien is in 'n dodelike aanval in 2012 wat lank vermoed — maar nooit bewys — is om die LRA te betrek. Peter Fearnhead, CEO van African Parks, het na die Azande jagdomein gewys as 'n bekende LRA-basis, en voorgestel dat die groep olifantebeen kan gebruik om wapens en kos te koop. Hy het egter beklemtoon dat dit nog nie duidelik is of die LRA, Soedanese kriminele netwerke of plaaslike jagters agter hierdie toename is nie. Plaaslike stemme uitdaag die aannames. Rev Benoit Kinalegu, 'n Katolieke predikant wat LRA-aktiwiteite vanaf nabygeleë Dungu volg, beweer dat die moorde deur geskoolde professionele jaggers uitgevoer is, nie deur die los-gevormde rebelle wat die wêreld onthou nie. 'Hierdie gebied is te militariseer,' het hy gesê, 'om te sê wie dit gedoen het.' Onderwyl 'n 5 000-man sterke Afrika-Unie-taakmag, ondersteun deur 100 Amerikaanse Spesiale Magte, voortgaan met die jag op Joseph Kony, die LRA’s vlugtige leier, wat deur die ICC vir oorlogsmisdade gesog word. Alhoewel Kony vermoed word om in 'n omstrede gebied van Suid-Soedan te skuil, steeds sy volgelinge in die afgeleë grensgebiede rondloop. Die LRA, ooit 'n rebellekrag in noordelike Oeganda, is lankal beskuldig van gruwelike misdrywe — insluitend kinderontvoering, seksuele slawery en verstommeling — almal onder Kony se bewering van goddelike sending. Maar terwyl die groep se verlede skakels met olifantebeenhandel gedokumenteer is, waarsku ekspernte daarteen om te haastig te oordeel terwyl nuwe akteurs in die skaduwee-handel opduik.

article_content: England’s final World Cup warm-up match ended in a 0-0 draw against Honduras in Miami, a game interrupted by a 30-minute delay due to a sudden electrical storm. While the result wasn’t thrilling, manager Roy Hodgson found reasons to be encouraged — particularly from the performances of Ross Barkley and Jack Wilshere, who came off the bench in the second half and injected fresh energy into England’s attack. Both midfielders looked lively, creating chances and pushing Honduras back, though the team ultimately couldn’t convert their dominance into goals. The biggest disappointment? The absence of Raheem Sterling, who was suspended after receiving a red card in the previous match against Ecuador. Hodgson told ITV that Sterling’s dribbling prowess in tight spaces could have been decisive in such a tightly contested game. Still, he emphasized that avoiding injuries and gaining experience against Central American opponents made the outing worthwhile. 'It’s time for the real thing now,' Hodgson said, reflecting on a productive three-week preparation period that, despite the lack of goals, left the squad in good shape heading into the tournament.

article_content: An Australian Muslim convert, Musa Cerantonio, who once claimed to be the third most 'liked' extremist preacher on Facebook, has announced his intention to travel to Syria to join ISIS. Born Robert Cerantonio to an Italian father and an Irish mother, he converted to Islam at age 17 after becoming disillusioned with Catholicism — particularly disturbed by Michelangelo’s Sistine Chapel frescoes, which he called 'idol worship.' He reportedly renounced his Australian citizenship and has lived in the Philippines since 2013. On Twitter, he posted: 'Insha'Allah, I will be arriving in Ash-Sham very shortly; keep us in your du'a as I prepare to travel,' using the Arabic name for Syria. His announcement drew widespread support from followers, some of whom appear to already be in Syria or Iraq. One joked about eating 'the khilafah’s finest falafel' when he arrives. Cerantonio has long used social media to recruit for global jihad, promoting the idea of uniting Muslims under a caliphate governed by Sharia law. A 2014 study by the International Centre for the Study of Radicalisation found that one in four foreign fighters followed his Twitter account, and his Facebook page ranked as the third most 'liked' among jihadist networks. He has openly mocked the Australian Federal Police, posting on Facebook: 'So apparently the AFP are looking for me — let’s see how well they can hunt. Have fun finding me; I’ll be waiting for you — or whichever dogs you send.' His follower Salafi Manhaj responded: 'HAHAHAHA lol good luck for them. May Allah always keep you safe, my dear beloved brother.' Cerantonio once hosted the English-language TV show 'Ask the Sheikh' from Egypt, answering questions about Islam. He has five siblings and two daughters, Aisha and Sophia, who converted to Islam alongside their family around 2002. In a 2011 video, he described his Catholic upbringing as superficial: 'We were Christian by name, but we didn’t really do much — we only went to church at Christmas or Easter.' He criticized the lack of spiritual practice in his former faith: 'I used to love hearing about all the gods... but I never had the access to turn that love into action.' The Australian Federal Police are investigating him for inciting Australians to join the conflict in Syria. While Cerantonio’s ideology is widely condemned by mainstream Muslim scholars and communities globally, his online influence persists. More than 1,000 Iraqis have fled Mosul and Tal Afar following ISIS occupation.

article_content: A two-year-old boy is lucky to be alive, thanks to the quick thinking of two onlookers, after his pram rolled down a train platform and onto the tracks. Dramatic CCTV footage has now been released showing the terrifying moment at Melbourne’s Camberwell train station at around 3:00 PM on Saturday, when the pram plunged onto the tracks. The mother had bent down to pick up an item she dropped and let go of the pram for just a second—when it began rolling toward the edge. The footage shows the pram tipping over heavily onto the tracks. Swiftly acting, two onlookers from a nearby platform rushed to the child’s aid. The mother also jumped down onto the tracks, grabbed her two-year-old son, and hugged him tightly. There were no scheduled trains at the time, and it was confirmed the boy suffered no injuries. When ambulance crews arrived, they found the child safely back on the platform. His parents took him to Box Hill Hospital for observation. He was in stable condition. A police media spokesperson said officers spoke to the mother following reports she had refused medical treatment for the child and was allegedly drunk—but no further action will be taken. As the mother hugged her son after the ordeal, onlookers helped return the pram to the platform.

article_content: Next week, two significant Indian firms — IREDA and Tata Technologies — are set to launch landmark initial public offerings, collectively aiming to raise more than ₹5,000 crore. IREDA, a public sector unit under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, will kick off its IPO on November 21 with a price range of ₹30–32 per share. Each bid lot consists of 460 shares, and the subscription window closes on November 23. Recognized as India’s largest dedicated green financing non-banking financial company, IREDA holds multiple historic firsts: it issued the country’s very first green masala bond listed on the IFSC exchange and was the first Indian financial institution to raise climate-focused funds from international development finance institutions. Meanwhile, Tata Technologies — the first company from the Tata Group to go public in nearly 20 years — will open its IPO on November 22, running until November 24. The price band is set between ₹475 and ₹500 per share, with an anchor book opening on November 21. Importantly, this offering contains no new shares; it is entirely an offer-for-sale by existing stakeholders. Tata Motors, the parent company, plans to sell 4.62 crore shares valued at ₹2,313.75 crore. Additionally, Alpha TC Holdings Pte Ltd will offload 97.17 lakh shares (₹485.84 crore), and Tata Capital Growth Fund I will sell 48.58 lakh shares (₹242.92 crore). The last time a Tata entity went public was Tata Consultancy Services back in 2004.

article_content: Washington (CNN) — Five weeks before the November midterm elections, voters give Democrats a slight edge over Republicans, according to a CNN/ORC poll released Tuesday. However, most of the Democrats’ gains are concentrated in the Northeast and not in the key battleground states where tight races could determine Senate control. In a generic ballot among likely voters, Democrats led Republicans 47% to 45% — a six-point swing from a CNN poll three weeks ago, when Republicans held a four-point advantage. The Democratic lead falls within the poll’s 3.5% margin of error. The generic ballot — which asks respondents to choose between an unnamed Democrat and an unnamed Republican for the U.S. House — suggests a national shift toward Democrats, though not necessarily in pivotal state races. The poll follows a week after the U.S. launched airstrikes against ISIS in Syria. While respondents overwhelmingly identified the economy as the most important issue, they gave Congress low marks for its handling of the ISIS threat and expressed greater confidence in President Barack Obama than in GOP leaders to manage military policy against the militant group. 'That may explain why Democrats have gained strength on the national generic ballot,' said CNN Polling Director Keating Holland. Democrats gained the most ground among men and independent voters — two crucial demographics in competitive races this November. Men showed a seven-point swing toward Democrats, narrowing the gap to just six percentage points behind Republicans’ 49% support. 'This may indicate that some men supported aggressive action against ISIS and are rewarding the president’s party — or that they believe Obama’s actions mean they no longer need to elect more Republicans to achieve the results they want,' Holland said. Republicans also lost ground among independents, as Democrats gained a seven-point boost, resulting in a 44% to 42% advantage. Although Democratic momentum coincides with Obama’s expanded military campaign, roughly two-thirds of Americans said the economy is more important than military action against ISIS in determining their midterm vote. This contrasts with the lead-up to the Iraq War, when 49% of Americans in September 2002 considered the prospect of war with Iraq more important than the economy. Today, 59% of Americans say the conflict with ISIS is not a war, according to a separate CNN/ORC poll released Monday. Americans remain dissatisfied with Congress’s handling of ISIS: 60% disapprove — just weeks after many members left Capitol Hill without voting on military action to focus on their reelection campaigns. Yet this disapproval may reflect an improvement: just three weeks ago, 83% of Americans disapproved of Congress’s overall job performance.

Die meeste van die Demokrate se wins is egter gekonsentreer in die Noordooste en nie in die sleutelgebiede waar stywe wedstryde die kontrole van die Senaat kan beslis nie. In 'n generiese balot tussen waarskynlike kiezers het Demokrate Republikeine met 47% teen 45% gelei — 'n ses-punt swinging van 'n CNN-opname drie weke gelede, toe Republikeine 'n vier-punt voordeel gehad het. Die Demokratiese voorsprong val binne die opname se 3,5%-marginaal van fout. Die generiese balot — wat respondente vra om te kies tussen 'n ongenoemde Demokraat en 'n ongenoemde Republikein vir die Amerikaanse Huis — dui op 'n nasionale verskuiving na die Demokrate, alhoewel nie noodwendig in sleutelstaatrede nie. Die opname volg 'n week ná die VSA se aanvalle teen ISIS in Sirië. Terwyl respondente oorwegend die ekonomie as die belangrikste kwessie identifiseer, het hulle Congress lae punte gegee vir sy hantering van die ISIS-dreiging en het hulle meer vertroue in President Barack Obama as in Republikeinse leiers om militêre beleid teen die militant Islamitiese groep te stel. 'Dit kan verduidelik waarom Demokrate sterkte gewen het op die nasionale generiese balot,' sê CNN-opnamedirekteur Keating Holland. Demokrate het die meeste grond gewen onder mans en onafhanklikes — twee kritieke demografieë in konkurrensievolle rasse hierdie November. Mans het 'n sewe-punt swinging na die Demokrate getoon, wat die gapings tot net ses persentpunte agter Republikeine se 49% steun verklein het. 'Dit kan aandui dat sommige mans ondersteuning vir aggressiewe aksie teen ISIS gegee het en die president se party beloon — of dat hulle glo dat Obama se aksies beteken dat hulle nie meer meer Republikeine na Washington moet stuur om die resultate te kry wat hulle wil nie,' sê Holland. Republikeine het ook grond verloor onder onafhanklikes, terwyl Demokrate 'n sewe-punt styging gehad het, wat 'n 44% tot 42% voorsprong gelyk het. Hoewel die Demokratiese momentum saamval met Obama se uitgebreide militêre kampanje, het ongeveer twee derdes van Amerikaners gesê die ekonomie is belangriker as militêre aksie teen ISIS by die bepalings van hul middelkiesstem. Dit tree in teenstelling met die tyd voor die Irakoorlog, toe 49% van Amerikaners in September 2002 die moontlikheid van oorlog met Irak belangriker as die ekonomie gevind het. Vandag sê 59% van Amerikaners dat die konflikt met ISIS nie 'n oorlog is nie, volgens 'n aparte CNN/ORC-opname wat maandag vrygestel is. Amerikaners bly ontevreden met Congress se hantering van ISIS: 60% disapprove — net weke ná baie lede van Capitol Hill vertrek het sonder om oor militêre aksie te stem om hul herverkiesing te fokus. Nogtans mag hierdie ontevredenheid 'n verbetering aandui: net drie weke gelede het 83% van Amerikaners ontevreden gewees oor Congress se algemene werkprestasie.

article_content: A 20-year-old man known as 'John' suffered serious head injuries and a suspected fractured jaw after being struck by a single punch — commonly referred to as a 'king-hit' — at Sydney Intergate, an internet cafe located in the basement of a McDonald’s on George Street in Sydney’s CBD, on Thursday night. After the attack, John returned to his seat but soon lost consciousness and collapsed. Staff at the cafe, who wished to remain anonymous, confirmed he was a regular customer well-known to them. Emergency services were called shortly before 9:30pm following reports of an assault. NSW Police stated that the victim did not know his attacker, who fled the scene immediately after the incident. A friend present during the attack provided first aid until paramedics and police arrived. John was treated on-site for suspected head injuries before being transported to St Vincent’s Hospital. Police have not yet made any arrests. The suspect is described as a man aged between 18 and 25, approximately 180cm tall, with a slim build, wearing a grey t-shirt, blue jeans, black shoes, and carrying a bag. Authorities noted he has an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander appearance. A police spokesperson clarified that a man seen being handcuffed in video footage was a witness — not the suspect — and was restrained only to help calm him after witnessing the violent incident. St Vincent’s Hospital confirmed John was in stable condition but left the emergency department voluntarily on Friday morning. Officials said the injury was not life-threatening. Police emphasized that alcohol does not appear to have been a factor in the attack, and the motive remains under investigation.

article_content: In an eight-and-a-half-minute video message posted on YouTube, Michele Bachmann, founder of the House Tea Party Caucus and a prominent conservative figure, announced on Wednesday morning that she will not seek re-election to the U.S. House of Representatives after the 2014 elections. A four-term congresswoman, Bachmann has represented Minnesota’s 6th Congressional District since 2007. 'The law limits anyone from serving as president of the United States for more than eight years,' Bachmann said in the video. 'In my opinion, eight years is also long enough for an individual to serve as a representative for a specific congressional district.' Bachmann has been a staunch advocate for pro-life policies, opposition to same-sex marriage, and repeal of the Affordable Care Act. Her lengthy video included repeated assurances that ongoing investigations into campaign finance violations and her narrow 2012 re-election victory did not influence her decision. Bachmann has faced allegations that she improperly used funds from a congressional political action committee to support her 2012 presidential campaign. Former campaign aides made these accusations, and both the Office of Congressional Ethics and the Federal Election Commission are investigating. The FBI has also looked into claims that her presidential campaign made secret payments to Iowa Republican state Senator Kent Sorenson ahead of the 2012 Iowa Caucuses. Andy Parrish, her former chief of staff, stated under oath that Bachmann 'knew and approved' of these payments. Bachmann denied wrongdoing in her video: 'It was clearly understood that compliance with all rules and regulations was an absolute necessity for my presidential campaign, and I have no reason to believe that was not the case.' Her 2012 presidential bid collapsed after reports emerged that chronic migraines impaired her ability to campaign effectively. She withdrew in February 2012 and returned to run for Congress with only nine months to campaign. She narrowly defeated Democrat Jim Graves in 2012 by just 4,200 votes—1.1 percent. Graves has since announced he will run again in 2014. Bachmann dismissed speculation that she might lose if she ran again: 'My decision was not in any way influenced by any concerns about my being re-elected to Congress. If I ran, I would again defeat the individual I defeated last year.' However, a Republican strategist told MailOnline that the Republican Congressional Campaign Committee would likely not invest significant resources in her 2014 campaign, suggesting her preemptive withdrawal may have been motivated by low odds of victory. 'Bachmann has less than a 50-50 chance of winning again, and she knows it,' the strategist said. 'She’s probably stepping aside gracefully so the RNC has time to find a stronger candidate. That way, if she ever runs again—for example, for governor of Minnesota—she won’t have burned too many bridges.' Bachmann left the door open to future political involvement: 'There is no future option or opportunity—be it directly in the political arena or otherwise—that I won’t give serious consideration to if it can help save and protect our great nation for future generations.'

article_content: Sri Lanka’s High Commissioner to Britain, Chris Nonis, has dismissed international criticism of the country’s human rights record as part of a 'proxy propaganda war' waged by those who once funded the Tamil separatist conflict. His remarks came ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Colombo, where leaders from Canada, Mauritius, and India chose not to attend, citing persistent concerns over post-civil war abuses. Speaking to CNN’s Fred Pleitgen on 'Amanpour,' Nonis expressed no surprise at the backlash, arguing that global perceptions are distorted by diaspora groups with vested interests in perpetuating negative narratives. He emphasized Sri Lanka’s extensive reconciliation, rehabilitation, and reconstruction efforts since the war ended in 2009, calling the hosting of CHOGM a rightful affirmation of national progress. Nonis rejected calls for an independent international investigation into alleged war crimes, asserting that Sri Lanka’s 2,500-year-old civilization and educated institutions are fully capable of conducting a credible domestic inquiry. He criticized UK opposition leader Ed Miliband’s proposal to strip Sri Lanka of its Commonwealth chairmanship as 'extremely silly' and uninformed. Meanwhile, leaders from Canada, Mauritius, and India voiced deep concern over unresolved human rights issues — including civilian deaths, judicial interference, media intimidation, enforced disappearances, and the continued militarization of the northern provinces. Canada’s Prime Minister Stephen Harper called the lack of accountability 'unacceptable,' while British Prime Minister David Cameron urged Sri Lanka to demonstrate 'genuine freedom of expression, an end to torture, and real reconciliation.' India, home to a large Tamil population, faced internal pressure to boycott the summit but opted for diplomatic engagement instead. External Affairs Minister Salman Khurshid reiterated India’s call for meaningful devolution of power and accountability, while affirming that dialogue remains preferable to isolation. A 2011 United Nations report found that Sri Lankan forces used 'large-scale and widespread shelling' during the war’s final months, resulting in massive civilian casualties. Exact death tolls remain disputed, with official Sri Lankan figures significantly lower than those of international observers. President Mahinda Rajapaksa maintains that Sri Lanka has a robust legal system and human rights commission, and welcomes Commonwealth support to strengthen them.

Sy opmerkings kom voor die Gemenebesthoofde van Regeringsbyeenkoms (CHOGM) in Colombo, waar leiers van Kanada, Mauritius en Indië besluit het om nie aan te tref nie, weens aanhoudende besorgdheid oor misbruik na die burgeroorlog. Tydens 'n onderhoud met CNN se Fred Pleitgen op 'Amanpour' het Nonis geen verrassing uitgedruk oor die terugslag nie, en beweer dat wêreldpersepsies verdraai word deur diasporagroepe met belange in die voortdurende verspreiding van negatiewe narratiewe. Hy het beklemtoon dat Sri Lanka uitgebreide versoening, herstel en heropbou-inspannings gedoen het sedert die oorlog in 2009 geëindig het, en het die gasheerskap van CHOGM as 'n regverdige bevestiging van nasionale vooruitgang beskryf. Nonis het kalle vir 'n onafhanklike internasionale ondersoek na vermeende oorlogsmisdade afgewys, en beweer dat Sri Lanka se 2500-jaar-oue beskawing en opgeleide instellings volkome in staat is om 'n geloofwaardige binnelandse ondersoek uit te voer. Hy het die voorstel van die Britse opposisieleier Ed Miliband om Sri Lanka van sy Gemenebest-voorsitterskap te ontneem as 'baie dom' en ongeïnformeerd gekritiseer. Tuisdans het leiers van Kanada, Mauritius en Indië hul diep besorgdheid oor onopgeloste menseregte-kwesties uitgedruk — insluitend burgerdodings, justitiele intervensie, media-intimidering, gedwonge verdwysings en die voortdurende militariserings van die noorde. Kanada se Eerste Minister Stephen Harper het die gebrek aan aanspreeklikheid 'onhaalbaar' genoem, terwyl Britse Eerste Minister David Cameron Sri Lanka opgeroep het om 'n ware vryheid van uitdrukking, einde aan foltering en werklike versoening te demonstreer. Buitelandse Sake Minister Salman Khurshid het Indië se oproep vir betekenisvolle deelging van mag en aanspreeklikheid herhaal, terwyl hy bevestig het dat dialoog voorkeur het bo isolasie. 'n 2011-verslag van die Verenigde Nasies het gevind dat Sri Lankaanse magte 'groot-skaal en wydverspreide kanonnering' gebruik het tydens die laaste maande van die oorlog, wat tot massale burgerdodings gelei het. Die presiese sterftesyfers bly omstridden, met amptelike Sri Lankaanse getalle wat beduidend laer is as dié van internasionale waarnemers. President Mahinda Rajapaksa handhaaf dat Sri Lanka 'n sterk regsstelsel en Menseregtekommissie het, en verwelkom die Gemenebest se ondersteuning om hulle te versterk.

article_content: Walking through the Farnborough airfield during the international airshow, you’re surrounded by towering symbols of aerospace power—Dreamliners, fighter jets, and luxury private aircraft—all priced beyond reach for ordinary buyers. While cars and computers became household items, private planes have done the opposite: growing more exclusive, not less. After the 2008 financial crisis, U.S. private jet sales plummeted by 3.4% in 2012, and barely crept up by 0.9% the next year—with nearly all growth happening among ultra-expensive models. Even Bombardier’s president admitted the entry-level jet market has struggled for years. For those dreaming of flight, options remain limited: building a kit plane or restoring an old model. But a new contender is stepping onto the scene—the SkyRunner, unveiled by UK-based Parajet at Farnborough. Priced at $80,000, it blends an all-terrain vehicle with a lightweight aircraft that can fly up to 15,000 feet at 55 mph for three hours, powered by a low-emission petrol engine. Its creator, Gilo Cardozo, even flew one from London to Timbuktu after five years of testing, drawing on tech developed for Parajet’s existing jetpack line. Tom Prideaux-Brune of Parajet says the design is proven and now waiting only for distribution partners to begin production. Still, it must clear aviation regulations: authorities need to know who’s flying, and that pilots are properly trained. The UK’s Civil Aviation Authority has shown encouraging support, but legal hurdles remain. Other companies like Terrafugia are entering the space too, reviving the idea of the ‘carplane’ once confined to sci-fi movies. Charles Alcock of Aviation International News notes that past affordability leaps happened before the recession—like very light jets dropping from $75 million to $1 million. Yet he warns that even if you buy one, training, licensing, and hangar fees often cost far more than the vehicle itself. And convincing regulators to approve these hybrids? That’s still a tall order. Still, the SkyRunner offers something rare: a tangible vision of flight becoming something anyone might one day enjoy—not just the wealthy.

Terwyl motors en rekenaars huishoudelike goed geword het, het privaatvliegtuie die teenoorgestelde gedoen: meer eksklusief geword, nie minder nie. Na die finansiële krise van 2008 is die Verenigde State se privaatvliegtuieverkope met 3,4% in 2012 gesak, en het hulle net met 0,9% in die volgende jaar gestyg—met amper al die groei wat by ultradyre modelle plaasgevind het. Selfs Bombardier se voorsitter het erken dat die inkomstevlak-vliegtuigmark die laaste paar jaar geskop het. Vir mense wat droom van vlieg, bly die opsies beperk: ’n kitsvliegtuig bou of ’n ou model herstel. Sy skepper, Gilo Cardozo, het self een van Londen na Timbuktu gevlieg ná vyf jaar toetsing, en gebruik gemaak van tegnologie wat ontwikkel is vir Parajet se bestaande jetpacklyn. Die Britse Burgerlike Lugvaartowerheid het aanduidings van ondersteuning gegee, maar wettige hawens bly. Ander maatskappye soos Terrafugia kom ook in die ruimte, en herleef die idee van die 'karvliegtuig' wat eers in wetenskapfiksie voorgekom het. Daar is nog baie werk om te doen. Maar die SkyRunner bied iets seldsaam: ’n greep op ’n toekoms waarin vlieg nie net vir die ryk is nie.

article_content: In June 2012, then-Prime Minister David Cameron unintentionally left his eight-year-old daughter, Nancy, behind at The Plough Inn pub in Buckinghamshire after a family outing. The Camerons, along with two other families, had spent the afternoon enjoying drinks and meals near Chequers, the official country residence. When it was time to depart, Nancy went to the restroom without informing anyone. As the group split into two vehicles—Cameron riding with security personnel and his wife driving the other children—each parent assumed the girl was with the other. It wasn’t until they reached Chequers that Cameron realized Nancy was missing. He immediately returned to the pub, where staff reported she had been calmly helping out for about 15 minutes. No harm came to the child. Downing Street later confirmed that the couple accepted full responsibility, clarifying that security teams were not at fault. The incident, described as a simple oversight, sparked public discussion about parenting under pressure and the private lives of public figures. While some media outlets highlighted Cameron’s known hobbies—including wine tasting, snooker, and video games—to paint a picture of relaxed leadership, the pub’s longtime owner, Steve Hollings, strongly defended him as a loving, grounded father who treats his family time as sacred. Hollings emphasized that Cameron is simply 'David' when he visits, not the Prime Minister.

Die voorval, beskryf as ’n eenvoudige fout, het openbare debat uitgelok oor ouerskap onder druk en die privaatlewens van openbare figure. article_content: During a press event unveiling a new immigration policy, President Obama was interrupted twice by Neil Munro, a reporter for the right-wing outlet The Daily Caller. The first interruption came when Munro shouted, 'Why do you favor foreigners over Americans?' Obama calmly replied, 'Excuse me, sir, but it's not time for questions.' When Munro pressed, 'Are you going to take questions?' Obama responded, 'Not while I'm speaking.' Moments later, Munro interrupted again — this time mid-sentence — and Obama chose to finish his remarks without further engagement. While some may view this as a single act of rudeness, the author — a comedian and commentator — argues it reflects a deliberate pattern. Drawing from his experience with hecklers, he notes that one interruption might be accidental; two suggest intent. Munro’s public social media activity reinforces this view: his tweets contain repeated attacks on Obama, including accusations of racial discrimination in hiring and attempts to co-opt Black culture for political appeal. But the author insists this isn’t really about Munro. He’s a minor figure in a larger, well-documented campaign to undermine Obama’s legitimacy since before he took office. From Rush Limbaugh declaring he hoped Obama would fail, to the debunked 'birther' conspiracy claiming Obama wasn’t born in the U.S., to claims he is secretly a Muslim, these attacks aim to paint Obama as fundamentally 'other' — not truly American. Historical context underscores the abnormality: no modern president faced such sustained, public disrespect. In 2009, Rep. Joe Wilson shouted 'You lie!' during Obama’s address to Congress — an unprecedented breach of decorum. Rep. Joe Walsh later demanded Obama 'quit lying' over the debt ceiling. Donald Trump repeatedly revived the birther myth and questioned Obama’s intellectual qualifications. All were Republican figures. Tucker Carlson defended Munro by comparing him to Sam Donaldson, who reportedly interrupted President Reagan. But Chris Wallace, a former White House correspondent who worked alongside Donaldson, stated that no such heckling occurred during Reagan’s presidency. The author labels this defense as misleading, illustrating how truth is often discarded when it contradicts political agendas. The author concludes that these incidents are not about policy differences — they’re about eroding the perceived legitimacy of America’s first Black president. As election season approaches, such provocations are likely to increase. They shouldn’t shock us. They’re part of a playbook.

Die eerste onderbreking het gekom toe Munro geskree het: 'Waarom gun jy buitelanders bo Amerikaners?' Obama het rustig geantwoord: 'Verontskuld my, meneer, maar dit is nie tyd vir vrae nie.' Toe Munro gevra het: 'Gaan jy vrae beantwoord?' het Obama geantwoord: 'Nieteen tydens ek praat.' 'n Oomblik later het Munro weer onderbreek — hierdie keer mid-deur sy uitspraak — en Obama het gekies om sy uitspraak te voltooi sonder verdere reaksie. Die historiese konteks benadruk die abnormaalheid: geen moderne president het so aanhoudende, openlike onbeskaamdheid ondervind nie. In 2009 het Rep. Joe Wilson geskree: 'Jy lieg!' tydens Obama se toespraak aan die Kongres — 'n onvoorbeeldde skending van die gebruikte sedes. Rep. Joe Walsh het later geëis dat Obama 'hou op om te lieg' oor die skuldgrens. Donald Trump het die birther-myt herhaaldelik herleef en Obama se intellektuele kwalifikasies bevraagteken. Die skrywer sluit af dat hierdie voorvalle nie oor beleidverskille gaan nie — hulle gaan oor die ondermyn van die waargenome legitimiteit van Amerika se eerste swart president. Soos die verkiesing nader kom, is sulke provokasies waarskynlik om te toeneem. Hulle behoort ons nie te skok nie. Hulle is deel van 'n planboek.

article_content: Six days after hackers breached iCloud accounts of more than 100 celebrities and leaked private, nude photos online, Reddit finally shut down the forum 'The Fappening'—a page dedicated to sharing the stolen images. Among those affected were high-profile figures including Oscar winner Jennifer Lawrence, model Kate Upton, and reality star Kim Kardashian, with at least 400 images reportedly circulated. In a blog post, Reddit CEO Yishan Wong acknowledged the violation of privacy but defended the platform’s delayed response by invoking free speech. He described Reddit not as a traditional company, but as 'the government of a new type of community,' where users are expected to self-regulate rather than be governed by top-down censorship. Wong stated that while Reddit does not condone the theft or distribution of these images, its infrastructure is designed to support user-generated content—including links to media—and changing policies due to this incident would compromise core principles. He emphasized: 'When you know something is right, you should choose to do it. But as much as possible, we will not force you to do it.' However, the situation became more serious when it emerged that some leaked photos included 16-year-old Olympic gymnast McKayla Maroney—a minor under U.S. federal law. Distributing nude images of minors constitutes child pornography, regardless of context, making the platform’s inaction legally and ethically indefensible. The images also spread widely on 4chan, an anonymous image board founded in 2003 by Christopher Poole, which receives 12 million monthly visitors and requires no user registration. Reddit, owned by Advance Publications (which also publishes Condé Nast), has indicated it will not alter its content policies despite the controversy.

article_content: In the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, some Republican lawmakers have pointed to the 2012 Benghazi attack as the root cause — claiming that America’s failure to respond forcefully emboldened Putin. Senator Lindsey Graham tweeted that when Americans are killed and no consequences follow, ‘you invite this type of aggression.’ But critics, including Democratic strategist Paul Begala, dismissed the connection as politically motivated nonsense. ‘It’s not about Obama,’ Begala said. ‘It’s about Putin’s ambition.’ The debate has become a mirror of American political dysfunction, where every international crisis is weaponized for domestic gain. With midterm elections looming, figures like Graham and Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell have seized on the moment to paint President Obama as passive and weak — even as they insist they don’t advocate for military intervention. McConnell, for instance, criticized Obama’s leadership but quickly added, ‘We’re not saying force is the answer — just that the world doesn’t respect us anymore.’ On the other side, former Democratic National Committee chair Howard Dean defended Obama’s cautious strategy, calling it a smart, calculated squeeze on Putin — tightening pressure without forcing him into a corner. ‘Putin needs room to back down without losing face,’ Dean explained. ‘That’s exactly what the President is doing.’ Despite the heated rhetoric, both parties largely agree on the solution: isolate Russia through sanctions, suspend military cooperation, and threaten its exclusion from the G8. Targets include Russian banks and oligarchs with assets abroad. Even Paul Ryan, seen as a moderate voice, acknowledged that while U.S. policy may have created a perception of weakness, Putin alone bears responsibility for the invasion. Underlying the debate is a deeper fight over defense spending. Republicans, many of whom face tough primaries, are using Ukraine to argue against Obama’s proposed military cuts. Meanwhile, analysts like Darrell West of Brookings note that the timing is no coincidence — ‘It’s easier to blame the president when the world is chaotic.’ And while some have drawn parallels between Putin and Hitler — notably Hillary Clinton — she later softened her remarks. The real story isn’t about who said what first. It’s about how a global crisis became a political football in an election year — with lives and sovereignty hanging in the balance.

article_content: According to scientists featured in a new documentary, the mummified body of Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun may have caught fire inside his sarcophagus due to a chemical reaction triggered by embalming oils applied after his death in 1323 BC. Researchers analyzed a fragment of his flesh and confirmed that his body burned while still sealed in the coffin. Tutankhamun became pharaoh at age 10 in 1333 BC and ruled for only nine years before his untimely death. He was the last ruler of the Eighteenth Dynasty of the New Kingdom, one of ancient Egypt’s most powerful royal lines. The discovery of his nearly intact tomb in 1922 by Howard Carter and the Earl of Carnarvon ignited worldwide fascination with ancient Egypt. Among the treasures found was a 24.2-pound solid gold death mask encrusted with lapis lazuli and semi-precious stones. Egyptologist Dr. Chris Naunton reviewed Howard Carter’s original excavation notes and conducted virtual autopsies using X-ray and CT scan data. He now believes Tutankhamun died from injuries sustained in a high-speed chariot crash. Dr. Naunton noted that Tutankhamun’s skeleton showed broken ribs on the left side, a missing sternum, and no heart — injuries consistent with being struck by a chariot wheel. These were likely fatal and occurred before burial. Contrary to long-standing theories, the loose fragment of skull bone detected in 1968 is now thought to have resulted from mishandling during early excavations, not murder. The embalmers, unaccustomed to working with severely mangled remains, may have inadvertently caused a chemical reaction with the oils, leading to spontaneous combustion after burial — a phenomenon never before documented in ancient Egyptian mummies. The documentary 'Tutankhamun: The Mystery Of The Burnt Mummy' will air on Channel 4 on November 10, presenting these revised conclusions based on modern forensic science.

article_content: When a blog you helped build starts falling apart, what do you do? You write about it — loudly. That’s exactly what MG Siegler, TechCrunch’s top editor, did after learning that founder Michael Arrington might be forced out. In a raw, unfiltered post, Siegler described TechCrunch as teetering on the edge, caught in chaos with no clear direction. 'No one knows what’s happening,' he wrote. 'Not even us.' The root of the problem? Arrington launched CrunchBase, a $20 million venture capital fund, to invest in startups that TechCrunch covers. At first, AOL — which bought TechCrunch in 2010 — didn’t object. In fact, they put money into the fund too. But as criticism mounted from journalists and the public, AOL reversed course. Arrington was told he could still write for the site… but only as an unpaid blogger. Many see this as a glaring conflict: how can a blog that shapes the fate of startups also control the purse strings behind them? David Carr of The New York Times called it absurd — comparing AOL’s ethics to opening a lemonade stand just to boost profits. He pointed out that TechCrunch has the power to destroy or elevate companies, making Arrington’s financial ties deeply problematic. But not everyone agrees. Jeff Jarvis, a journalism professor, argues Arrington never pretended to be a neutral reporter. He built TechCrunch to connect startups, share insights, and promote his own investments — and that’s still what he’s doing. 'He’s not a journalist,' Jarvis says. 'He’s a connector — and he does it better than most major papers.' Siegler admits TechCrunch might survive without Arrington. The traffic is high, the revenue solid. But he insists the site won’t be the same. Arrington’s voice, energy, and vision are woven into every post, every headline, every comment — invisible, yet essential. 'You won’t realize you’re missing him until he’s gone.'

Aanvanklik het AOL — wat TechCrunch in 2010 gekoop het — nie teen geweier nie. Selfs het hulle geld in die fonds geïnvesteer. 'Jy sal nie besef dat jy hom mis nie totdat hy weg is.'

article_content: Fernando Santos, the new head coach of Portugal’s national team, has had his appeal against an eight-match FIFA suspension denied. The ban stems from an incident during the 2014 World Cup, when Santos — then managing Greece — verbally abused match officials after extra time ended in a 1-1 draw against Costa Rica. His team lost on penalties, and he was sent to the stands, a moment that marked a low point in an otherwise historic run for Greek football. Despite the ban, the Portuguese Football Federation appointed him last Tuesday, betting on his experience — particularly his achievement of leading Greece to their first-ever World Cup knockout stage. Santos will serve the suspension during Euro 2016 qualifying matches, barring him from the touchline. But he retains full control over squad selection and is allowed to participate in training sessions, leaving open questions about how much influence he’ll truly have during games. This appointment comes after Portugal’s shocking 1-0 home loss to Albania in Aveiro — a result that ended Paulo Bento’s tenure following a disappointing World Cup campaign. Santos now shoulders the pressure to revive Portugal’s chances in Europe, but if the ban covers all qualifiers, he could be sidelined for the entire campaign. His only remaining option is to appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport — though no outcome is guaranteed.

article_content: Nearly 600 patients die in hospitals each year due to hunger and dehydration, according to official figures. Bereaved families have described how their loved ones were 'forgotten to death' by staff who failed to assist them with eating or drinking. Data from the Office for National Statistics shows that 7,949 deaths over the past decade were attributed to hunger or thirst. In 2013, dehydration was recorded as an underlying cause or contributory factor in 574 deaths across NHS and private hospitals—down from 942 in 2008. A further 336 deaths in 2013 involved malnutrition as an underlying cause or contributing factor. These figures cannot be combined, as some patients were counted in both categories. Additionally, 88 deaths in care homes in 2013 were linked to dehydration, and 33 to malnutrition, according to figures obtained by Channel 4 News. The family of Stanley Mack, a 77-year-old retired engineer who died of acute dehydration in 2008 at Selly Oak Hospital in Birmingham, recounted how staff left drinks beside his bed without helping him consume them. Mack was admitted with a chest infection and later diagnosed with Clostridium difficile. His wife, Carol, said there was no reliable record of his fluid intake, and staff often falsely documented that he had been given fluids. She added: 'It wasn't run in a way that met the patient’s needs. His condition deteriorated, and he became acutely dehydrated.' After a five-year legal battle, a second inquest in 2013 concluded that Mack died from dehydration. His widow said: 'We felt we had to persist—to do justice to Stan’s memory and prevent others from suffering the same fate.' His son Ian stated: 'My dad was forgotten completely. The hospital failed at the most basic level. Something went terribly wrong at Selly Oak Hospital.' The Mail has long campaigned on hospital and care home neglect through its 'Dignity for the Elderly' initiative.

article_content: After nearly half a decade leading the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Janet Napolitano has announced she’s leaving her Cabinet role to take on a new challenge: becoming the 20th president of the University of California. While the move caught many off guard, those who’ve worked alongside her for decades weren’t surprised. Napolitano has spent her career breaking barriers—not just as the first woman valedictorian at Santa Clara, the first elected female governor of Arizona, or the first woman to helm DHS, but as someone who turns chaotic systems into well-oiled machines. As governor, she turned a $1 billion budget deficit into a surplus—without raising taxes. At DHS, she merged 22 fragmented federal agencies into a cohesive unit, shifting from rigid, one-size-fits-all security policies to smarter, intelligence-led strategies. Under her watch, FEMA went from punchline to powerhouse, responding effectively to disasters like Hurricane Sandy and the Midwest floods, thanks to strong partnerships with professionals like Director Craig Fugate. What sets Napolitano apart isn’t just her policy wins—it’s how she leads. She doesn’t seek the spotlight. Whether she was walking the Gulf Coast after the BP oil spill, meeting families in tornado-ravaged towns, or testifying before Congress on immigration, she made space for others to speak. Her approach to immigration wasn’t ideological; it was practical—prioritizing public safety while recognizing the deep contributions of immigrant families, including her own Italian roots. Behind closed doors, she’s equally remarkable. When a longtime Arizona staffer fell seriously ill, Napolitano visited her every day, offering comfort and companionship until her passing. She didn’t just acknowledge the woman’s professional role—she honored her as a writer, a hospice volunteer, and a woman of deep faith. That kind of humanity doesn’t come with a title. She’s also a football fan, an opera lover, and someone who shows up—for colleagues, for causes, for people. As she moves to lead the nation’s largest public university system, students and faculty will soon discover what her colleagues already know: Janet Napolitano isn’t just a leader. She’s the kind of person who makes institutions better—not because she demands it, but because she cares.

article_content: Thousands of Roman artefacts have been unearthed in an archaeological dig hailed as 'the most important excavation ever held in London'. Archaeologists have discovered coins, pottery, shoes, lucky charms, and an amber gladiator amulet dating back nearly 2,000 years. Experts leading the excavation have also uncovered wooden structures from the 40s AD, approximately 40 feet beneath the ground. The site lies just yards from the River Thames and adjacent to the Bloomberg Place office development on Queen Victoria Street, in the heart of London’s financial district. Once home to the Roman Temple of Mithras and situated along the now-buried Walbrook stream, the location will become the new headquarters of Bloomberg. Among the finds are a ceramic beaker from the 1st century AD, a stag-shaped oil lamp, Roman pins, and a lead or tin plaque depicting a bull — possibly representing the zodiac sign Taurus. The artefacts have been exceptionally preserved due to the muddy, waterlogged conditions of the ancient Walbrook River, prompting archaeologists to nickname the site 'the Pompeii of the North'. Sadie Watson, site director at the Museum of London Archaeology, said: 'The archaeology on this project so far is probably the most important excavation ever held within London — certainly within Roman London. The depth, preservation, and extent of the findings mean the entire Roman period is represented by remarkable buildings and artefacts.' The three-acre site, once on the banks of the Walbrook, also contains the remains of the Temple of Mithras, originally discovered in the 1950s. Since the Bloomberg Place construction began, around 10,000 artefacts have been recovered by 60 archaeologists — the largest number of small finds ever uncovered in a single excavation in the capital. Approximately 3,500 tonnes of soil — equivalent to 21,000 wheelbarrow loads — have been carefully excavated by hand. This site has yielded the largest collection of Roman leather ever found in London, including hundreds of shoes. Over 100 fragments of Roman writing tablets have been uncovered, and 700 boxes of pottery shards are set to be analyzed by specialists. Sophie Jackson of the museum added: 'The site is a wonderful snapshot of London’s first four centuries. The waterlogged conditions left by the Walbrook stream have preserved layer upon layer of Roman timber buildings, fences, and yards — along with astonishing personal items, clothing, and even documents — all of which will transform our understanding of life in Roman London.'

Die site lê net ‘n paar meter van die Rivier Thames af en langs die Bloomberg Place-kantoorontwikkeling op Queen Victoria Street, in die hart van Londen se finansiële distrik. Eers die tuiste van die Romeinse Tempel van Mithras en geleë langs die nou-verlore Walbrook-stroom, sal die plek die nuwe hoofkwartier van Bloomberg wees. article_content: Khartoum, Sudan — For a fourth consecutive day, civic unrest swept across Sudan Wednesday as citizens protested a dramatic spike in fuel prices. Gunfire echoed through the capital and other regions as security forces attempted to quell the demonstrations. The initial protest, held Sunday in Wad Madani — a city about 190 kilometers southeast of Khartoum — was led primarily by high school and university students, one day before the price increase officially took effect. During that rally, a student was killed by gunfire; while authorities have not determined the source of the fatal shot, activists on social media have accused police of responsibility. Over the following days, hundreds joined similar protests nationwide. Witnesses reported outbreaks of violence and property damage, including attacks on gas stations, vandalism of buses, and looting of shops. Offices of the ruling party in various parts of Khartoum were also targeted. Police responded with tear gas, according to eyewitnesses. By Wednesday night, tensions showed no sign of easing. Internet services in Khartoum were reportedly cut, and gunfire continued to reverberate across the city — though it remained unclear whether the shots came from security personnel or armed demonstrators. The unrest stems from a government policy, debated for over a month, aimed at stabilizing the national economy. As part of this plan, Sudan removed its longstanding fuel subsidy, causing gasoline prices to nearly double overnight. The cost increase has already affected public transportation fares and is expected to drive up food prices significantly in the coming weeks. Separately, an aid worker was killed in an attack in South Sudan. CNN journalist Isma'il Kushkush reported from Sudan, with additional contributions from Greg Botelho.

Skietery het deur die hoofstad en ander stede geëko terwyl veiligheidspersoneel probeer het om die demonstrasies te onderdruk. Die eerste protes, wat Sondag in Wad Madani — ‘n stad ongeveer 190 km suidoos van Khartoum — gehou is, is hoofsaaklik gelei deur hoërskool- en universiteitstudente, een dag voor die prysverhoging van kracht geword het. Tydens daardie protes is ‘n student doodgeskiet; hoewel owerhede nie die bron van die dodelike skoot bepaal het nie, het aktiwiste op sosiale media polisie verantwoordelik gehou. Gedurende die dae wat volg het, het honderde aan soortgelyke protesse in die hele land deelgeneem. Ooggetuies het geweld en eiendomsskade gerapporteer, insluitende aanvalle op petrolstasies, beskadiging van busse en plondering van winkels. Kantore van die regerende party in verskillende dele van Khartoum is ook aangeval. Polisie het traangas gebruik, volgens ooggetuies. Teen woensdag nag het die spanning geen teken van afname getoon nie. Die onrus stam uit ‘n regeringbeleid wat meer as ‘n maand lank bespreek is, met die doel om die nasionale ekonomie te stabiliseer. article_content: The W.i.P. nightclub in Manhattan has had its liquor license suspended following a series of violent incidents, most notably a chaotic brawl in the early hours of June 15 that left multiple people injured — including singer Chris Brown and NBA star Tony Parker. The New York State Liquor Authority acted decisively, citing 17 violations ranging from unauthorized use of the club’s name and drug activity on-site to dangerously insufficient security. SLA Chairman Dennis Rosen emphasized that venues posing threats to public safety will face immediate consequences. Officials confirmed the June 15 altercation — which involved members of Brown’s and Drake’s entourages — was the tipping point in their decision. Brown’s team described him as a victim of a 'brutal attack' that also harmed his girlfriend, Karrueche Tran, and his bodyguard. Drake’s representatives, however, have consistently maintained he was not involved in any misconduct that night. Separately, Tony Parker, who was seated away from the conflict, filed a $20 million lawsuit alleging a serious corneal laceration that has impaired his ability to play basketball. The suit claims the club negligently allowed rival groups to mingle without adequate protection. Brown has cooperated with NYPD investigators, and the club’s owner may petition for a hearing to appeal the suspension. CNN’s Carolyn Sung contributed to this report.

Die New York State Liquor Authority het beslis opgetree met 17 oortredings wat ‘n wye spektrum het: ongeoorloofde gebruik van die klub se naam, drugaktiwiteit op die terrein en gevaarlik ontoereikende sekuriteit. article_content: Woody Harrelson has defended his confrontation with a TMZ photographer at New York’s LaGuardia Airport, claiming he mistook the man for a zombie — a role he’d been portraying in the recently completed film 'Zombieland'. According to an airport spokesperson, the photographer filed a police complaint alleging that Harrelson damaged his camera and shoved him in the face. The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey confirmed it is reviewing the incident and may refer it to authorities if warranted. The photographer, whose identity has not been disclosed, recorded the encounter using a smaller backup camera after his primary equipment was reportedly damaged. In a statement released by his publicist, Harrelson said he had just finished filming 'Zombieland' in Atlanta and remained emotionally immersed in his character — playing 'the most frightened person on Earth' — when he was startled by the paparazzo at the airport. He added that his reaction was a mistaken, instinctive response to what he perceived as a zombie. TMZ published two videos of the event. One shows the photographer following Harrelson and his daughter down an escalator and out of the terminal, ending with Harrelson appearing to reach for the lens. The second video captures the aftermath: the photographer accusing Harrelson of breaking his camera, followed by a brief scuffle. The photographer repeatedly shouts, 'This is assault!' and 'Chill out!' as he continues to follow Harrelson for several minutes toward the parking lot. Harrelson is no stranger to such allegations. In 2006, a different TMZ photographer sued him for an alleged assault outside a Hollywood nightclub. Although prosecutors declined to press criminal charges, the photographer, Josh Levine, filed a civil suit seeking $2.5 million in damages. Levine’s attorney, Cyrus Nownejad, stated Friday that Harrelson has a documented history of aggression and that they intend to hold him accountable. Notably, TMZ is partially owned by AOL, which is part of Warner Bros. Discovery — the current parent company of CNN. CNN’s Marc Balinsky contributed to this report.

article_content: (CNN) -- Pressure is mounting for world leaders to respond to Syria’s brutal crackdown on anti-regime protests. Earlier this week, United Nations Human Rights Commissioner Navi Pillay stated that more than 5,000 people had been killed in Syria since the uprising began in March. The Syrian government issued an ultimatum to activists in the restive city of Homs: cease protests or face bombardment, raising fears of escalating violence. Human rights groups have urged an international response, but some diplomats warn that intervention could worsen the situation. Mousab Azzawi of the London-based Syrian Observatory for Human Rights compared Syria’s crisis to pre-intervention Libya, arguing that the same atrocities and crimes against humanity justify a similar response. 'When the international community went to Libya to protect civilians, were they deceiving everyone?' he asked CNN’s Connect the World. 'If protecting civilians is the guiding principle, then what is happening in Syria is no different — the same tyranny, the same crimes.' However, Oliver Miles, former British ambassador to Libya, rejected any equivalence. 'Syria is different in many ways,' he said. 'Iraq was invaded by a foreign power and is still in ruins eight years later. Libya was not invaded; it saw a popular uprising that succeeded in toppling a tyrant and is moving toward rebuilding. Syria is larger, more complex, and offers no viable path for foreign intervention.' Miles added that without a United Nations mandate, meaningful action is unlikely. 'I wish there were a way to intervene effectively, but I fear it would make things worse. In Libya, we had a clear UN mandate — legality was established. There is no such possibility in Syria today.' Azzawi countered that inaction amounts to complicity. 'By failing to act, foreign powers are participating in the bloodshed,' he said. He also warned that without international support, peaceful protesters may turn to the Free Syrian Army, risking the militarization of the uprising. 'The people in Syria are clinging to nonviolence — but if they feel abandoned, they’ll pick up arms. That could spark a civil war — one that would spread rapidly across borders.' CNN’s Max Foster contributed to this report.
translated_content: (CNN) -- Druk is toeneem dat wêreldleiers reageer op Surië se brutaal onderdrukking van anti-regeringsprotes. Vroeër hierdie week het die Verenigde Nasies se Kommissaris vir Menseregte, Navi Pillay, gesê dat meer as 5 000 mense in Surië vermoor is sedert die opstand in Maart begin het. Die Suriese regering het aktiwiste in die onrustige stad Homs ‘n ultimatum gegee: hou op met julle protes of kry bombardemente, wat vrees vir toename in geweld veroorsaak het. Menseregte-aktiwiste het ‘n internasionale reaksie op die geweld geëis — maar sommige diplomate het gewaarsku dat intervensie die situasie slegter kan maak. Mousab Azzawi van die Londen-basiseerde Suriese Observatorium vir Menseregte het die situasie in Surië vergelyk met Libië voor die NAVO-intervensie en gesê dat dit ‘n soortgelyke respons verdien. 'Toe die internasionale gemeenskap na Libië gegaan het om burgerlikes te beskerm, het hulle mense bedrieg?' het hy aan CNN se Connect the World gevra. 'As die beginsel van die beskerming van burgerlikes die motivering van die internasionale gemeenskap is, dan is wat in Surië gebeur nie anders as wat in Libië gebeur het — dit is dieselfde wredekheid, dieselfde tirannie en dieselfde misdade teen die mensdom.' Maar Oliver Miles, voormalige Britse ambassadeur na Libië, het gesê dat daar geen vergelyking is tussen die twee lande nie — of tussen Surië en Irak, ‘n ander hoogs opgemerkte voorbeeld van internasionale intervensie. 'Surië verskil op baie, baie maniere. Irak is deur ‘n buitelandse regering binnegedring, en sewe, agt jaar later, is dit in puin. Libië is nie deur ‘n buitelandse regering binnegedring nie; in Libië was daar ‘n opstand wat suksesvol was om ‘n tirannie te stort en op die weg is om iets te bou wat daardie tirannie vervang. Surië het geen ooreenkomste met een van hulle nie. Surië is ‘n groter land as Libië, dit is ‘n meer ingewikkelde land, en dit bied geen ruimte vir buitelandse intervensie nie.' Miles het gesê dat politici en diplomate onwaarskynlik groot aksie teen die Suriese regering sal neem sonder steun van die VN — en dat sulke steun onwaarskynlik is. 'Ek dink die situasie in Surië is absoluut verschriklik, en as ek ‘n manier kon dink waarop die Britse regering, of enige ander regering, of die Verenigde Nasies effektief kon interveer, sou ek daarvoor wees, maar ek dink intervensie sou waarskynlik die dinge slegter maak,' het hy aan CNN gesê. 'Toe buitelandse lugmagte begin het om deel te neem aan die Libiese stryd in Maart, het hulle ‘n duidelike mandaat van die Verenigde Nasies gehad, wat beteken het dat onder internasionale wet, wat ons gedoen het, as wettig beskou kon word. Daar is geen moontlikheid dat ons ‘n mandaat van die Verenigde Nasies sal kry om in Surië te interveer soos dit tans staan.' Maar Azzawi het gesê dat sulke pragmatiese houdings die situasie slegter maak en buitelandse magte wat nie optree nie, beskuldig van 'deelname aan die bloedvergieting in Surië' per omweg. En hy het gesê hy vrees die invloed van Suriese militêre afvalliges, die Vrye Suriese Leger, op die protes — tensy die vegters internasionale ondersteuning gekry het. 'Die getalle van die Vrye Suriese Leger — sonder ondersteuning van die internasionale gemeenskap — is nou so klein, en die groot risiko is dat hierdie vredeliewende demonstrante deur die FSA geneig word om wapens te hou en dan beweeg ons na ‘n stadium van militariserings van die opstand, wat ‘n groot risiko is. Die mense in Surië probeer hartseer om vas te hou aan die beginsel van vrede,' het hy gesê. 'Ek dink dit sal nie vir altyd duur nie, maar as ons militariserings van die opstand het, sal ons ‘n burgeroorlog hê en ek dink dit is die laaste ding wat die internasionale gemeenskap in Surië wil sien, want enige burgeroorlog in Surië sou baie vinnig na die buurlande versprei.' CNN se Max Foster het bygedra tot hierdie verslag.

article_content: A new reality series on Bravo, titled 'Start-Ups: Silicon Valley,' premieres on November 5 and follows six young entrepreneurs as they attempt to launch companies and strike it rich. But the preview video reveals almost nothing about their products — instead, it highlights poolside lounging, rock climbing, toga parties, and heavy drinking, all framed under the slogan 'work hard, play hard.' The 2-minute, 21-second trailer is saturated with overused tech clichés and exaggerated metaphors: 'The future of the world is in our hands,' 'Silicon Valley is balls to the wall,' and 'We have to up our game more than ever.' One participant quips, 'People have been intimidated because this package generally doesn't come with a brain.' Critics have reacted sharply. Gizmodo observes that the cast appears less like founders and more like failed actors stringing together buzzwords. TechCrunch’s Alexa Tsotsis joked, 'Here Comes Silicon Valley Boo Boo.' On Bravo’s own website, the video holds a mere 2/5-star rating. Viewers also highlight troubling omissions: the near-total absence of Asian and Indian professionals, who constitute a large share of Silicon Valley’s workforce. One viewer remarked, 'Asian people apparently don’t exist in the Hollywood version of Silicon Valley.' Despite being co-produced by Randi Zuckerberg — former Facebook marketing director and sister of Mark Zuckerberg — the show fails to gain credibility. CNNMoney satirically suggests turning it into a drinking game: take a shot every time someone mentions 'business development' by the pool, and down the entire bottle if anyone writes a single line of code.

article_content: On Monday, a wave of coordinated bombings ripped through several regions of Iraq, leaving at least 42 people dead and more than 257 injured, according to local police. The blasts struck in at least seven provinces — including Baghdad, Anbar, Babil, Kirkuk, Salahuddin, Diyala, and Nasiriyah — with multiple incidents reported in the capital alone. Two explosives detonated near the entrance to Baghdad’s international airport, while other attacks focused on security checkpoints, political buildings, and predominantly Shiite neighborhoods. Police sources told CNN that many of the Baghdad attacks specifically targeted Shia communities. Al Qaeda in Iraq, a Sunni militant faction, has publicly claimed responsibility for numerous violent incidents over the past few months. As provincial elections loom just five days away, political leaders are growing increasingly anxious that persistent violence could deter voters from heading to polling stations, potentially undermining the legitimacy of the electoral process.
