Twee bomme het naby die ingang van Bagdad se internasionale lughawe ontplof, terwyl ander aanvalle op veiligheidskontrolepunte, politieke geboue en oorwegend Sjiitiese wyke gefokus het. Polisiebronne het CNN vertel dat baie van die Bagdad-aanvalle spesifiek Sjiitiese gemeenskappe gemik het. article_content: Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg has stated that while individuals should be free to wear religious clothing, full veils like the niqab or burqa may be inappropriate in certain settings—such as airports and classrooms—where clear identification or face-to-face communication is essential. Clegg emphasized that he does not support a legal ban on religious attire, calling instead for a national conversation rooted in mutual respect. He stressed that Britain should avoid imposing top-down rules on personal dress, calling such measures 'very un-British.' However, he acknowledged exceptions: security protocols at airports require visibility, and in classrooms, teachers need to see students’ faces to foster effective learning and engagement. The government, including Prime Minister David Cameron, supports allowing institutions like schools to establish their own uniform policies, but insists Parliament should not legislate on everyday clothing choices. Home Office minister Jeremy Browne expressed discomfort with restricting religious expression but raised concerns about young girls potentially feeling pressured to wear veils, comparing it to societal limits on underage drinking or marriage. The debate intensified after Birmingham Metropolitan College overturned its eight-year ban on full-face veils following a 9,000-signature petition and accusations of Islamophobia. The college had previously required students to be 'easily identifiable' at all times, a rule that also applied to hoodies and hats. Conservative MP Sarah Wollaston has been a vocal advocate for banning veils in educational institutions, arguing they conflict with gender equality by rendering women 'invisible.' Her remarks sparked backlash, with critics accusing her of Islamophobia, while she defended her stance as a feminist critique—not bigotry. Meanwhile, a landmark court case is underway at Blackfriars Crown Court, where a judge must decide whether a Muslim woman can wear her veil during her trial for witness intimidation. The court is weighing the defendant’s religious rights against jurors’ need to assess her facial expressions. With 43% of Birmingham Metropolitan College’s 44,000 students belonging to non-white ethnic groups, the controversy highlights broader tensions between cultural inclusion, institutional authority, and individual rights in modern Britain.

article_content: Once hailed as the greatest hope in U.S. soccer, Freddy Adu — the teenage prodigy dubbed 'the next Pele' — has seen his career plummet from international stardom to hosting nights at a Washington, D.C. nightclub. The 25-year-old forward, who made headlines in 2004 by signing with D.C. United at age 14, now appears regularly at the Shadow Room, according to a recent Facebook event listing. His professional journey since then has been marked by instability: after a promising start, Adu moved through nine clubs across five countries — including Benfica, Monaco, Philadelphia Union, and FK Jagodina — often without making a single appearance. He played 87 matches for D.C. United between 2004 and 2006, scoring 24 goals, and represented the U.S. at the 2007 U-20 World Cup and the 2008 Olympics. But since the end of the 2012 MLS season, he has logged just 59 minutes of competitive play. In 2013, after two seasons with Philadelphia Union, he briefly joined Brazilian side Bahia before being released. He later trained with England’s Blackpool and Norway’s Stabaek, and even had a trial with Dutch club AZ Alkmaar — all without securing a contract. His final club, FK Jagodina in Serbia, released him in 2014 after six months without a single appearance. Since then, Adu has been without a team. Despite his struggles, Adu remains the only American to have scored a hat-trick at the U-17 World Championships — a testament to his early brilliance. Born in Ghana and raised in the U.S., he holds American citizenship and represented the U.S. at youth and senior levels.

Die 25-jarige aanvaller, wat in 2004 berug geword het toe hy op 14-jarige ouderdom by D.C. United geteken het, verskyn nou gereeld by die Shadow Room, volgens 'n onlangse Facebook-gebeurtenis. Hy het 87 wedstryde vir D.C. United tussen 2004 en 2006 gespeel, met 24 doele, en die VSA verteenwoordig by die 2007 U-20-Wêreldkampioenskap en die 2008 Olimpiese Spele. article_content: For centuries, many Britons have believed their island nation was a fortress — too remote and resilient to ever be conquered after 1066. But a new book by historian Ian Hernon, titled 'Fortress Britain,' turns that idea on its head. Hernon has uncovered evidence of at least 73 significant foreign incursions onto British soil between the Norman Conquest and the Nazi occupation of the Channel Islands. These weren’t just big, headline-making invasions; many were small raids by French privateers, Spanish fleets, or even Barbary pirates from North Africa. Some succeeded briefly, others fizzled out due to stormy seas or poor coordination. The famous Glorious Revolution of 1688? That was an invasion too — when William of Orange landed in Devon with a Dutch army and took the throne without firing a shot. Even the sinking of the Mary Rose in 1545 happened during a French naval assault. The last time enemy troops set foot on mainland Britain was in 1797, when French soldiers landed in Fishguard, Wales. The final armed clash occurred in 1940, when German paratroopers skirmished with British militia in Kent. Meanwhile, while Britain prides itself on being uninvadable, records show it has launched military operations in nearly 90% of the world’s countries — a stark contrast to how it sees itself. Hernon’s goal? To remind people that history isn’t always what we’re taught — and that even islands have porous borders.

Hernon het bewyse van ten minste 73 beduidende buitelandse ingrypings op Britse grond ontdek tussen die Normandiese Verowering en die Nazi-besetting van die Kanaleilande. Dit was nie net groot, koplyn-invasies nie; baie was klein aanvalle deur Franse privaatiers, Spaanse vloote, of selfs Barbaryske piraate uit Noord-Afrika. Sommige het kortstondig sukses gehad, ander het weens stormagtige see of swak koördinasie misluk. Die beroemde Glorieuze Revolusie van 1688? Daar was ook 'n inval — toe William van Oranje in Devon met 'n Nederlands leger geland het en die troon oorgeneem het sonder 'n skoot af te vuur. Selfs die sink van die Mary Rose in 1545 het tydens 'n Franse see-aanval gebeur. Die laaste gewapende botsing het in 1940 plaasgevind toe Duitse parachutiste 'n klein geveg met Britse milisie in Kent gehad het. Tuis, terwyl Brittanje trots is op sy oninvalbare status, toon rekords dat dit militêre operasies in byna 90% van die wêreld se lande begin het — 'n skerp teenstelling met hoe dit homself sien. article_content: With ambulance services stretched to breaking point, firefighters across England are increasingly being called upon to transport patients to A&E departments — despite having only basic medical training and limited equipment such as bandages. This shift has become more common as hospitals report unprecedented patient volumes, with seven facilities still under 'major incident' status after 13 hospitals declared such emergencies within just 36 hours on Monday and Tuesday. These declarations — typically reserved for large-scale disasters like terrorist attacks or train crashes — reflect a system under severe strain. At Weston General Hospital, expectant mothers were redirected 16 miles away because labor wards had been converted into overflow A&E space. In Birmingham, administrative staff with no clinical training have been asked to assist on hospital wards. Meanwhile, A&E waiting times have reached their worst levels in a decade. One case involved 88-year-old Jenny Knowles, who waited over seven hours for treatment after fracturing her nose in a fall. Her family reported that an ambulance didn’t arrive until 3:30 a.m., nearly four hours after the 999 call was placed. Another heartbreaking story came from Portsmouth, where an 81-year-old woman spent 16 hours waiting for care after a suspected stroke. Her family eventually took her home, exhausted and disillusioned. The Fire Brigades Union warns that these practices endanger the public. General Secretary Matt Wrack blames years of cuts to both NHS and fire service budgets, noting that firefighters are being pulled away from their core duties. Ambulances are often stuck outside hospitals, unable to offload patients, leaving them unavailable for new emergencies. In York, firefighters transported a fall victim simply because no ambulance was available. While the Department of Health claims that firefighter involvement is rare and limited to initial stabilization, evidence from multiple regions suggests a growing pattern of reliance on fire crews as de facto ambulances.

article_content: As the United States closes several diplomatic posts abroad amid concerns over potential attacks, major U.S. cities like New York and San Francisco have heightened security measures — not because of any specific threat, but out of an abundance of caution. In New York, police have increased patrols around transportation hubs and religious sites, according to NYPD spokesman James Duffy. Similarly, San Francisco authorities have boosted presence at mass transit stations, popular landmarks, and foreign embassies, said spokesman Gordon Shyy. In Washington, D.C., Metro Transit Police Chief Ron Pavlik emailed staff Friday night, stating, 'There is no specific or credible threat against Metro or any other U.S. transportation system. But this global alert serves as a reminder to stay vigilant at all times.' Meanwhile, U.S. Park Police spokesman Paul Brooks confirmed no additional security measures have been ordered at national monuments. In Los Angeles, police and the county sheriff’s office reported no formal directives but advised officers to remain slightly more alert than usual. Miami police told CNN operations remain 'business as usual,' with constant threat monitoring in place. Houston police declined to comment on tactical operations. CNN contributors Josh Levs, Chuck Johnston, Greg Seaby, Chris Boyette, Devon Sayers, Marlena Baldacci, and Stella Chan provided reporting support.

article_content: On a quiet Monday morning at Holywood Golf Club in Northern Ireland, the usual rhythm of the course was interrupted by a gentle buzz — not from tournaments or crowds, but from memory. At ‘Rory’s Corner,’ a modest display case in the clubhouse now holds more than trophies; it holds the story of a boy who became a legend. Just days after lifting the Claret Jug at Hoylake, Rory McIlroy’s latest triumph joined his US Open trophy, Ryder Cup bag, MBE medal, and childhood prize from the World Under-10 Championship. But the real magic isn’t in the objects — it’s in the people who watched him grow. McIlroy didn’t just play here — he was raised here. His grandfather, Jimmy, worked the cranes at Harland and Wolff. His father, Gerry, once tended the bar. His uncles, Brian and Colin, were past club champions. Even the club’s rules bent for him: at seven, he was too young to join, so members voted to change the constitution. One surviving member, Jimmy Curtis, recalls the whole snooker team being named Jimmy — all seven of them — and how those bonds still echo today. Paul Gray, the club’s former pro, remembers watching a seven-year-old Rory chip balls near the bar. By thirteen, Gray admitted, Rory was better than him. He recalls one unforgettable shot: a 200-yard four-iron into a gale, the pin tucked behind a bunker — and the ball landed two feet from the hole. ‘That’s when you knew,’ Gray said. ‘It wasn’t if he’d be great. It was how great.’ In Holywood, celebrations were quiet. No fireworks. No street parties. Just a montage of Rory’s face in the window of the local hardware store, and another in the estate agent’s glass. But the impact? Profound. Schoolkids now flood the course. Americans fly in just to stand where he took his first swing. And one local man, Wilbur Walker, pocketed £25,000 after betting years ago that Rory would win the Open by 26 — a prediction that turned out to be eerily precise. From a boy who broke the rules to a man who rewrote history, McIlroy’s journey didn’t begin on a global stage — it began in a small club with a stubborn constitution, a loving family, and a community that believed before the world did.

article_content: Sanjeev Sanyal, an advisor to India’s Prime Minister on economic matters, argues that the idea of 'jobless growth' doesn’t exist. He insists that when an economy grows—even under tough global conditions like war and supply chain chaos—it naturally creates jobs. Right now, India is growing at 6.5% to 7%, and if global conditions improve, that could easily jump past 8%. According to Sanyal, the secret isn’t just growth—it’s compounding growth over time, which steadily builds employment opportunities. He also defends the government’s free ration program, clarifying it’s not meant to tame inflation. Instead, it’s a lifeline for low-income families. While rice and wheat prices may rise, their share in household spending is shrinking as Indians eat more varied diets—eggs, fish, lentils, vegetables. So, the program helps the poorest most, but barely affects overall price trends for the average person. Sanyal points to strong domestic signals: car sales jumped 16% last year (after already recovering from pandemic lows), bank lending is soaring at nearly 19% annually, air travel is up 18%, and tax collections (GST) rose 13%. These aren’t flukes—they show real momentum. Even global institutions like the IMF and World Bank agree: India is the fastest-growing major economy today. While exports are flat—partly because Europe is struggling and global demand is weak—India’s growth is being fueled internally. The country is drawing in factories relocating from China, especially in electronics and pharma. Plus, big bets are being placed on future-ready industries like green hydrogen and nuclear power. Some worry that household savings are collapsing. Sanyal says that’s misleading. People aren’t saving less—they’re spending more on homes. With lower interest rates in recent years, many took loans to build or upgrade houses. Now that rates are rising again, financial savings are starting to bounce back. Total savings and investment in the economy are still climbing. Poverty, he notes, has dropped sharply over the past decade thanks to targeted programs—clean cooking gas, health insurance (Ayushman Bharat), toilets, and housing. Free rations are part of keeping that progress secure as the economy transforms. And when asked about ancient wisdom, Sanyal highlights thinkers like Kautilya—who believed the state should focus on infrastructure, security, and fair markets, but stay out of micromanaging citizens. That balance, he suggests, still holds lessons today.

Tans groei Indië met 6,5% tot 7%, en as die globale omstandighede verbeter, kan dit maklik bo 8% uitkom. Volgens Sanyal is die sleutel nie net groei nie—dit is die kumulatiewe groei oor tyd, wat geleidelik werksgeleenthede bou. Hy verdedig ook die regering se gratis graanprogram, en verduidelik dat dit nie bedoel is om inflasie te beheer nie. In plaas daarvan is dit 'n lewenslyn vir lae-inkomste families. Hoewel ryshawers en tarwe pryse mag styg, neem hul aandeel in huishoudelike uitgawes af terwyl Indiërs meer gevarieerde diëte eet—eiers, vis, lente, groente. Dus, die program help die armste die meeste, maar het min invloed op die algemene prysvlak vir die gemiddelde persoon. Sanyal wys na sterk interne tekens: motorverkope het die vorige jaar met 16% gestyg (ná reeds herstel van pandemiese lae), leningsgroei is byna 19% jaarliks, lugverkeer is met 18% gestyg, en belastinginkomste (GST) het met 13% toegeneem. Dit is nie toevalle nie—hulle toon werklike momentum. Selfs globale instellings soos die IMF en Wereldbank stem saam: Indië is vandag die vinnigste groeiende groot ekonomie. Terwyl uitvoere plat is—deels omdat Europa struikel en globale vraag swak is—word Indië se groei gedryf deur interne faktore. Die land trek fabrieke aan wat vanaf China verplaas word, veral in elektronika en farmaseutika. Buitendien word groot inskrywings gemaak in toekomstgerigte industrieë soos groen waterstof en kernenergie. Sommiges worry dat huishoudelike besparings instort. Sanyal sê dit is misleidend. Mense spaar nie minder nie—hulle gee meer uit aan huise. Met laer rentekoerse in die onlangse jare, het baie lenings geneem om hul huise te bou of te verbeter. Nou dat rentekoerse styg, begin finansiële besparings weer terugkeer. Totale besparings en belegginge in die ekonomie styg steeds. Armoede, hy merk op, het die afgelope dekade skerp afgenam dankzij gerigte programme—skoon kookgas, gesondheidsversekering (Ayushman Bharat), toilette en huisvesting. Gratis graan is deel van die beskerming van hierdie vooruitgang terwyl die ekonomie transformeer. En toe gevra oor antieke wijsheid, noem Sanyal denkers soos Kautilya—wat glo dat die staat fokus moet wees op infrastruktuur, sekuriteit en billike markte, maar buite mikrobestuur van burgers moet bly. Daardie balans, hy stel voor, hou nog steeds lesse vir vandag.

article_content: Kieran Trippier, the 23-year-old right-back currently shining for Burnley in the Premier League, is setting his sights on an England recall. Once a standout in the Championship — named to the league’s Team of the Season for two consecutive years — Trippier believes his consistent performances could finally catch the eye of England manager Roy Hodgson. Having represented England at every youth level from U18 to U21, he hasn’t given up on his childhood dream of wearing the Three Lions shirt at senior level. 'It’s always been my goal,' he said. 'I loved every moment playing for England as a kid, and now that I’m competing in the top flight, I’m determined to show what I’m capable of.' Despite speculation linking him with a move to Arsenal last summer, Trippier chose to commit fully to Burnley, signing a three-year deal that keeps him at Turf Moor until 2017. 'Leaving was never even on my mind,' he insisted. 'I’ve had two great seasons here, and I’m thrilled to be part of this journey. Getting the contract sorted early meant I could relax over the summer and come back focused.' His journey to the Premier League wasn’t straightforward. A product of Manchester City’s academy since age eight, Trippier never broke into their first team. After two loan spells at Barnsley, he joined Burnley on loan in 2011 and made the switch permanent months later. 'I knew I needed games — not reserve football — so I made the decision to leave City, even though it was tough emotionally,' he reflected. 'I still keep in touch with some of the staff who helped me grow, but when I walk onto the Etihad pitch, I’ll be wearing Burnley blue — no friends, no second thoughts.' Burnley’s rise from Championship contenders to Premier League survivors has been remarkable. Last season, few expected them to escape relegation — let alone win automatic promotion after selling star striker Charlie Austin. Now, facing another uphill battle, Trippier draws hope from Crystal Palace’s dramatic 11th-place finish in 2013–14 after being written off by Christmas. 'We’ve been counted out before — and we proved everyone wrong,' he said. 'So why not again?' With their opening Premier League fixture against Chelsea looming, Trippier and Burnley are ready to defy the odds once more.

article_content: Reality star and fashion influencer Uorfi Javed made headlines on Friday after a viral video showed her being falsely 'arrested' by two women posing as police officers — allegedly for her bold outfit. The clip quickly spread across social media, prompting an official response from Mumbai Police. In a statement posted on their verified Instagram account, they clarified that no real arrest occurred, condemned the misuse of police uniforms and insignia, and emphasized that 'one cannot violate the law of the land for cheap publicity.' The Mumbai Police shared a screenshot from the video and confirmed that a criminal case has been filed under Sections 171, 419, 500, and 34 of the Indian Penal Code at Oshiwara Police Station. The individual impersonating an officer has been taken into custody, and the vehicle used in the stunt has been seized. On the same day, Uorfi Javed addressed the incident on her Instagram, revealing it was a planned campaign for the launch of her new clothing line, 'FREAKIN’ UORFICATION,' in collaboration with @Freakinsindia. She captioned a photo, 'Arrested by the fashion police for my fierce fashion game — but nothing can stop me!' Known for her daring style and frequent appearances on reality TV — including Bigg Boss OTT — Uorfi has long been a target of online trolling and paparazzi attention. While her stunt sparked controversy, it also underscored the fine line between creative promotion and legal boundaries in digital culture.

article_content: E-cigarette use among U.S. high school students dropped significantly this year, falling from 14% to 10%, according to a government survey released on Thursday, November 2. Despite this decline, e-cigarettes remain the most commonly used tobacco product among teenagers and younger adolescents. The 2023 school-based survey, conducted by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) between March and June, marks the first clear downward trend in youth vaping since the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted year-over-year comparisons. For middle school students—typically aged 11 to 13—the change in e-cigarette use was not statistically significant, rising slightly from 3.3% in 2022 to 4.6% in 2023. Health officials noted troubling patterns: about half of students who have ever tried e-cigarettes report currently using them, suggesting high rates of continued use after initial experimentation. Overall, 22.2% of surveyed students—roughly 6.2 million in total—reported using any tobacco product, while 10% reported current e-cigarette use. Among current users, 25.2% vape daily, and 89.4% use flavored products. 'The decline in e-cigarette use among high school students shows great progress, but our work is far from over,' said Deirdre Lawrence Kittner, Director of the CDC's Office on Smoking and Health. 'Findings from this report underscore the threat that commercial tobacco product use poses to the health of our nation’s youth.'

Vir middelskoolleerlinge—gewoonlik ouderdom 11 tot 13—is die verandering in e-sigaretgebruik nie statisties betekenisvol nie, en het dit effens gestyg van 3,3% in 2022 na 4,6% in 2023. Onder tansgebruikers gebruik 25,2% daagliks en 89,4% geurige e-sigarette. 'Die daling in e-sigaretgebruik onder hoërskoolleerlinge toon groot vooruitgang, maar ons werk is ver van verby,' sê Deirdre Lawrence Kittner, direkteur van die CDC se Kantoor vir Rook en Gesondheid. 'Vindinge uit hierdie verslag onderstreep die dreigement wat kommersiële tabakprodukte op die gesondheid van ons nasie se jeug uitoefen.'

article_content: A couple whose teenage son drowned during a school excursion was awarded just a fraction of the $100 million they sought, after a judge ruled the father was not a credible witness. The Presbyterian Church will pay the Chaina family $492,373 in compensation following the 1999 death of 15-year-old Nathan Chaina during a hiking trip organized by Scots College’s Glengarry campus in Kangaroo Valley. Nathan drowned after being swept away by floodwaters while crossing Yurrunga Creek, 24 hours after he went missing. His parents, George and Rita Chaina, sued the Presbyterian Church Property Trust, arguing the school failed in its duty of care. Justice Davies of the NSW Supreme Court acknowledged the family’s grief but rejected the bulk of their claim, stating that George Chaina’s testimony lacked consistency and was influenced by a 'fixed and almost delusional view' of his personal achievements and business success. Chaina had falsely claimed to hold a science degree from UNSW and to have been recruited by Procter & Gamble — fabrications he maintained for decades. The court found that any decline in the family’s businesses after Nathan’s death was not caused by the school, but by their own decisions not to re-engage with their enterprises. Justice Davies also noted that Chaina’s motivations appeared 'at least partly driven by a desire for vengeance.' However, a 2001 coronial inquest by Deputy Coroner Jan Stevenson had already concluded that Nathan’s death was 'primarily attributable to the school overlooking ordinary aspects of human nature, together with a lack of risk management and safety procedures.' The family, from Vaucluse, reportedly spent over $20 million on legal costs. After the verdict, George Chaina stated, 'We are trying to do the right thing by the public — so it doesn’t happen again.' Justice Davies is yet to rule on whether interest will be added to the compensation and who will bear the legal costs.

Die Presbiteriaanse Kerk sal die Chaina-familie $492 373 in vergoeding betaal ná die 1999-dood van 15-jarige Nathan Chaina tydens 'n wandeltocht wat georganiseer is deur Scots College se Glengarry-kampus in Kangaroo Valley. article_content: WASHINGTON (CNN) — President Obama is expected to approve a plan to withdraw the majority of U.S. combat troops from Iraq within 19 months, according to Pentagon officials. The decision is set to be formally announced at Camp Lejeune in North Carolina on Friday, a senior administration source told CNN. While the White House has not yet issued an official statement, officials indicate the timing reflects a shift in policy. Obama initially pledged to remove combat forces within 16 months during his campaign. Shortly after taking office, however, he requested alternative timelines from military leaders, who presented options for withdrawal at 16, 19, and 23 months. The anticipated final plan calls for the bulk of combat units to leave, while approximately 50,000 troops remain in Iraq primarily as trainers and advisers. Even these residual forces may be drawn into combat operations if necessary. Over the past two months, U.S. Central Command has been evaluating logistical plans for the drawdown, including routes through Jordan and Kuwait. Officials are also determining whether equipment will be repatriated to the United States, transferred to Iraqi or Jordanian authorities, redirected to Afghanistan, or decommissioned. A U.S. military official, speaking on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of pre-announcement planning, confirmed the ongoing assessments.

article_content: In 1917, Walter Tull became the first Black officer in the British Army — a groundbreaking achievement at a time when racial barriers were deeply entrenched. During the First World War, he led troops with distinction in Italy and France, earning praise from fellow officers for his calm courage under fire. After his death in March 1918, letters from Lieutenant Pickard and Major Poole confirmed that Tull had been formally recommended for the Military Cross, Britain’s highest award for gallantry. Yet, the medal was never bestowed. Decades later, historians and family members suspect racial prejudice was to blame: official regulations at the time forbade non-European officers from commanding white soldiers. Today, more than 90 years after his death, a grassroots campaign led by MP Brian Binley and Tull’s great-nephew Edward Finlayson is pushing for the award to be granted posthumously. The effort has gained momentum with support from acclaimed author Michael Morpurgo, whose novel 'A Medal for Leroy' draws inspiration from Tull’s life. Beyond the battlefield, Tull was also a trailblazer in sport: he was the first Black outfield player in England’s top-flight football league, starring for Tottenham Hotspur and Northampton Town. Born in Kent in 1888 to a Barbadian carpenter and a local Englishwoman, Tull lost both parents by age ten and grew up in an orphanage in East London. His journey from poverty and loss to military leadership and sporting fame makes him a powerful symbol of resilience. Though his body was never recovered from No Man’s Land, his legacy lives on — now taught in schools across Britain as a lesson in courage, equality, and the fight against racism.

article_content: In a heartwarming scene at Lake Clark National Park in Alaska, a six-month-old brown bear cub scratched its back against its mother’s fur — turning her into a living scratching post. Moments before, the playful cub had been tumbling and wrestling with its sibling, full of energy. The candid moments were captured by wildlife photographer D. Robert Franz, who has spent years observing bears near Yellowstone National Park. Franz, 56, says the bears embody the essence of true wilderness and are among his favorite subjects to photograph. From a safe distance of about 25 meters, he watched as the family interacted: playing, napping, and bonding. He notes that while people often react to the images with delight over the cubs’ cuteness, the deeper message is about respecting wild animals in their natural habitat. Franz warns that growing urban disconnection leads many to underestimate the risks of approaching wildlife — a behavior that endangers both humans and animals. Bear cubs stay with their mothers for two to four years, learning everything they need to survive. Though he feels no fear during shoots, Franz stresses that grizzly bears remain powerful and unpredictable creatures.

article_content: In 2011, a Florida man named Christopher Chaney became the center of a major cybercrime case after hacking into the private email accounts of more than 50 celebrities. Among those targeted were high-profile stars like Scarlett Johansson, Mila Kunis, and Christina Aguilera. Chaney didn’t break into their phones directly—he used publicly available details to guess passwords and then hijacked email forwarding settings, allowing him to secretly copy every message they received. He admitted to leaking intimate photos of Johansson to a celebrity site, but insisted he never sought money or threatened his victims. In a rare interview after his arrest, Chaney described his actions as stemming from a troubling obsession—not greed. 'I was just curious,' he said. 'It became something I couldn’t stop.' He later apologized, calling the breach one of the worst forms of privacy invasion possible. Federal prosecutors charged him with 26 counts, including identity theft and illegal access to protected computers. The FBI revealed that Chaney operated under several online aliases and exploited weaknesses in common security practices. His methods were methodical: reset passwords using public info, take control of accounts, search for sensitive material, and set up automatic email forwarding to stay informed—even after victims changed their passwords. The case, dubbed 'Operation Hackerazzi,' drew national attention not just because of the famous names involved, but because it exposed how vulnerable even tech-savvy individuals can be. U.S. Attorney Andre Birotte Jr. condemned the hackers as 'scum' and warned the public that weak passwords and careless online habits leave everyone at risk. The scandal echoed earlier controversies in the UK, like the News of the World phone-hacking scandal, reminding society that privacy violations aren’t new—they’re just evolving. Investigators hope the high-profile nature of this case will push more people to use stronger passwords, enable two-factor authentication, and rethink what they share online. As Birotte put it: 'Protecting your digital life isn’t optional—it’s essential.'

article_content: On Wednesday night, Edgar Tamayo, a 46-year-old Mexican citizen, was executed by lethal injection in Texas for the 1994 murder of Houston police officer Guy Gaddis. Despite heartfelt appeals from the Mexican government and the U.S. State Department to halt the execution, Texas proceeded. Tamayo, who was living in the U.S. illegally and had a prior robbery conviction in California, was never told after his arrest that he had the right to contact the Mexican consulate — a legal protection under the 1963 Vienna Convention. His defense team argued this failure deprived him of vital legal assistance that could have altered the outcome of his trial. At the moment of execution, Tamayo declined to speak and showed no visible reaction as the lethal drug took effect. He was pronounced dead 17 minutes later at 9:32 p.m. CST. While Gaddis’s mother and close relatives watched through a window inside the prison, Tamayo’s cousin Edelmira Arias wept alongside family members gathered at his parents’ home in Miacatlán, Mexico. Outside the facility, dozens of police officers and supporters revved their motorcycles in tribute to the fallen officer. Texas officials stood firm, stating that regardless of nationality, anyone who commits a grave crime under Texas law must answer for it — including facing the death penalty. Although the U.S. Supreme Court and lower courts acknowledged the Vienna Convention violation, they ruled that without specific federal legislation, states are not obligated to reopen such cases. Mexico called the execution a violation of international obligations, while Texas reaffirmed its dedication to enforcing its own judicial system.

article_content: An injured female cuckoo named Idemili, who was airlifted in business class to Italy to resume her migration, has been successfully released back into the wild. The two-year-old bird began her journey from Brechfa Forest in Carmarthenshire, Wales, alongside four male cuckoos, but became stranded in Tolworth, Surrey — malnourished, emaciated, and unable to carry her GPS tracker. After a month of intensive care at the Wildlife Aid Centre in Leatherhead, she was flown by British Airways from Gatwick to Turin, Italy — traveling in a custom carrier placed in a business-class seat, complete with security screening and access to the business class lounge. Accompanied by vet nurse Lucy Kells, Idemili slept through most of the flight. Upon arrival, she was met by Dan Chamberlain and Enrico Caprio, University of Turin students who coordinated her release. Despite plans to wait a day, the team decided to release her immediately after hearing the call of a wild cuckoo nearby — a sign she was in suitable habitat. Released at the Association Center for Storks in Racconigi, Idemili did not fly away immediately. Instead, she perched in a tree, preened for nearly 30 minutes, and feasted on caterpillars. Then, in a deeply emotional moment, she called out — a sound Kells had never heard from her during their month together. The response moved Kells to tears. Though no longer tracked, Idemili is now continuing her epic migration across the Mediterranean and Sahara Desert toward her wintering grounds in the Congo. Kells, a veteran vet nurse with 21 years’ experience, described the encounter as the most extraordinary of her career — and a privilege she will never forget.

article_content: Ride-sharing service Uber has issued an apology after it implemented surge pricing as frightened Sydneysiders fled last week’s siege at Martin Place. With police urging evacuation, demand for Uber far exceeded available vehicles, triggering an automatic price surge designed to attract more drivers to the area. During the early stages of the siege, fares reportedly quadrupled. In a statement, Uber apologized, saying: 'The events of last week in Sydney were upsetting for the whole community, and we are truly sorry for any concern our pricing process may have caused.' Ride-sharing apps like Uber have become popular alternatives to taxis — much to the frustration of taxi associations worldwide. During the siege, staff and customers were held hostage inside the Lindt Chocolate Café in the heart of Sydney’s CBD. Uber stated it aimed to help evacuate as many people as possible from the CBD, but acknowledged it communicated its intentions poorly, leading to widespread misunderstanding. 'We didn’t stop surge pricing immediately,' Uber admitted. 'This was the wrong decision.' The company later reversed course, offering free rides out of the city center and full refunds to those affected by the price spikes. 'It’s unfortunate that some perceive Uber acted against the public interest,' the company said. 'We certainly did not intend to.' Three people died in the siege at Martin Place’s Lindt Café: gunman Man Haron Monis and two hostages, Tori Johnson and Katrina Dawson. Thousands of tributes have been left at Martin Place in memory of the victims. Initially, Uber attempted to justify the price increase via tweet: 'We are all concerned with events in the CBD. Fares have increased to encourage more drivers to come online and pick up passengers in the area.' But commuters reacted with fury. Web developer Tyson Armstrong tweeted: 'What a shameful disgrace. How low can you go? A marketing fail is one thing — but a lack of compassion is another.' Julie Gozali echoed the sentiment. Mashable reported one user paid $145 for an Uber ride to Sydney Airport under surge pricing, with a temporary minimum fare of $100.

article_content: In a remarkable triumph of science and perseverance, Maggie — a Herdwick sheep born from a frozen embryo preserved during the devastating 2001 foot-and-mouth disease outbreak — has given birth to healthy twin lambs in April 2013. Her birth in 2011 was already a miracle: the product of an emergency effort by Cumbrian farmers and scientists to rescue one of Britain’s most vital sheep breeds from extinction. Now, two years later, Maggie has become a mother herself, proving that the legacy of that desperate act continues. The initiative began when Professor Dianna Bowles, a researcher at the University of York and founder of the Sheep Trust, teamed up with local farmers to freeze embryos of purebred Herdwicks as the epidemic wiped out tens of thousands of animals. Among those saved was the embryo that would become Maggie. Raised from infancy by a young girl named Evie Church, who was moved by her father’s stories of animals being culled on their farm in Lofthouse, Yorkshire, Maggie was later passed to Margaret Hall, a farmer who welcomed her into her flock. When Maggie fell seriously ill in late 2012, the Sheep Trust stepped in again to care for her — and, to everyone’s surprise, she became pregnant soon after. Against the odds, Maggie recovered and delivered two healthy lambs, joining another ewe from the same program who also gave birth to twins. ‘This isn’t just luck,’ says Professor Bowles. ‘It’s science making real, lasting change. Twelve years after the crisis, we’re seeing life come from something we froze in a test tube.’ The Herdwick breed, known for its hardiness and deep cultural roots in the Lake District and Yorkshire Dales, was nearly lost — but thanks to foresight, community effort, and cutting-edge biology, it’s now thriving again. Maggie’s story isn’t just about one sheep. It’s about how ordinary people, guided by science, can rewrite the future of agriculture.

article_content: On a dramatic Wednesday night at Celtic Park, 60,000 fans turned the stadium into a sea of Palestinian flags—not to cheer for football, but to stand with Gaza. As Celtic faced Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, the sight of thousands waving Palestinian banners sent ripples across the globe, amplified by social media and broadcast worldwide. The movement was spearheaded by the Green Brigade, a passionate fan group founded in 2006 known for its staunch advocacy of Palestinian rights and Irish republican ideals. Their display, however, came at a cost. Days earlier, the club had warned fans not to bring political symbols to the game, and shortly after, the Green Brigade was banned from all matches—home and away. The club cited pyrotechnics and unauthorized banners as reasons, but the group insists the real trigger was their solidarity with Palestine. 'The other issues are a smokescreen,' they told Al Jazeera. 'They’re punishing us because they know most fans agree with us.' Celtic’s identity is inseparable from its roots: founded by Irish immigrants in 19th-century Glasgow, the club has long been a beacon for marginalized voices. Support for Palestine isn’t new—it predates the Green Brigade. In 2016, after UEFA fined Celtic for displaying pro-Palestinian banners, fans didn’t pay the penalty—they raised £175,000 to build a football team in Aida refugee camp. That bond still thrives today, with regular exchanges between Glasgow and Bethlehem. Meanwhile, in Gaza, the Benn’a Sports Club, whose players once wore Celtic’s green and white hoops, now sits in ruins. Its manager, Hazem Tabash, watched the match on his phone, despite Israel’s communications blackout. 'Your flags gave us hope,' he said. 'You’re reminding the world we’re not forgotten.' Yet the club’s leadership appears increasingly isolated. The Celtic Trust and fellow ultras group Bhoys Celtic have denounced the ban, with the latter staging a walkout during their next match. 'There will be no return to normality,' they declared. Critics argue that football authorities are applying double standards: Russia was swiftly banned from competitions after invading Ukraine, yet no similar action has been taken against Israel despite its devastating assault on Gaza. 'Is it because Palestinians are brown?' asked David Webber, a football and politics expert. 'Or is it because power chooses who gets to be heard?' The Green Brigade, undeterred, stands by their motto: 'Until The Last Rebel.' For them, football isn’t just sport—it’s a platform for justice. And they won’t let a boardroom decide what they can or can’t believe.

article_content: Lionel Messi didn’t have time to master Cockney rhyming slang during his brief visit to London’s East End — but the West Ham faithful certainly couldn’t 'Adam and Eve' it when they saw the world’s greatest footballer light up Upton Park. Despite playing at less than full throttle, Messi dazzled the crowd, ultimately sealing a 2-1 victory for Argentina with a clinical penalty. Thousands of fans arrived hours before kickoff just to watch him warm up, wearing his signature orange Adidas boots. The atmosphere exploded when his name was called, and within five minutes, his dazzling dribble left Croatia’s defense scrambling — though Sergio Aguero missed the follow-up. Croatia struck first in the 11th minute through Anas Sharbini, leaving Messi visibly frustrated for much of the first half. Yet every time he touched the ball, the crowd held its breath. He carved open defenses with precise passes, forced saves from goalkeeper Lovre Kalinic, and nearly equalized with a near-post strike that clipped the side netting. The breakthrough came in the 48th minute when Cristian Ansaldi’s powerful long-range shot deflected off Aguero to level the score. The home crowd roared as if it were a league decider. Then, in the 57th minute, Messi delivered perfection: a slide-rule pass to Aguero, who was brought down in the box. Messi stepped up and calmly converted his 45th international goal. Upton Park erupted in chants of 'Messi, Messi!' The night’s second emotional highlight came when Carlos Tevez, the beloved former West Ham striker, entered the pitch in the 61st minute. Though dubbed a 'legend' by the announcer — a stretch given his short tenure — the crowd’s deafening roar proved his enduring bond with the club. Even though Messi missed a late chance, his dominance was undeniable. In a night filled with nostalgia and flair, it was clear: this wasn’t just a friendly. It was a celebration of greatness — and for once, even Tevez had to share the spotlight.

article_content: Four years after being acquitted of murdering his new wife during their honeymoon in South Africa, Shrien Dewani is returning to Britain aboard a private jet funded by his affluent family. Yet despite his wealth and social standing, the one thing he has long sought—public respect—is slipping further away. New legal action, initiated by Anni Hindocha’s family, aims to expose the hidden truths of his personal life, particularly his secret relationships with male sex workers and his participation in fetish communities. Vinod Hindocha, Anni’s father, has hired a London law firm to sue Dewani for deliberately concealing his bisexuality before marriage, arguing that this deception turned their union into a sham. 'Would any parent let their daughter marry someone who sleeps with men?' he asked. 'This wasn’t love—it was performance.' The family also seeks compensation for the £200,000 spent on the lavish wedding, which they believe was built on lies. During the murder trial, Dewani’s sexuality was deemed legally irrelevant by the presiding judge, a decision that blocked prosecutors from exploring potential motives tied to his hidden identity. This ruling stunned many, especially since evidence showed Dewani had spent years and tens of thousands of pounds to keep his double life buried. He retained Max Clifford—a now-imprisoned media fixer—for £30,000 monthly to discredit reports linking him to gay escorts. Clifford publicly swore Dewani had never been intimate with a man, even fabricating stories of female admirers. Only on the first day of the trial, as witnesses prepared to testify, did Dewani quietly admit he was bisexual—in just three sentences. Behind the polished facade, Dewani lived a fractured existence. Raised in a devout, high-status Hindu family in Bristol—with a magistrate father and multi-million-pound property holdings—he was expected to uphold tradition. Yet from his early twenties, he secretly used the username 'asiansubguy' on Gaydar and Recon, sites catering to men into leather and latex fetishes. He frequented Hoist, a notorious London nightclub, and paid Leopold Leisser hundreds of pounds per encounter. These encounters began just months after he started dating Anni. Anni, a Swedish engineering graduate whose family escaped Uganda under Idi Amin, was unaware of her husband’s hidden world. Their relationship was strained from the start. She described feeling rejected, criticized for her appearance, and emotionally isolated. Texts reveal her despair: 'Fighting a lot with Shrien. Wish I never got engaged.' Despite multiple breakups, Dewani’s family pressured her to reconcile, fearing scandal if the engagement collapsed a second time. On their wedding night in Mumbai, the couple barely spoke. Dewani scolded her for not folding her clothes and slept on the sofa—their marriage unconsummated. Days later, in South Africa, Anni was shot dead after a staged carjacking. That same night, Dewani logged into Gaydar from their luxury hotel. Anni’s uncle put it plainly: 'We don’t care if he’s gay. We care that he lied to her. He chose a beautiful woman to appear normal—and destroyed her life in the process.' Now, as Dewani flies home, the world watches. His wealth may shield him from criminal charges, but it cannot erase the pain he left behind—or the legal reckoning still to come.

Maar ondanks sy rykdom en sosiale status, is die een ding wat hy altyd gewens het—openbare respek—besig om te ontglip. Nuwe regtelike aksie, aangebring deur Anni Hindocha se familie, wil die verborge waarhede oor sy persoonlike lewe blootlê, veral sy geheime verhoudings met manlike sekswerkers en sy deelname aan fetisjgemeenskappe. Vinod Hindocha, Anni se pa, het ‘n Londense regsfirm ingehuur om Dewani te kla vir bewustelik sy biseksualiteit voor die huwelik te verskuil, en beweer dat hierdie bedrog hul unie ‘n skynsel gemaak het. 'Wou enige ouer hul dogter laat trou met iemand wat met mans slaap?' het hy gevra. 'Dit was nie liefde nie—dit was prentjie.' Die familie soek ook vergoeding vir die £200 000 wat aan die luukse troue bestee is, wat hulle glo op leuen gebou is. Tydens die moordproses is Dewani se seksualiteit as regsrelevant beskou deur die regspreker, ‘n beslissing wat aanklagters van die moontlike motiewe verhoed het wat verband hou met sy verborge identiteit. Hierdie beslissing het baie verbaas, veral aangesien bewyse getoon het dat Dewani jare en tienduisende pond bestee het om sy dubbellewe te verberg. Hy het Max Clifford—‘n nou geïmprisonseerde mediavaste—vir £30 000 maandeliks aangestel om verslae oor sy verhoudings met manlike escortdiensverleners te ontken. Clifford het openlik beweer dat Dewani nog nooit intiem met ‘n man was nie, selfs fabelagtige verhale van vroulike bewonderaars uitgedink. Net op die eerste dag van die proses, toe getuienis gereed was, het Dewani stilweg erken dat hy biseksueel is—in net drie sinne. Agter die gepolierde voorkoms het Dewani ‘n gespleten bestaan gelei. Opgevoed in ‘n devoted, hoë-status Hindoe-familie in Bristol—met ‘n regspreker-vader en ‘n miljoene-pounds eiendomsempire—was daar verwagting dat hy tradisie sal handhaaf. Maar vanaf sy vroeë twintigerjare het hy stilletjies die gebruikersnaam 'asiansubguy' op Gaydar en Recon gebruik, webwerwe wat op mans gerig is wat lief is vir leer en latex. Hy het Hoist, ‘n berugte Londen-nagklub, besoek en het Leopold Leisser honderde pond per ontmoeting betaal. Hierdie ontmoetings het begin net maande ná hy met Anni begin uitgaan. Anni, ‘n Sweedse ingenieursgraadstudent wie se familie onder Idi Amin uit Oos-Afrika gevlug het, was onbewus van haar man se verborge wêreld. Hul verhouding was vanaf die begin gespanne. Sy het gevoel dat sy afgeweier, krities oor haar voorkoms en emosioneel geïsoleer was. Tekste toon haar disperasie: 'Baie met Shrien stryd. Ek wens ek het nooit verloof nie.' Ten spyte van verskeie skeidings, het Dewani se familie haar gedruk om te versoen, uit vrees vir skandaal as die verloofding ‘n tweede keer misluk. Tydens hul troue in Mumbai het die paar amper nie gespreek nie. Dewani het haar gekritiseer omdat sy haar klere nie gevou het nie en het op die bank geslaap—hul huwelik is nie verbruik nie. Dae later, in Suid-Afrika, is Anni doodgeskiet na ‘n vervalsde motorontvoering. Dié selfde nag het Dewani Gaydar binnegekom vanaf hul luxe hotel. Anni se oom het dit duidelik gestel: 'Ons gee nie om as hy homoseksueel is nie. Ons gee om dat hy vir haar gebedel het. Hy het ‘n pragtige vrou gekies om normaal te lyk—en het haar lewe vernietig.' Nou, terwyl Dewani huisvlieg, kyk die wêreld. Sy rykdom mag hom beskerm teen strafregtelike aanspreeklikheid, maar dit kan die pyn wat hy agtergelaat het—of die regsrekening wat nog kom—nie uitvee.

article_content: In late 2013, 27-year-old Bret Bohn, a fit and active hunting guide from Alaska, sought treatment for minor nasal polyps. After surgery, the growths returned, and he was prescribed Prednisone—a steroid known for possible psychiatric side effects. Soon after, his family noticed alarming changes: severe insomnia, confusion, and erratic behavior. In October, his parents, Glenn and Lorraine, took him to Providence Medical Center in Anchorage after he hadn’t slept for days. Doctors gave him additional medications and sent him home, but his condition worsened. After a seizure, he was readmitted—and reportedly went without sleep for nearly three weeks. His mental clarity declined sharply. The Bohns, who held a legally valid power of attorney dating back to 2007 when Bret was healthy, attempted to assume control of his medical decisions. They requested alternative treatments or a second opinion, but were denied. They also sought to discharge him from the hospital, but were told they lacked legal authority to do so. The hospital, citing concerns about potential self-harm and mental instability, contacted Alaska’s Adult Protective Services. A judge subsequently ruled that Bret, now classified as mentally incapacitated, should become a ward of the state. Since then, his parents have been granted only brief, supervised visits—the most recent occurring on Christmas Day. Lorraine Bohn told KTUU-TV, 'I cry every day. It’s a nightmare.' Meanwhile, supporters have rallied online under the hashtag #FreeBretBohn, calling for transparency and his release. Providence Medical Center declined to comment on the specifics due to patient privacy laws but affirmed its obligation under state law to report suspected harm to vulnerable adults—even when family directives conflict with professional judgment about the patient’s best interests.

Ná 'n ruk het sy familie verontrustingende veranderinge opgemerk: swaar slapeloosheid, verwarring en onstabiliteit. In Oktober het sy ouers, Glenn en Lorraine, hom na Providence Mediese Sentrum in Anchorage geneem ná hy reeds dae sonder slaap gewees het. Dokters het hom meer medikasie gegee en hom huis toe gestuur, maar sy toestand het versleg. Na 'n sekelse het hy weer opgeneem word—en het hy volgens verslae naby drie weke sonder slaap deurgebring. Sy geestelike skerpheid het dramaties afgenom. Die Bohns, wat 'n wettig geldige magsverleening gehad het sedert 2007 toe Bret gesond was, het gepoog om beheer oor sy mediese besluite te verkry. Hulle het alternatiewe behandeling of 'n tweede meningsvorming versoek, maar is geweier. Hulle het ook probeer hom uit die hospitaal laat gaan, maar is vertel dat hulle nie wettig reg het om dit te doen nie. Die hospitaal, met betrekking tot moontlike selfbeskadiging en geestelike instabiliteit, het die Alaskanse Diens vir Beskerming van Volwassenes ingeskakel. 'n Regter het daarna beslis dat Bret, nou as geestelik onbekwaam geklassifiseer, 'n staatseling moet wees. Sedertdien het sy ouers slegs kort, toesigte besoeke gekry—die onlangste op Kersdag. Lorraine Bohn het aan KTUU-TV gesê: 'Ek huil elke dag. Dit is 'n nagmerrie.' Tuis het ondersteuners online saamgekom onder die hashtag #FreeBretBohn en vra vir deursigtigheid en sy vrylating. Providence Mediese Sentrum het geweier om oor die besonderhede te kommentaar weens patientprivaatheid, maar het bevestig dat hulle wettig verplig is om mishandeling of verwaarlozing van kwesbare volwassenes te rapporteer—selfs wanneer familieberaad in stryd is met professionele oordeel oor die pasiënt se beste belange.

article_content: Hong Kong (CNN) — Chinese authorities have culled more than 20,000 birds from a live-poultry trading zone in Shanghai after an unusual strain of bird flu, H7N9, was detected in pigeons sold at a local market, state-run outlet Xinhua reported Friday. The mass cull—including chickens, ducks, geese, and pigeons—comes as Shanghai prepares to temporarily shut down all its live poultry markets. The duration of these closures, announced Friday via the Shanghai Municipal Government’s microblog, remains unclear. By Friday morning, authorities had already closed the Huhai agricultural market, where the H7N9 virus was found in pigeons, according to Xinhua. This strain had not previously been detected in humans until a series of cases emerged in China this week. The Chinese Ministry of Agriculture stated Thursday that genetic analysis revealed a strong overlap between the virus found in the Huhai market pigeons and the strain infecting humans. At the Huhai market, officials are disinfecting surfaces and items that came into contact with the birds, while tracing the origin of the infected pigeons. A 64-year-old man in Huzhou, Zhejiang province, died Thursday night after being confirmed infected with H7N9, the provincial health bureau said Friday. He is one of 14 human cases reported so far—all in eastern coastal China. The first cases were reported Sunday. Four deaths occurred in Shanghai; two in Zhejiang. Ages of infected individuals range from a 4-year-old child, who is recovering, to an 83-year-old man. No cases of human-to-human transmission have been confirmed. A Shanghai resident who developed flu-like symptoms after close contact with a deceased patient tested negative for H7N9, city officials said. Dr. Joseph Bresee, head of the epidemiology and prevention branch at the U.S. CDC’s influenza division, said, 'We don’t yet know how humans contracted the virus.' He added that the virus does not appear to spread easily between people. The CDC in Atlanta is working closely with Chinese authorities to identify the infection source. Meanwhile, researchers are developing a vaccine for H7N9, and U.S. state health departments are preparing contingency plans. In response to regional concerns, Hong Kong’s Hospital Authority dispatched a six-member team—including experts from Hong Kong University and the Center for Health Protection—to Shanghai on Thursday to study the outbreak response. The team returned late Friday. Japan’s National Institute of Infectious Diseases will receive virus samples from China this month to begin genetic analysis and accelerate vaccine readiness, CNN affiliate NHK reported. Professor Malik Peiris of Hong Kong University noted that other H7 strains, such as H7N7, previously caused outbreaks in poultry across the Netherlands, Britain, Canada, the U.S., and Mexico—with documented human infections in all except Mexico. The 2003 H7N7 outbreak in the Netherlands infected 89 people, resulting in one death. The more widely known H5N1 avian flu has infected over 600 people since 2003, killing more than 370, according to the WHO. In February, China reported two new H5N1 cases in Guizhou province, both critically ill. Cambodia has also seen a spike in H5N1-related deaths, particularly among children, raising alarms among regional health officials.

Die massa-afslag—waarby hens, eendjies, ganse en duife vermoor is—kom terwyl Sjanghai voorberei om al sy lewende pluimveemarkte tydelik te sluit. Die duur van hierdie sluitings, aangekondig op Vrydag via die mikroblog van die Sjanghai-stadsgewesregering, is nog onduidelik. Die Chinese minister van Landbou het Donderdag gestel dat genetiese ontleding ‘n sterk ooreenkoms getoon het tussen die virus wat in die Huhai-markduife gevind is, en die een wat mense besmet het. Hy is een van die 14 menslike gevalle wat tot dusver gerapporteer is—almal in die oos-kusgebied van China. Die eerste gevalle is Sondag gerapporteer. Vier sterftes het in Sjanghai plaasgevind; twee in Zhejiang. Die ouderdomme van die besmette mense wissel van ‘n 4-jaar-oue kind, wat herstel, tot ‘n 83-jarige man. Geen gevalle van mens-tot-mens oordrag van die H7N9-virus is tot dusver bevestig nie. ‘n Persoon in Sjanghai wat griepverskynsels ontwikkel het na nabye kontak met ‘n pasiënt wat aan die virus oorlede is, het negatief getoets vir H7N9, het stadsowerhede gesê. Dokter Joseph Bresee, hoof van die epidemiologie- en voorkomingafdeling by die Amerikaanse CDC se griepafdeling, het gesê: 'Ons weet nog nie waar mense die virus vandaan gekry het nie.' Hy het bygevoeg dat die virus nie maklik tussen mense versprei nie. Die CDC in Atlanta werk nou saam met Chinese owerhede om die bron van die menslike infeksies te vind. Tuisdies, navorsers werk aan ‘n vaccin vir H7N9, en Amerikaanse staatgesondheidsdepartemente berei hul voor vir die moontlikheid. In reaksie op regionale besorgdheid het Hongkong se Hospitaalowerheid ‘n ses-lid-span—waaronder ekspernte van die Universiteit van Hongkong en die Sentrum vir Gesondheidsbeskerming—na Sjanghai gestuur op Donderdag om die uitbraakrespons te bestudeer. Die span het laat Vrydag teruggekeer. Japan se Nasionale Instituut vir Infeksiële Siektes sal virusmonster van China hierdie maand ontvang om genetiese ontleding te begin en vaccinlesbaarheid te versnel, het CNN-verwante NHK gerapporteer. Professor Malik Peiris van die Universiteit van Hongkong het opgemerk dat ander H7-strame, soos H7N7, voorheen uitbrake in pluimvee in lande soos Nederland, Brittanje, Kanada, die VSA en Meksiko veroorsaak het—menseinfeksies is in almal behalwe Meksiko gedokumenteer. Die 2003 H7N7-uitbraak in Nederland het 89 mense besmet, waarvan een oorlede is. Die beter bekende H5N1-voëlgrypevirus het sedert 2003 meer as 600 mense besmet, waarvan meer as 370 oorlede is, volgens die WHO. In Februarie het China twee nuwe H5N1-gevalle in die suidelike provinsie Guizhou gerapporteer, albei kritiek siek. Cambodja het ook ‘n toename in H5N1-verwante sterftes, veral onder kinders, gesien, wat regionale gesondheidsowerhede bekommerd maak.

article_content: Bill Cosby and his wife, Camille, are opening their private collection of African-American art to the public for the first time in a landmark exhibition at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of African Art in Washington, D.C. Titled 'Conversations: African and African-American Artworks in Dialogue,' the exhibit will debut on November 9, 2015, and run into early 2016. It will place works from the Cosbys’ collection alongside pieces from the museum’s own African art holdings, exploring shared themes of history, identity, creativity, and power. The collection — comprising more than 300 paintings, prints, sculptures, and drawings — features major figures in African-American art, including Beauford Delaney, Faith Ringgold, Jacob Lawrence, Augusta Savage, and Henry Ossawa Tanner. Many of these works have never been publicly displayed, except for one. Highlights include Henry Ossawa Tanner’s acclaimed oil painting 'The Thankful Poor,' Gerard Sekoto’s 'Boy and the Candle,' and rare 18th- and early 19th-century portraits by Baltimore artist Joshua Johnston, as well as family quilts passed down through generations. In a written statement, Bill Cosby emphasized the importance of giving visibility to artists long silenced: 'It’s a way for people to see what exists and to give voice to many of these artists who were silenced for so long, some of whom will speak no more.' The exhibition marks the museum’s 50th anniversary. Museum Director Johnnetta Betsch Cole stated, 'The exhibition will encourage all of us to draw from the creativity that is Africa, to recognize the shared history that inextricably links Africa and the African diaspora and to seek the common threads that weave our stories together.' Bill Cosby, 77, remains a recognizable cultural icon best known for creating and starring in 'The Cosby Show' (1984–1992), which portrayed a successful Black family on television — a groundbreaking moment in American media. He is currently in discussions with NBC regarding a potential new sitcom. (Note: Cosby was convicted in 2018 of aggravated indecent assault; the conviction was overturned in 2021 on procedural grounds.)

Met die titel 'Conversations: Afrikaanse en Afrika-Amerikaanse Kunstwerke in Dialoog' sal die uitstalling op 9 November 2015 begin en tot vroeg in 2016 loop. Dit sal werke uit die Cosbys se versameling langs stukke uit die museum se eie Afrika-kunssameling plaas, en gedeelde temas soos geskiedenis, identiteit, kreatiwiteit en mag ondersoek. Die versameling — wat meer as 300 skilderye, drukke, beeldhouwerke en tekeninge omvat — bevat belangrike figure in Afrika-Amerikaanse kuns, insluitend Beauford Delaney, Faith Ringgold, Jacob Lawrence, Augusta Savage en Henry Ossawa Tanner. Baie van hierdie werke is nog nooit openbaar vertoon nie, behalwe een. Hoogtepunte sluit in Henry Ossawa Tanners bekende olieverfskildery 'The Thankful Poor', Gerard Sekoto se 'Boy and the Candle', en seldsame 18de- en vroeë 19de-eeuse portrette deur die Baltimore-kunstenaar Joshua Johnston, sowel as familie-dekens wat oor generasies oorgedra is. In ‘n geskrewe verklaring het Bill Cosby die belangrikheid van sigbaarheid vir kunstenaars wat lank onderdruk is, benadruk: 'Dit is ‘n manier vir mense om te sien wat bestaan en om ‘n stem te gee aan baie van hierdie kunstenaars wat so lank stilgehou is, sommige van wie nie weer sal praat nie.' Die uitstalling vier die museum se 50ste verjaardag. article_content: MOSCOW — Russian President Vladimir Putin told a senior Chinese military official on Wednesday that Moscow and Beijing should expand their cooperation on military satellites and other emerging defense technologies — a statement signaling increasingly close defense ties between the two allies. Putin made the remarks during televised comments at the outset of his meeting with General Zhang Youxia, China’s second-highest-ranking military official and vice chairman of the Central Military Commission. The Russian leader emphasized the importance of deepening military collaboration, noting that high-tech domains now take priority. 'I mean space, including high-orbit assets, and new prospective types of weapons that will ensure the strategic security of both Russia and the People’s Republic of China,' Putin said, without elaborating. He stressed that while 'Russia and China aren’t building any military alliances based on Cold War patterns,' their cooperation is a 'serious factor in stabilizing the international situation.' Putin has previously indicated that Russia has shared highly sensitive military technologies with China, significantly bolstering its defense capabilities. In October 2019, he confirmed that Russia was assisting China in developing an early warning system to detect ballistic missile launches — a system relying on ground-based radar and satellites that only Russia and the United States previously possessed. Beijing declared last year that it shares a 'no-limits' friendship with Russia. China has denounced Western sanctions against Moscow and accused NATO and the United States of provoking Russia’s military action in Ukraine, even as it claims neutrality in the conflict. In return, Russia has consistently voiced support for Beijing on issues concerning Taiwan. Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping have forged strong personal bonds to strengthen their 'strategic partnership' as both confront escalating tensions with the West. Xi visited Moscow in March to further solidify ties, and Putin traveled to Beijing last month for a summit of China’s Belt and Road Initiative. Putin asked Zhang to convey his gratitude to Xi for a warm welcome, noting their 'very friendly personal ties' contribute to the development of Russia-China relations. Over recent years, Russia and China have conducted multiple joint military exercises, including naval drills and long-range bomber patrols over the Sea of Japan and the East China Sea. Ground forces from both nations have also deployed to each other’s territories for joint training. Speaking to Zhang, Putin criticized NATO’s efforts to expand its reach into the Asia-Pacific region, calling it 'an attempt to go beyond its geographic sphere of influence.' 'The U.S. has increasingly drawn alliance members into inciting tensions in the Asia-Pacific region and sought to create new military-political alliances, including regional countries, based on its own self-interest,' he said. He added that Russia and China are responding in a 'calm and balanced way' and strengthening their security through joint air force and navy drills. Zhang praised Moscow for resisting Western pressure, stating, 'The Russian Federation under your leadership is standing firm in the face of Western sanctions, demonstrating that you and Russia will not be bent by any difficulties.' He added, 'The Chinese side expresses its respect for you for this.' Earlier in the day, speaking with Russian Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu, Zhang said Russia-China relations are 'at the highest level in the new era,' and that the two countries 'consistently support each other on issues of fundamental interest and core concerns.' He described the relationship as a 'model of strategic trust and mutually beneficial cooperation' and stated his visit aims to further enhance military collaboration. Shoigu asserted that defense ties between Russia and China are not directed at any third country. 'Unlike certain aggressive Western countries, we are not forming a military bloc,' he said, adding that mutual cooperation 'sets an example of strategic interaction based on trust and respect.' 'We conduct regular operational and combat exercises on land, in the air, and at sea, and successfully carry out complex combat training missions side by side,' Shoigu said. 'All these actions serve no third party and are undertaken solely in our mutual interests.' He invited Zhang to discuss further steps to expand cooperation in defense and international affairs.
translated_content: MOSKOU — Russiese president Vladimir Poet het op woensdag ‘n hoë-rang Chinese militêre beampte gesê dat Moskou en Peking hul samewerking op militêre satelliete en ander opkomende verdedigingstegnologieë moet uitbrei — ‘n stelling wat toenemend noue verdedigingsbande tussen die bondgenote aandui. Poet het hierdie opmerkings gemaak tydens ‘n televisie-uitgesending by die begin van sy ontmoeting met Generaal Zhang Youxia, China se tweede hoogste rang militêre beampte en adjunkvoorsitter van die Sentrale Militêre Kommissie. Die Russiese leier het die belangrikheid van die verdieping van militêre samewerking beklemtoon en opgemerk dat hoë-tegnologie-domeine nou voorrang geniet. 'Ek bedoel ruimte, insluitend hoë-baan bates, en nuwe potensiële tipes wapens wat die strategiese sekuriteit van beide Rusland en die Volksrepubliek China sal verseker,' het Poet gesê sonder verdere verduideliking. Hy het beklemtoon dat hoewel 'Rusland en China geen militêre alliansies op grond van Koude-Oorlogpatrone bou nie,' hul samewerking '‘n ernstige faktor is in die stabilisering van die internasionale situasie.' Poet het vroeër aangedui dat Rusland hoog-sensitiwe militêre tegnologieë met China gedeel het wat die ontwikkeling van haar verdedigingsvermoë aansienlik versterk het. In Oktober 2019 het hy bevestig dat Rusland China help om ‘n vroegtijdige waarskuwingstelsel te ontwikkel om ballistiese rakketlanserings op te spoor — ‘n stelsel wat grondgebaseerde radars en satelliete gebruik wat voorheen slegs deur Rusland en die Verenigde State besit is. Peking het vorige jaar verklaar dat dit ‘n 'geen-limiete' vriendskap met Rusland deel. China het Westerse sanksies teen Moskou veroordeel en NATO en die Verenigde State beskuldig van die provocering van Rusland se militêre aksie in Oekraïne, selfs al beweer dit neutraliteit in die konflikt. In ruil het Rusland aanhoudend ondersteuning vir Peking oor sake wat Taiwan betref, uitgespreek. Poet en die Chinese president Xi Jinping het sterk persoonlike bande gevorm om hul 'strategiese partnerskap' te versterk terwyl hulle albei toenemende spanninge met die Weste ervaar. Xi het in Maart na Moskou besoek om bande te verstevig, en Poet het vorige maand na Peking gereis vir ‘n topontmoeting van China se Belt and Road-initiatief. Poet het Zhang gevra om sy dankie aan Xi te oordra vir ‘n warm ontvangs, en opgemerk dat hul 'baie vriendelike persoonlike bande' bydra tot die ontwikkeling van Rusland-China-verhoudings. Gedurende die laaste jare het Rusland en China verskeie gesamentlike oorlogsoefeninge gehou, insluitend maritieme oefeninge en langafstand-bomwerperpatrollings oor die See van Japan en die Oos-Chinese See. Grondmagte van beide nasies het ook na mekaar se grondgebiede gestuur vir gesamentlike opleiding. Tydens sy gesprek met Zhang het Poet kritiek geuit op NATO se pogings om sy bereik na die Asië-Pasifiese gebied uit te brei, en dit beskryf as '‘n poging om buite sy geografiese invloedsfeer te gaan.' 'Die VSA het al hoe meer allianselede getrek om spanninge in die Asië-Pasifiese gebied te verhoog en nuwe militêr-politieke alliansies probeer skep, insluitend lande van die gebied, op grond van hul eie selfisiese belange,' het hy gesê. Hy het bygevoeg dat Rusland en China op ‘n 'kalm en gebalanseerde wyse' reageer en hul sekuriteit versterk deur gesamentlike lug- en see-oefeninge. Zhang het Moskou geprys vir die weerstand teen Westerse druk, en gesê: 'Die Russiese Federasie onder u leierskap staan stevig op teen Westerse sanksies, en toon dat u en Rusland nie deur enige moeilikhede gebuig sal word nie.' Hy het bygevoeg: 'Die Chinese kant uitdruk sy respek vir u hiervoor.' Vroeër op die dag, tydens ‘n ontmoeting met Russiese verdedigingsminister Sergei Shoigu, het Zhang gesê dat die verhoudings tussen Rusland en China 'op die hoogste vlak in die nuwe era' is, en dat die twee lande 'onveranderlik mekaar ondersteun op vraagstukke van fundamentele belang en kernakepte.' Hy het die verhouding beskryf as '‘n model van strategiese vertroue en wederkerige voordeelbringende samewerking' en opgemerk dat sy besoek bedoel is om militêre samewerking verder te verhoog. Shoigu het verklaar dat verdedigingstipes tussen Rusland en China nie op derde lande gerig is nie. 'In teenstelling met sekere aggressiewe Westerse lande, vorm ons nie ‘n militêre blok nie,' het hy gesê, en bygevoeg dat wederkerige bande '‘n voorbeeld van strategiese interaksie op grond van vertroue en respek stel.' 'Ons voer gereelde operasionele en vegt-oefeninge uit op land, in die lug en op die see, en suksesvolle komplekse vegtopleidings op verskillende vlakke saam uit,' het Shoigu gesê. 'Al hierdie aksies is nie op derde lande gerig nie en word uitsluitlik in ons wederkerige belange gedoen.' Hy het Zhang uitgenooi om oor verdere stappe na samewerking op die verdedigings- en internasionale gebied te bespreek.

article_content: In a wild Copa Libertadores clash, Montevideo Wanderers edged out Venezuelan side Zamora 3–2 in a match packed with drama, red cards, and a goal that will live on in highlight reels. Arles Flores lit up the stadium with a breathtaking 35-yard rocket that flew past goalkeeper Leandro Burian, putting Zamora ahead 2–1. But what truly stole the show wasn’t just the strike—it was the joyous 'bowling-ball strike' celebration that followed, with Flores and his teammates mimicking a bowler’s motion in pure delight. The game was far from smooth sailing. Zamora went down to 10 men just 20 minutes in after Ángel Faria was sent off. Jhon Murillo then capitalized on the chaos to give Zamora the lead, but Montevideo responded quickly—though not with a goal. Instead, they reduced themselves to 10 men too, as Adrian Colombino received a red card. Gastón Rodríguez equalized before halftime with a crisp finish inside the box. After the break, Flores delivered the match’s defining moment: picking up the ball near midfield, he surged forward and unleashed a curling shot into the top corner. His celebration, a playful nod to bowling alley culture, became an instant viral sensation. Zamora nearly doubled their lead when Murillo chipped the keeper—only for the ball to smack off the crossbar. That miss proved costly. Montevideo equalized from the penalty spot after Luis Ovalle fouled Nicolas Albarracín, earning himself a second yellow. Substitute Leandro Reymundez then headed home the winner in the 82nd minute. As if the drama wasn’t enough, injury time brought two more red cards: Murillo and Montevideo’s Juan Mascia were both dismissed, leaving just nine players on the pitch for Zamora and eight for Montevideo. The final whistle blew amid stunned silence and roaring cheers—a match remembered not just for its scoreline, but for its sheer unpredictability.

Arles Flores het die stadion verlig met 'n asemrowende 35-meter-rocket wat verby doelwaakhouder Leandro Burian gevaar het en Zamora 2–1 voor gestel. Maar wat werklik die aandag gevat het, was nie net die doel nie—dit was die vrolike 'bowling-ball strike'-viering wat gevolg het, waar Flores en sy spanmaats 'n bowler se beweging nageboot het in suiwer vreugde. Die wedstryd was ver van glad. Zamora het na net 20 minute na 10 mense gegaan toe Ángel Faria uitgestuur is. Jhon Murillo het dan die chaos benut om Zamora die lei te gee, maar Montevideo het gou gereageer—hoewel nie met 'n doel nie. In plaas daarvan het hulle hulself ook tot 10 mense verminder toe Adrian Colombino 'n rooi kaart gekry het. Gastón Rodríguez het voor die halftyd met 'n skerp skiet binne die strafplek gelykgemaak. Ná die halftyd het Flores die wedstryd se definierende oomblik gelewer: hy het die bal naby die middelyn opgepik, vooruit gebewe en 'n boogskoot in die boonste hoek geskiet. Sy viering, 'n speelse verwysing na klokkenspel-kultuur, is onmiddellik 'n viral-sensasie geword. Zamora het byna hul voorsprong verdubbel toe Murillo die doelwaakhouder gechip het—net om die bal teen die dwarsbalk te tref. Dié mislukking het hulle gekoste. Montevideo het gelykgemaak vanaf die strafskop nadat Luis Ovalle Nicolas Albarracín geskop het, wat homself 'n tweede geel kaart opgelê het. Substituut Leandro Reymundez het daarna 'n kopbal doel in die 82ste minuut gemaak. Asof die drama nie genoeg was nie, het die byeertyd nog twee rooi kaarte gebring: Murillo en Montevideo se Juan Mascia is beide uitgestuur, wat agt spelers op die veld vir Montevideo en nege vir Zamora agtergelaat het. Die whisle het geblaas onder versteende stilte en juigende gejuig—'n wedstryd wat onthou sal word nie net vir die teller nie, maar vir sy suiwer onvoorspelbaarheid.

article_content: SEOUL, South Korea (CNN) — She has determination — but perhaps not the luck. A 68-year-old South Korean woman, known only as Cha, has now attempted to pass her driver’s license exam 771 times — and still hasn’t succeeded. Her journey began in April 2005, when she first took the written test to help with her door-to-door sales business, according to Choi Young-cheol of the Jeonju Driver’s License Agency. She failed that day. Then she tried again the next day. And the day after that. And so it went — every day, at first. Today, though she no longer works, Cha still visits the licensing office once a week. According to agency estimates, she has spent more than 4 million won — roughly $2,888 — on exam fees. As Kim Rahn of the Korea Times notes, candidates must score at least 60 out of 100 to pass the written test. Cha typically scores under 50. Her most recent attempt was on Monday. She plans to try again for the 772nd time either Thursday or Friday.

Haar reis het begin in April 2005, toe sy die geskrewe toets eerste geneem het om haar deur-deur-verkope te ondersteun, volgens Choi Young-cheol van die Jeonju-bestuurderlike Lisensieagentskap. Sy het daardie dag misluk. Toe het sy weer probeer die volgende dag. En die dag daarna. En so het dit gegaan — elke dag, eers. Vandag, alhoewel sy nie meer werk nie, besoek Cha steeds die lisensiekantoor een keer per week. Volgens agentskapberamings het sy meer as 4 miljoen won — ongeveer $2 888 — op toetskoste bestee. Soos Kim Rahn van die Korea Times opmerk, moet kandidate ten minste 60 uit 100 punte behaal om die geskrewe toets te slaag. Cha skoring gewoonlik onder 50. Haar mees onlangse poging was op Maandag. Sy plan om vir die 772de keer te probeer, is op Donderdag of Vrydag.
