article_content: More than 1,200 NASA employees will be laid off this Friday, even though Congress approved a $19 billion budget for the agency just two days prior. Lori Garver, NASA’s deputy administrator, stated Thursday that the new funding would not prevent the planned layoffs — 'certainly not for tomorrow.' Thursday marked the final day for affected workers to report to their stations, where many received their final paperwork. A significant number of those leaving have dedicated their careers to the Space Shuttle program since its inception in the early 1980s. Late Wednesday, the House passed the NASA Reauthorization Act after the Senate had approved it, granting NASA the authority to implement President Barack Obama’s long-term space strategy. The bill passed with strong bipartisan support, and President Obama signed it into law on October 11, 2010. While the exact funding allocations for individual programs won’t be finalized until after the November elections, the legislation authorized one additional shuttle mission, pushing the program’s official retirement from February 2011 to June 2011. This final flight, STS-135, aimed to deliver critical supplies to the International Space Station (ISS). Additionally, the bill extended the ISS’s operational life through 2020. As the shuttle program winds down, more than 9,000 jobs across NASA and its contractors are projected to be lost.

Terwyl die ruimteveerprogram afgelop word, word meer as 9 000 werksgeleenthede oor NASA en sy kontrakteurs geraam as verlore.

article_content: Criminal past: Declan Rooney, as he emerged smirking from court in 1993. The Mail on Sunday can today unmask an anonymous sperm donor who claims that an astonishing 32 women are expecting his babies and another 15 are about to take pregnancy tests after requesting donations. Declan Rooney, 42, describes himself as 'Britain’s most successful sperm donor' and says he has donated sperm to two additional women who have since given birth. He also has six children born naturally to three different mothers — meaning he could be the biological father of up to 55 children. The former web designer operates under the online alias 'Upton North', advertising his services on Facebook to single women, lesbians, and couples seeking to conceive. Last night, experts called for an investigation into his unregulated and potentially dangerous practices. One sociologist accused him of 'determinedly engineering a one-man eugenics movement'. Medical experts warn that Rooney is flouting official guidelines, which limit licensed sperm donors to helping a maximum of 10 families. Children conceived through his donations may grow up near each other, risking unintentional genetic relationships. The unregulated world of online sperm donation has drawn increased scrutiny as the internet enables anonymous, low-cost conception outside licensed clinics — bypassing mandatory health screenings and legal safeguards. A private artificial insemination cycle typically costs £850 and is restricted on the NHS to eligible patients. Rooney began offering his services last March, visiting women within a 50-mile radius of his Middlesbrough home to provide sperm in a specimen container for self-insemination. His website — taken down after contact by The Mail on Sunday — stated: 'I am willing to help either through artificial insemination or naturally, with no strings attached.' He insists he does not have sex with recipients. While private sperm donation is not illegal unless payment is made, risks include coercion, abuse, and financial exploitation. Rooney claims he only charges for expenses and acts out of altruism: 'I like helping people. Have you changed anyone’s life for the better?' Since becoming a donor, he says two lesbian women in the North East have given birth to his children. 'When I was told, I was really happy for the mothers,' he said. 'I like meeting new people, hearing their stories, problem-solving. I’m quite altruistic.' On his site, Rooney posted ultrasound images, testimonials, and a photo of a specimen pot to support his claims. A spokesperson for the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority (HFEA) warned: 'Women finding a sperm donor online — rather than through a licensed clinic — face serious risks. The donor isn't screened for infectious diseases like HIV or inherited conditions, and he may legally be the child’s parent.' Dr. Suvir Venkataraman of Harley Street Fertility Clinic added: 'Licensed clinics track all children born from a single donor to prevent accidental consanguinity. This man cannot monitor every child he fathers — that’s a huge risk.' Rooney claims his family has no recorded medical issues across five generations. 'I wouldn’t donate if I had a genetic disorder,' he said. He also dismissed concerns about siblings meeting, claiming: 'There is no scientific evidence that evolution prevents attraction between genetically similar individuals — this belief is unfounded.' He further stated he believes he is 'immune' to the Child Support Agency: 'They’d struggle to trace my income,' he said — though in reality, the Child Maintenance Service can access bank records, tax filings, and employment data to enforce payments. Rooney was photographed on the front page of the Daily Mail in 1993 after being convicted of causing £60,000 in graffiti damage. He received a suspended sentence and served seven months in a young offenders’ institution. At the time, he said: 'My barrister’s a genius. I’m laughing. It’s a soft touch.' When questioned about his past, he admitted: 'I don’t mention it to recipients, but if it comes up, I’ll talk about it.' Sociologist Claire McQuoid, who researches private sperm donation and is founding a charity for abused women, said: 'When Upton North appeared, he built a reputation for aggressively impregnating as many women as possible, with no regard for child welfare or the women themselves. His online marketing resembles a eugenics mission.'

Sy webwerf — wat afgehaal is ná kontak met die Mail on Sunday — het gestel: 'Ek is bereid om te help deur kunsmatige inseminasie of natuurlik, sonder enige voorwaardes.' Hierdie man kan nie elke kind wat hy gevestig het volg nie — dit is ’n groot risiko.' Rooney beweer dat sy familie geen mediese probleme in vyf generasies gehad het nie. Hy het ook beweer dat hy 'immun' is teen die Child Support Agency: 'Hulle sal moeilikheid hê om my inkomste op te spoor,' het hy gesê — hoewel die Child Maintenance Service in werklikheid bankrekeninge, belastingopnames en werksdata kan gebruik om betalinge af te dwing. Rooney is op die voorblad van die Daily Mail in 1993 gefotografeer toe hy skuldig bevind is vir die aanrichting van £60 000 in graffitiskade. Hy het ’n gesuspendede vonnis ontvang en sewe maande in ’n jongmisdadigersinrigting gesit. Toe hy daardie tyd gesê het: 'My prokureur is ’n genie. Ek lag. Dit is ’n sagte tref.' Toe hy na sy verlede gevra is, het hy erken: 'Ek noem dit nie aan ontvangers nie, maar as dit opkom, sal ek daaroor praat.' article_content: In a touching display of community kindness, an anonymous benefactor has gifted £24,000 to 88-year-old D-Day veteran Gordon Fowle and his wife Betty, enabling them to restore their crumbling Cornish cottage. After a section of their home’s exterior wall collapsed during harsh winter conditions in January, the couple — who’ve lived in the property for four decades — were forced to relocate temporarily, unsure if they could ever afford repairs. Their insurer, Prudential, declined coverage, arguing the damage resulted from prolonged exposure to moisture and frost, not a sudden incident covered under their £500 annual policy. Undeterred, a mysterious donor from their village stepped forward with the full sum needed to rebuild, allowing construction to begin almost immediately. Local builder Mark Williams helped keep costs manageable, reducing the total from an estimated £30,000. Gordon, who was a teenager during the Normandy landings, called the gesture 'unbelievable,' saying it lifted a heavy burden from their hearts. Betty echoed his gratitude, describing the donation as 'overwhelming' and 'wonderful.' James Flynn, the couple’s grandson-in-law and a local locksmith, contrasted the donor’s compassion with the insurer’s rigid stance, noting the act had 'shamed' the company. While Prudential maintains its position aligns with standard policy exclusions for aging infrastructure, neighbors and friends have rallied around the Fowles, celebrating a quiet triumph of humanity over bureaucracy.

article_content: A catering company makes a staggering 500-mile round trip every day during the school year to deliver lunches to pupils, it has been revealed. Meals for more than 100 schools in Dorset are prepared 230 miles away in Nottingham before being transported in refrigerated lorries across the country—a journey that takes up to four hours. Parents have called the trip 'ludicrous,' as the vehicles cover approximately 2,300 miles per week transporting food (based on 230 miles one way × 2 × 5 school days). Each round trip costs at least £80 in fuel, according to estimates. The company, Cygnet Catering, supplies 118 schools in Dorset with 5,140 meals per day at a cost of up to £2.02 per lunch, which it says includes fuel and transportation. It costs an average small car more than £80 in petrol to complete one return journey between Nottingham and Dorset. Over five school days, this amounts to more than £400—or £12,000 per school year. In a large refrigerated lorry, the cost is likely significantly higher. Parent groups have raised concerns about food freshness upon arrival and the carbon emissions from such long-distance transport. Margaret Morrissey, spokesperson for the campaign group Parents Outloud, said: 'It takes at least four hours to complete this journey—that’s a long way for food to travel. It just seems ludicrous when there are Dorset-based companies capable of preparing excellent, locally sourced, home-cooked meals.' The meals, provided by Cygnet Catering, include lasagne, fish fingers, southern fried chicken pizza, and sausage and mash. Dorset County Council signed a £1.2 million annual contract with Cygnet Catering, based in Beeston, Nottingham, in 2007, citing it as a 'value for money' service. Meals are prepared on-site in Nottingham, chilled, and reheated at schools in areas including Weymouth, Portland, Poole, and Bournemouth. Some schools have opted out of the service and pay an additional eight pence per meal to source and cook meals locally. One such school is Holy Trinity, a Church of England primary school in Weymouth, which sources meals from a nearby college at a cost of £2.10 each. Helen Toft, a governor at Holy Trinity, said: 'For some children, the meal they get at lunchtime is the best they will eat all day. That is a sad fact—and makes it our responsibility to ensure they receive the best possible food, which means fresh, local ingredients.' Toni Coombs, cabinet member for education at Dorset County Council, said: 'To provide a value-for-money service, we used a formal tendering process. Cygnet Catering was awarded the contract in 2007 because there was insufficient local capacity. We did have reservations about the distance, but Local Food Links, a Bridport-based supplier, already provides meals to several schools.' Mrs. Coombs added that the Cygnet contract expires next July, and the council intends to seek a more local supplier. A spokesperson for Cygnet Catering said: 'We have an expert team that ensures our distribution network is as efficient as possible, helping us reduce road miles and deliver high-quality meals to schools across the country.'

article_content: At that moment, Joe Cocker looked less like a rock star and more like a stranger who had accidentally wandered onto the stage from the sea of young, untamed souls swaying beneath the Woodstock sky. Disheveled and utterly unglamorous, he seemed out of place among the glittering icons of rock ‘n’ roll gathered in upstate New York 45 summers ago. But then he began to sing. The song was 'With a Little Help From My Friends' — a lighthearted tune from the Beatles’ landmark album 'Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band.' A melody so simple, so inviting, that even your grandparents could hum it. Yet Cocker didn’t just sing it — he unraveled it. With every gasp, every tremor of his body, he tore its cheerful fabric apart and stitched it back together as something wilder, deeper, more elemental — a soul-stirring epic that no one had ever imagined possible. Cameras lingered on him, tracking the violent grace of his movements: fingers clawing the air like he was pulling notes from thin air, voice a gritty, howling force that turned a pop song into a hymn. For three minutes, he didn’t perform — he transfigured. That moment, immortalized in the 'Woodstock' documentary, became the defining image of his career. When news broke of his death at 70 from lung cancer, it was that performance — not his chart-toppers — that first came to mind. CBS Evening News opened their tribute with it. Social media overflowed with clips of his trembling, triumphant cry. But Cocker’s story didn’t end at Woodstock. He built a lasting legacy with blues-rock anthems like 'Feelin’ Alright' and 'You Are So Beautiful,' and cemented his place in history with the 1982 duet 'Up Where We Belong' — a Grammy-winning ballad that still echoes in romances and commercials alike. His voice, thick with emotion and grit, remained sought-after across generations. And fittingly, in a quiet, perfect full circle, Ringo Starr — the very man who originally sang the song that changed everything — sent a single, tender tweet: 'Rest in peace, Joe. Peace and love.'

Vrede en liefde.'

article_content: New York (CNN) — You’ve tried social media marketing, but so far, it’s brought more headaches than sales. How can Twitter help you sell ice cream? How will Facebook fill seats at your restaurant or boost sales of your handmade clothes? Small business owners and professionals have voiced this frustration countless times: 'How do I actually make money from social media?' Mitch Goldstone has run a photo-developing shop in Irvine, California, since 1990. Back then, he processed 24-exposure film cartridges. Today, he scans the dusty shoeboxes of photos under your bed—turning analog memories into digital assets. His website, ScanMyPhoto.com, boasts 10,600 Twitter followers and over 32,000 tweets. But Goldstone doesn’t just promote himself. He joins conversations about photography, shares useful links, and offers thoughtful reviews. His authentic presence has turned his local shop into a global service, scanning photos from across the street to across the ocean—in Australia, Europe, and beyond. 'If you’re not on social media,' Goldstone says, 'you’re going to be out of business. Let me repeat that: You will be out of business if you don’t tweet, use Facebook, and engage on social media today.' Ido Leffler, co-founder of the natural beauty brand 'Yes To...', faced a similar challenge. After a costly traditional ad campaign flopped, he turned to social media to find the face of his brand. The result? 150,000 Facebook fans—and sales doubled within six months. 'Social media is an equalizer,' Leffler says. 'You don’t need a big budget. Setting up a Facebook page or Twitter account costs nothing.' Here’s what top performers do—and what to avoid: - Don’t say, 'It takes too much time and doesn’t help sales.' That mindset is dangerous. An online presence isn’t optional—it’s as essential as a phone number. Customers expect it. - Listen. Pay attention to what people are saying about your business online. Respond personally when you can. Positive word-of-mouth grows your brand. Negative feedback? Use it to improve. - Be nimble. In California, food trucks tweet their daily locations. In New York, during a brutal snowstorm in February 2010, the Broadway show 'Mamma Mia!' offered discounted tickets to those brave enough to walk through the snow—and filled the house. - Watch your competitors. See how others in your industry are succeeding—and adapt those ideas. - Think of a tweet as a 'tap on the shoulder.' It’s not just advertising; it’s connection. - Share value. Discounts work, but so do helpful tips, funny links, and genuine insights. - Stay authentic. 'Be yourself,' says Mike Hofman, deputy editor at Inc. Magazine. 'Corporate jargon won’t cut it. People want personality, wit, and brevity.' - Assign responsibility. Designate someone in your team to manage your social voice—but don’t hand it off to an intern and walk away. 'Do you really want your intern deciding how your brand speaks to the world?' Hofman warns.

Stryngente, korporatiewe taal sal jou nie ver bring nie. Mense wat op sosiale media reageer, beweeg vinnig, is slim en wil slim en beknopte inhoud. Neem dit ernstig. article_content: While the surge of unaccompanied migrant children crossing into Texas has sparked a national debate over humanitarian responsibility, Governor Rick Perry has redirected attention toward what he calls the ‘real’ threat: criminals and terrorists entering through the southern border. In interviews on CNN and NBC, Perry dismissed the influx of children — numbering over 62,000 in 2014 — as a ‘side issue,’ insisting instead that illegal border crossings by violent offenders pose the greatest danger to public safety. He claimed that since 2008, undocumented criminals have committed 3,000 homicides and nearly 8,000 sexual assaults — figures later thoroughly discredited by PolitiFact Texas as baseless and misleading. Despite this, Perry continues to stand by the numbers, using them to justify deploying up to 1,000 Texas National Guard troops to the border. His stance contrasts sharply with the broader context: overall undocumented immigration has dropped to its lowest level since the early 1980s, while child arrivals have more than doubled compared to the previous year. Republican political analysts are divided on his motives. Some, like Ana Navarro, admit they can’t follow his logic, while others, such as Leslie Sanchez, argue he’s addressing one legitimate piece of a complex problem. Perry also invoked post-9/11 fears by suggesting terrorists exploit the border, a point echoed by Rep. Mike Rogers of the House Intelligence Committee. Yet just weeks earlier, Perry had urged Congress to collaborate with President Obama on managing the child crisis, signaling a notable shift in tone. Public opinion reflects similar contradictions: a majority want stricter controls on immigration, yet nearly half support spending billions to care for the children — even as a majority also back faster deportations. With Perry eyeing a 2016 presidential run, his messaging appears carefully calibrated to align with GOP base concerns, sidestepping the humanitarian dimensions of the crisis in favor of a security-focused narrative.

In onderhoude op CNN en NBC het Perry die toestroming van kinders — wat meer as 62 000 in 2014 was — as 'n 'kantkwestie' afgedaan en eerder aangedui dat onwettige grensoorgange deur gewelddadige oortreders die grootste gevaar vir openbare veiligheid vorm. Ondanks hierdie ontkenning, hou Perry vas aan hierdie syfers en gebruik hulle om die uitsending van tot 1 000 Texas Nasionale Wagtroepe na die grens te regverdig. Sy standpunt staan skerp teenoor die breër konteks: die totale aantal onwettige immigrante het tot sy laagste vlak sedert die vroeë 1980's daal, terwyl kinderaankomste meer as verdubbel het in vergelyking met die voorafgaande jaar. Republikeinse politieke analiste is verdeel oor sy motiewe. Sommige, soos Ana Navarro, gee toe dat hulle sy denke nie kan volg nie, terwyl ander, soos Leslie Sanchez, beweer dat hy een legitieme aspek van 'n komplekse probleem aanspreek. Perry het ook die kommer na 9/11 aangespreek deur te suggereer dat terreuriste die grens uitbuit, 'n punt wat deur Rep. Mike Rogers van die Huisgeheime Veiligheidskomitee bevestig is. Maar net weke tevore het Perry die Kongres nog aangemoedig om saam te werk met President Obama om die kinderkrisis te hanteer, wat 'n merkbare verskuiwing in toon aandui. Openbare opinie reflekteer soortgelyke teenstellinge: 'n meerderheid wil strengere beperkings op immigrasie, maar byna die helfte ondersteun miljarddollar se uitgawes om kinders te versorg — selfs al ondersteun 'n meerderheid ook sneller deportasies. Met Perry wat op 'n 2016-presidensiële kandidatuur kyk, lyk sy boodskap bewus geskik om met die GOP-basis se bekommernisse in lyn te wees, en vermy die menslike dimensie van die krisis in gunste van 'n veiligheidsgebaseerde narratief.

article_content: England’s spirits may need a boost in the coming months as they head into a World Cup where expectations are low. Captain Alastair Cook is likely searching for a morale-lifting moment—and he may have found it in Joe Root’s unexpected hobby: the ukulele. Before England’s fifth one-day international against Sri Lanka on Wednesday, Root—quietly showcasing his hidden talent—was filmed by the ECB strumming along to Arctic Monkeys’ 'Mardy Bum' in his hotel room. The 23-year-old Yorkshireman admits his skills are 'horrendous' and refuses to sing while playing. 'I can’t really sing,' he said, 'so I play loud enough so no one can hear that. It sounds awful right now—but I hope, one day, it’ll sound alright.' The song choice is fitting: Arctic Monkeys hail from Sheffield, Root’s hometown. While Cook might encourage him to pick something more uplifting for the team, Root remains modest about his abilities. But when it comes to cricket, Root is far more confident. England trails 3-1 in the seven-match series, yet he believes there’s still time to turn things around. 'There’s no reason why we can’t,' he said. 'We’ve shown glimpses of what we’re capable of in every game. Now we just need one complete performance.' Even in their sole win, they weren’t at their best—which he sees as encouraging. 'We don’t want to keep talking about being promising. Now is the time to step up. This is the perfect chance to prove ourselves under pressure before the World Cup.'

Voor Engeland se vyfde een-dae-interaksie teen Sri Lanka op Woensdag, is Root—stilweg sy verborge talent aan die wys—deur die ECB gefilm toe hy saam met Arctic Monkeys se 'Mardy Bum' op sy hotelkamer speel. Die 23-jarige Yorkshireman erken dat sy vaardighede 'verskriklik' is en weier om te sing terwyl hy speel. 'Ek kan nie regtig sing nie,' sê hy, 'dus speel ek luid genoeg sodat niemand kan hoor dat ek nie goed is nie. Dit klink tans verskriklik—maar ek hoop dat dit een dag beter sal klink.' Die keuse van die liedjie is gepas: Arctic Monkeys kom uit Sheffield, Root se geboortestad. Hoewel Cook hom dalk kan aandring om iets meer opbeurendes te kies vir die span, bly Root beskeie oor sy vermoëns. Maar wanneer dit om krieket gaan, is Root baie selfversekerder. Engeland is agter met 3-1 in die sewe-wedstrydreeks, maar hy glo dat daar nog tyd is om die situasie te keer. 'Daar is geen rede waarom ons nie kan nie,' sê hy. article_content: CNN — When Iraq War veteran Angela Peacock showers, she sometimes closes her eyes and is transported back to the day in Baghdad in 2003 that brought her to the brink. Sgt. Angela Peacock, seen here in 2004 after returning from Iraq, was assigned to security detail for an Army convoy stuck in heavy traffic when her vehicle pulled alongside a van filled with Iraqi men who began shouting threats: 'We’re going to kill you.' One man stared directly at her. 'I can remember his eyes,' she said. 'I put my finger on the trigger and aimed at him — but my driver screamed at me to stop. I was seconds away from firing — but I didn’t.' Now 30 and back in Missouri, Peacock is unemployed, living rent-free in a friend’s home in North St. Louis County without a lease. She credits the Baghdad incident as a turning point in her battle with drug addiction and post-traumatic stress disorder — PTSD. 'I’m one step away from living on the street,' she said. Shortly after her 2004 discharge, Peacock developed a dependency on pain medication. After her husband left her, she was evicted and spent years couch-surfing between friends and relatives. 'I could be kicked out of this house at any time,' she said. Experts say Peacock’s experience mirrors that of many female veterans returning from Iraq and Afghanistan. The rate of homelessness among female veterans is rising, according to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and advocacy organizations. The VA defines PTSD as an anxiety disorder triggered by traumatic events involving intense fear, helplessness, or horror. 'You’re sitting on your couch, hear a car drive by, and you think it’s coming through your door — you catastrophize automatically,' Peacock explained. 'Normal people don’t do that. But if you’re constantly on convoy duty, you can’t help it.' Those around her 'just don’t get it,' she said, leading to isolation. PTSD often leads to depression, job loss, and homelessness — especially for women who are also caring for children. Compounding the crisis, post-9/11 veterans face higher unemployment than the national average — now at 11.3%, nearly double what it was a year prior, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. A 2005 congressional analysis found that 6.3% of veterans — roughly 1.5 million — lived below the federal poverty line. With women now making up 15% of the U.S. Army and serving increasingly in combat-support roles, female veterans are becoming homeless faster than their male counterparts, said VA spokesperson Pete Dougherty. Conservative estimates place the total number of homeless veterans at 131,000, mostly from the Vietnam era. The VA identifies 3,717 homeless veterans of Iraq and Afghanistan — but the true number could be as high as 7,400. About 10% of homeless veterans are women, meaning approximately 740 Iraq/Afghanistan-era female veterans are currently without stable housing — a number that’s growing. Peacock attributes her PTSD to multiple traumas: near-misses from sniper fire, constant fear of IEDs, and, most devastatingly, being raped by a noncommissioned officer while deployed in South Korea in 2001. On the advice of a superior, she never reported it. 'He told me if I spoke up, they’d put me on trial and paint me as a party girl,' she recalled. Although the Army later reached out to investigate, Peacock declined to participate, believing it would be futile. CNN contacted the Army regarding these allegations but has not yet received an official response. Known as Military Sexual Trauma (MST), such experiences are recognized by advocates as a major contributor to veteran homelessness and PTSD. Some communities are piloting early intervention strategies — identifying veterans at risk of losing housing and offering immediate aid: landlord negotiations, job placement, or emergency funds. Steve Berg, VP of Programs at the National Alliance to End Homelessness, says rapid rehousing — helping veterans transition directly from shelters into stable housing — yields better outcomes than prolonged homelessness. Eric Shinseki, former Army four-star general and current VA Secretary, has pledged to end veteran homelessness within five years. In 2008, VA and HUD allocated $75 million for 10,000 permanent housing vouchers nationwide. Another $75 million was announced in June 2009 for another 10,000 units. 'These are good programs,' Berg said, 'but they lack sufficient capacity.' To house all 131,000 homeless veterans, an estimated $975 million annually would be needed. The Senate is considering legislation cosponsored by Sen. Patty Murray (D-WA) to authorize $50 million over five years for VA special needs grants targeting homeless veterans with children. Peacock, who has no children, has been sober for three years. She’s committed to healing through a 12-step program and weekly therapy with a VA counselor. She also participates in VA vocational rehab — which provided her with a dog she named GI Joe. 'His name was already Joe,' she laughs. 'I just added the GI.' Her goal? Return to college, earn a degree in transpersonal psychology — 'spiritual psychology' — to help others navigate trauma and find meaning. 'It’s about exploring your place in the world,' she said. 'I’m trying to save myself first. Then I can help someone else.' 'I’m getting there,' Peacock said. 'It’s slow… but I’m clean, sober, back in my hometown, and I’ve got a new support system. It’s better. And I’m not done yet.'
translated_content: CNN — Wanneer die Irak-oorlogsveteraan Angela Peacock onder die dousj is, sluit sy soms haar oë en word sy teruggevoer na die dag in Bagdad in 2003 wat haar tot die rand gebring het. Sgt. Angela Peacock, gesien hier in 2004 ná haar terugkeer uit Irak, was toegeken aan sekuriteitsdienste vir ‘n leërkonvooi wat vasgevang was in verkeersophoping toe haar voertuig langs ‘n bakkie vol Irakese mans gekom het wat dreigings geroep het: 'Ons gaan julle doodmaak.' Een man het direk na haar gestaar. 'Ek kan sy oë onthou,' sê sy. 'Ek het my vinger op die trekker geplaas en op hom gerig — maar my bestuurder het geskree om te stop. Ek was sekondes van skiet — maar ek het nie.' Nou 30 en terug in Missouri, is Peacock werkloos en woon gratis by ‘n vriend se huis in Noord-St. Louis County sonder ‘n huurkontrak. Sy skryf die Bagdad-incident toe as ‘n keerpunt in haar stryd teen verslawing en posttraumatiese stressteuring — PTSS. 'Ek is een stap weg van om op die straat te woon,' sê sy. Kort na haar ontslag in 2004 het Peacock ‘n afhanklikheid ontwikkel tot pynmedisyne. Ná haar man haar verlaat het, is sy uit haar appartement verwyder en het sy jare lank tussen vriende en familie op die bank geskuif. 'Ek kan op enige oomblik uit hierdie huis uitgeskop word,' sê sy. Eksperte sê Peacock se ervaring is soortgelyk aan dié van baie vroulike veterane wat terugkeer uit Irak en Afghanistan. Die tempo van vroulike veterane wat dakloos word, neem toe, volgens die Amerikaanse Departement van Veteranewaardes en advokate. Die VA definieer PTSS as ‘n angssteuring wat veroorsaak word deur traumagtige gebeurtenisse wat intensiewe vrees, hulpeloosheid of skrik veroorsaak. 'Jy sit op jou bank, hoor ‘n motor voorbyry en dink dit kom deur jou huis — jy kataliseer dinge outomaties,' sê Peacock. 'Normale mense doen nie so nie. Maar as jy altyd op konvooie is, kan jy dit nie help nie.' Mense in haar lewe 'begryp dit eenvoudig nie,' sê sy, wat lei tot isolasie. PTSS lei dikwels tot depressie, werkverlies en dakloosheid — veral vir vroue wat ook kinders versorg. Die krise word vererger deur die feit dat veterane vanaf 9/11 ‘n hoër werkloosheidsyfer het as die nasionale gemiddelde — tans 11,3%, byna dubbel wat dit ‘n jaar gelede was, volgens die Buro vir Arbeidsstatistiek. ‘n 2005-kongressionele ontleding het bevind dat 6,3% van veterane — ongeveer 1,5 miljoen — onder die federale armoedegrens gewoon het. Met vroue wat nou 15% van die Amerikaanse leër uitmaak en alhoe meer in vegsteunrolle dien, word vroulike veterane vinniger dakloos as hul mansgenote, sê VA-spreker Pete Dougherty. Konservatiewe skattings plaas die totale aantal daklose veterane op 131 000, meeste uit die Viëtnam-oorlogstydperk. Die VA identifiseer 3 717 daklose veterane van Irak en Afghanistan — maar die werklike getal kan so hoog wees as 7 400. Omtrent 10% van daklose veterane is vroue, wat beteken dat ongeveer 740 Irak/Afghanistan-erage vroulike veterane tans sonder stabiele huisvesting is — ‘n getal wat styg. Peacock skryf haar PTSS toe aan verskeie traumas: byna-ontkominge van sniperskote, konstante vrees vir IED’s, en, die mees verwoestende, verkrachting deur ‘n nie-offisier terwyl sy in Suid-Korea gedien het in 2001. Op die raad van ‘n hoër-ranking soldaat het sy dit nooit gerapporteer nie. 'Hy het gesê as ek sê, sal hulle my teregstel en my laat lyk as ‘n partymeisie,' sê sy. Hoewel die leër later uitgekom het om te ondersoek, het Peacock geweier om saam te werk, omdat sy geglo het dit sou niks uitmaak nie. CNN het die leër oor Peacock se bewerings kontak, maar nog geen amptelike respons ontvang nie. Bekend as Militêre Seksuele Trauma (MST), word sulke ervarings deur advokate erken as ‘n groot bydraer tot dakloosheid en PTSS by veterane. Sommige gemeenskappe is besig om vroeë intervensiestrateëgie te ontwikkel — om veterane te identifiseer wat in gevaar is om hul huis te verloor en hulle onmiddellik te help: onderhandeling met huurders, werksplekke of noodfinansiële hulp. Steve Berg, VP van Programme by die Nasionale Alliansie om Dakloosheid te Beëindig, sê dat vinnige herhuisvesting — om veterane direk vanaf skilderye na stabiele huisvesting te bring — beter resultate lewer as langdurige dakloosheid. Eric Shinseki, voormalige leër-vierster-generaal en huidige VA-sekretearis, het beloof om dakloosheid onder veterane binne vyf jaar te beëindig. In 2008 het die VA en HUD $75 miljoen toegewys vir 10 000 permanente huisvestingsvouchers oor die hele land. Nog $75 miljoen is in Junie 2009 aangekondig vir nog 10 000 eenhede. 'Dit is goeie programme,' sê Berg, 'maar hulle het nie genoeg kapasiteit nie.' Om al 131 000 daklose veterane te huisves, sou ‘n geskatte $975 miljoen per jaar nodig wees. Die Senaat beskou ‘n wetgewing wat saamgestel is deur Senator Patty Murray (D-WA) om $50 miljoen oor vyf jaar te stel vir VA-spesiale behoeftesgrante vir daklose veterane met kinders. Peacock, wat geen kinders het nie, is drie jaar lank skoon. Sy is toegewy aan genees deur ‘n 12-stappe-program en wekelikse terapie met ‘n VA-terapeut. Sy neem ook deel aan VA-vocasionele rehabilitasie — wat haar ‘n hond gegee het wat sy GI Joe genoem het. 'Sy naam was reeds Joe,' lag sy. 'Ek het net die GI bygevoeg.' Haar doel? Terugkeer na universiteit, ‘n graad in transpersoonlike sielkunde behaal — 'spirituele sielkunde' — om ander te help om met trauma te navigeer en sin te vind. 'Dis oor jou plek in die wêreld te ontdek,' sê sy. 'Ek probeer eers myself red. Dan kan ek iemand anders help.' 'Ek kry daar,' sê Peacock. 'Dit is stadig… maar ek is skoon, sober, terug in my tuisstad, en ek het ‘n nuwe ondersteuningssirkel. Dit is beter. En ek is nog nie klaar nie.'

article_content: For years, the echidna has captivated observers with its bizarre yet endearing appearance—spiky, round, digger-feet, and a snout that looks like it was carved by a whimsical artist. But now, scientists have uncovered another layer of mystery: these elusive mammals aren’t as quiet as once believed. Researchers at Curtin University in Western Australia have, for the first time ever, recorded the sounds echidnas make in the wild. The audio captures a surprising array of vocalizations: soft coos, low grunts, and odd wheezes—all occurring during the breeding season. Dr. Christine Cooper, who’s spent years observing echidnas in Dryandra National Park, recalls the moment she first heard them: 'We didn’t have a recorder handy, and we just stared at each other like, ‘Did we just hear that?’' The team later returned with handheld mics and a permanently placed camera-mic setup near a cave frequented by echidnas, successfully capturing the sounds. Previously, scientists suspected echidnas made noise, but no concrete evidence existed. Now, the leading theory is that these vocalizations play a role in courtship. The Australian Broadcasting Corporation aptly dubbed them 'the sounds of echidnas flirting.' Whether it’s a mating call, territorial signal, or social bonding cue, one thing is clear: echidnas are far more communicative than anyone imagined. And yes, the recordings do sound oddly charming—like a dove trying to neigh through a kazoo. They’re weird. They’re wonderful. And now, we know they talk.
translated_content: Jare lank het die echidna die aandag getrek met sy vreemde maar aantreklike voorkoms—stekelig, rond, graafpote en ‘n snuit wat lyk of dit deur ‘n whimsiese kunstenaar gesny is. Maar nou het wetenskaplikes ‘n ander laag misterie ontdek: hierdie ontsnapte soogdiere is nie so stil soos een geglo het nie. Navorsers van Curtin Universiteit in Wes-Australië het vir die eerste keer ooit die geluide wat echidnas maak in die wild opgeneem. Die opnames vang ‘n verrassende verskeidenheid vokalisasies: sagte koeie, lae gromme en vreemde wheezes—allemaal tydens die broeiseisoen. Dr. Christine Cooper, wat jare lank echidnas in Dryandra Nasionale Park geobserveer het, herinner aan die oomblik toe sy hulle eers gehoor het: 'Ons het nie ‘n rekordertoestel by ons gehad nie, en ons het net na mekaar gestaar soos: ‘Het ons net daardie gehoor?’' Die span het later teruggekom met draagbare mikrofone en ‘n permanente kamera-mikrofoonstelsel naby ‘n grot wat dikwels deur echidnas besoek word, en het suksesvol die geluide opgeneem. Vroeër het wetenskaplikes vermoed dat echidnas geluide maak, maar daar was geen konkrete bewys nie. Nou is die voorlopige teorie dat hierdie vokalisasies ‘n rol speel in hulle hofmaking. Die Australiese Uitsaaikorporasie het hulle slim as 'die geluide van echidnas wat flirt' genoem. Of dit nou ‘n paarkoers, territoriale sein of sosiale bandvorming is, een ding is duidelik: echidnas is baie meer kommunikatief as iemand ooit gedink het. En ja, die opnames klink wonderlik aantreklik—soos ‘n dove wat probeer skreeu deur ‘n kazo. Hulle is vreemd. Hulle is wonderlik. En nou weet ons hulle praat.

article_content: When the £210 million Hello Kitty theme park opened in Anji, Zhejiang Province, in early 2015, it sparked a media frenzy and high hopes among Chinese fans. But the reality has fallen far short of the hype. Visitors have widely criticized the park as cheesy, boring, and poorly executed. One blogger, Ian Louisell of SmartShanghai.com, called it 'a mess' — citing inconsistent branding, mediocre rides, and what he described as 'some of the most wretched food I’ve encountered in seven years in China.' The park, developed by Sanrio — the Japanese company behind Hello Kitty — and California-based Hettema Group, is located in a scenic but remote area. Access is notoriously difficult: Anji has no direct rail connection, forcing visitors to first reach Huzhou or Hangzhou by high-speed train, then take a bus for over an hour to the Anji County Bus Terminal, followed by a shuttle to the park. One TripAdvisor reviewer, Nehow, described the journey as 'an arduous trek,' warning that international travelers might need to plan a minimum two-night stay just to reach the site. Food inside the park has drawn particular ire. Louisell noted it was worse than train food in China — and five times more expensive. Comments on Chinese platform Livedoor.com echoed these frustrations, labeling the park 'cheesy,' 'boring,' and noting the overpowering smell of fresh paint and 'stupidly high' prices. One anonymous commenter even called it a 'despicable project.' While the Hettema Group’s website describes the park as 'a very special home-away-from-home for Hello Kitty,' nestled in the green hills of Anji and celebrating local nature, the visitor experience tells a different story. Despite the grand opening and massive investment, positive reviews remain scarce — and the dream of a major themed park centered on a Western cartoon character appears to have fizzled before it truly began.

Maar die werklikheid het ver van die ophef afgekom. Besoekers het die park wyd kritiseer as sleg, vervelig en swak uitgevoer. Een blogskrywer, Ian Louisell van SmartShanghai.com, het dit 'n rommel' genoem — met verwysing na onkonsistente merkering, gemiddelde rye, en wat hy beskryf het as 'somme van die mees wreshte kos wat ek in sewe jaar in China ontmoet het.' Die park, ontwikkel deur Sanrio — die Japannese maatskappy agter Hello Kitty — en die Kaliforniese Hettema-groep, is geleë in 'n pragtige maar afgeleë gebied. article_content: Paul and Sandra Dunham, a British couple in their late 50s, were preparing to fly to the United States to face fraud charges tied to their time working for the American company PACE — but instead, they were rushed to hospital after a suspected suicide attempt. Just hours before they were meant to surrender to US marshals at a London police station, emergency services were called to their Northampton home. Officers broke down the door to find the pair unresponsive upstairs. Paul was assisted out of the house; Sandra, pale but awake, was carried out on a stretcher. Both were treated for a suspected drug overdose. Their family and friends believe the looming threat of extradition — and the possibility of spending decades in a US prison — pushed them to despair. The couple, who spent over 25 years with PACE, insist the expenses they claimed were approved by senior management and were entirely legitimate. When leadership changed at the company in 2009 and Eric Siegel returned to the business, tensions rose, leading to their resignation and return to the UK. Years later, Eric Siegel accused them of stealing over $1 million through inflated expense claims — a claim the Dunhams strongly deny. In December 2011, a US grand jury indicted Paul on 13 counts of fraud and money laundering, potentially carrying a 340-year sentence; Sandra faces eight counts with up to 240 years. Despite pleas from their lawyer and public outcry, the UK Home Office has refused to intervene, saying all legal avenues have been used. Their case echoes that of Gary McKinnon, a man with Asperger’s who was spared extradition after massive public pressure. Advocates like Liberty and McKinnon’s mother, Janis Sharp, argue that extradition should be reserved for violent crimes, not corporate disputes. A close friend visiting the couple in hospital said they were emotionally shattered after learning their MP could no longer stop the process. While their condition has since improved, many fear that once cleared medically, they’ll be handed over — and that the UK’s current extradition laws may have already cost them their dignity, if not their lives.

article_content: New security footage from Channel Seven reveals a man believed to be Man Haron Monis walking slowly through Martin Place at 8:30 a.m. on December 15, 2014 — roughly an hour before he entered the Lindt Cafe and took 18 people hostage. The camera, positioned above the square, captured no signs of agitation. Instead, Monis appeared composed, even routine, as if simply passing through. Later that morning, witnesses say Monis sat quietly inside the cafe for up to an hour before pulling out a sawn-off shotgun. One of his former lawyers, who happened to be in the same café, recalled a startlingly normal interaction: Monis greeted him by name, asked how he was doing, and even inquired about pending legal cases. The lawyer, who wished to remain anonymous due to threats against Monis’s legal team, said he didn’t recognize him at first. 'He was cool as a cucumber,' the lawyer told The Australian. 'No scanning the room. No nervous glances. Just… coffee.' This calmness stands in stark contrast to later accounts describing Monis as increasingly volatile during the 17-hour standoff. The discrepancy has fueled debate over whether his behavior was calculated or symptomatic of psychological instability. Monis’s legal history was equally turbulent. Just three days before the siege, his latest appeal to the High Court — challenging the constitutionality of charges related to sending threatening letters to families of deceased soldiers — was summarily dismissed. He had previously lost similar appeals in lower courts. Meanwhile, his personal life was marked by violence and isolation: he was estranged from his two daughters in Iran and locked in a bitter custody battle over his two young sons. In 2013, his ex-wife, Noleen Hayson Pal, was stabbed 18 times and set on fire in the stairwell of his apartment building. Though Monis was never convicted of her murder, he was charged as an accessory; his then-girlfriend, Amirah Droudis, was charged with the actual killing. Adding another layer of eerie coincidence, Monis’s lawyers, Guy Renolds SC and David Hume, shared a building — just two floors below — with Katrina Dawson, one of the two hostages killed in the siege. Their offices were mere steps from the Lindt Cafe. Monis, a man of sharp intellect but extreme views, had spent years navigating Australia’s legal system — filing appeals, writing letters, and pushing boundaries. Yet despite his notoriety, he remained socially engaged, maintaining contact with his legal team right up until the moment he turned a quiet café into a crime scene.

Die kamera, geplaas bo die plein, het geen teken van onrus opgelewer nie. In plaas daarvan het Monis rustig en selfs gewoonlik gelyk, asof hy net deur die plek loop. 'Geen rondkyk nie. Geen nervose blikke nie. Net… koffie.' Hul kantore was net 'n paar stappe van die Lindt-café af. Monis, 'n man van skerp intelligensie maar ekstreme oorsake, het jare lank die Australiese regsisteem deurgeloop — appèle ingedien, briewe geskryf, en grense uitgedaag. Maar ondanks sy berugtheid, het hy sosiaal betrokke gebly, en kontak met sy regspleeg onderhou tot op die oomblik toe hy 'n stil café in 'n misdadige toneel verander het.

article_content: New figures from the Home Office reveal that the 2013-14 football season saw the fewest fan arrests in recorded history. Across all major competitions—including the Premier League, Football League, domestic cups, and European matches—a total of 2,273 supporters were arrested. That’s 183 fewer than the year before, marking a 7% drop, even as more than 38 million fans packed stadiums to watch games live. Manchester United fans accounted for the highest number of arrests at 112, followed by Manchester City (71) and Arsenal (67). At the opposite end, newly relegated Norwich City had just four arrests, while Swansea City and Southampton recorded nine and 14 respectively. Arrests linked to racist or offensive chanting have plummeted by 76% since 2000, with only 21 such cases reported in 2013-14. The Football League emphasized that clubs are investing heavily in safety: over £10 million annually on venue security and another £6 million on police services, although more than half of Football League fixtures now operate without police presence. A spokesperson noted that the sharp decline in incidents over the past decade confirms the effectiveness of current crowd management strategies. With arrests representing less than 0.01% of total attendance—that’s roughly one arrest per 16,800 spectators—the data paints a picture of increasingly safe and well-behaved football environments.

article_content: On the walls of Senator Barbara Mikulski’s Capitol office hang cherished portraits — taken every two years — of every woman serving in the U.S. Senate. The first, from 1988, shows just two: Mikulski, a Democrat from Maryland, and Republican Nancy Kassebaum of Kansas. 'The hemlines were different, the hair colors changed,' Mikulski reflected. 'Back then, there were only two.' Today’s photo includes 17 women — five Republicans and twelve Democrats — more than the total number of women who had ever served in the Senate when Mikulski first took office over thirty years ago. A trailblazer in every sense, Mikulski was the first Democratic woman elected to the Senate in her own right, the first woman in Senate Democratic leadership, and, in 2010, became the longest-serving woman in Senate history. On Saturday, she surpassed Representative Edith Nourse Rogers of Massachusetts — who served from 1925 to 1960 — to become the longest-serving woman in the entire history of the U.S. Congress. To commemorate the milestone, Mikulski invited three fellow female senators — Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Olympia Snowe (R-ME), and Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) — to gather around a dining table from her childhood home. Over wine and conversation, they spoke about what they call their 'zone of civility': a rare, bipartisan space built on trust, not politics. These monthly dinners — strictly off the record — are not about policy. They’re about family, fears, friendships. 'We rarely get nights off,' Gillibrand joked. 'So this is our big night out.' Snowe, who retired in 2013 after growing disillusioned with Congress’s polarization, called the gatherings 'critical' — a chance to 'let our hair down.' Murkowski’s husband, she said, knows the date is non-negotiable: 'It’s when I feel most connected to my purpose.' Mikulski describes the Senate as a 'lonely place.' These dinners, she says, offer 'no agenda, nothing to prove — just common ground.' The bonds formed here have led to real legislative wins. Murkowski credits her personal rapport with former Senator Barbara Boxer for helping resolve differences on the highway bill during their overlapping terms. Gillibrand recalls Snowe and Murkowski offering strategic advice — though not official sponsorship — during her fight to pass the 9/11 first responders health bill. 'We’re natural allies,' Snowe said. 'We trust each other’s counsel.' They attribute their success to fewer egos, deeper listening, and a shared understanding of what it means to be a woman in a historically male institution. 'We’re competitive — we wouldn’t be here otherwise — but we don’t need to claim all the credit,' Murkowski noted. 'It’s not my way or the highway. It’s how we get things done.' While they agree on core women’s issues — from healthcare to workplace equity — Murkowski acknowledged voting against the Affordable Care Act’s contraceptive mandate in 2012, a decision that drew backlash in Alaska. She regrets it. 'I wish we’d talked about it,' she admitted, criticizing her own party’s stance on women’s health. 'Many women feel under attack.' Surrounded by photos of Geraldine Ferraro, Madeleine Albright, and the Girl Scouts, Mikulski’s colleagues credit her with building this sanctuary. Gillibrand remembers Mikulski reaching out when she first arrived: 'She guided me through the system.' After 12,858 days of service, Mikulski’s greatest legacy may not be her record-breaking tenure — but the enduring culture of civility she helped create. 'I won’t always be here,' she said. 'But I hope this spirit remains.'

Die eerste, uit 1988, toon net twee: Mikulski, ’n Demokraat uit Maryland, en die Republikeinse Nancy Kassebaum uit Kansas. 'Die roklyne was anders, die hare se kleur het verander,' het Mikulski nagedink. 'Toe was daar net twee.' Die huidige foto toon 17 vroue — vyf Republikeine en twaalf Demokrate — meer as die totale aantal vroue wat ooit in die Senaat gedien het toe Mikulski vir die eerste keer aangedui is, meer as dertig jaar gelede. 'n Pionier in elke sin, was Mikulski die eerste Demokratiese vrou wat in haar eie reg na die Senaat verkies is, die eerste vrou in die Demokratiese leierskap van die Senaat, en in 2010 het sy die langste dienende vrou in die Senaat geword. Op Saterdag het sy Represe ntante Edith Nourse Rogers van Massachusetts — wat van 1925 tot 1960 gedien het — oortref om die langste dienende vrou in die geskiedenis van die hele Amerikaanse Kongres te word. Om die mijlpaal te vier, het Mikulski drie ander vroulike senatore uitgenodig — Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Olympia Snowe (R-ME) en Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) — om rondom ’n tafel uit haar kinderjare te versamel. Oor wyn en gesprek het hulle oor hul 'sfeer van beskaafdheid' gepraat: ’n seldsame, bipartisane ruimte gebaseer op vertroue, nie politiek nie. Hierdie maandelikse byeenkomste — streng vertroulik — gaan nie oor beleid nie. Hulle gaan oor familie, vrees en vriendskap. 'Ons kry selde nagte vry,' het Gillibrand gejoke. 'Dus is dit ons groot nag uit.' Snowe, wat in 2013 afgetree het na sy ontsteltenis oor die polarisasie in die Kongres, het die byeenkomste 'krities' genoem — ’n kans om 'haar hare los te maak.' Murkowski se man, het sy gesê, weet dat die datum nie onderhandelbaar is nie: 'Dis wanneer ek die meeste verbonden voel met my doel.' Mikulski beskryf die Senaat as 'n eenzaam plek.' Hierdie byeenkomste, sê sy, bied 'geen agenda, niks om te bewys — net gemeenskaplike grond.' Die bande wat hier gevorm is, het tot werklike wetgewingswinnings gelei. Murkowski skryf haar persoonlike verhouding met voormalige senator Barbara Boxer toe aan om verskille op die snelwegwet te verhelp tydens hul oorvleuelingstermyn. Gillibrand herinner hoe Snowe en Murkowski strategiese raad gegee het — alhoewel nie amptelike sponsors nie — tydens haar stryd om die 9/11-first responders-siektebil aan te neem. 'Ons is natuurlike bondgenote,' het Snowe gesê. 'Ons vertrou mekaar se raad.' Hulle skryf hul sukses toe aan minder ego, dieper luister en ’n gedeelde begrip van wat dit beteken om ’n vrou te wees in ’n histories manlike instelling. 'Ons is mededingend — ons sou hier nie wees nie — maar ons hoef nie al die erkenning te eis nie,' het Murkowski opgemerk. 'Dis nie my manier of die pad nie. Dis hoe ons sake doen.' Hoewel hulle eens is oor kernvraagstukke wat vroue aangaan — van gesondheid tot werksplekregte — het Murkowski erken dat sy gestem het teen die verband van die Affordable Care Act se anticonsepsie-voorskrif in 2012, ’n beslissing wat in Alaska op weerstand gestuit het. Sy spyt dit. 'Ek wens ons het daardie gesprek gehad,' het sy erken, en kritiseer haar eie party se houding teenoor vroue se gesondheid. 'Baie vroue voel aangeval.' Omring deur foto’s van Geraldine Ferraro, Madeleine Albright en die Meisjies Scouts, dank haar kollegas Mikulski vir die bou van hierdie heilige plek. Gillibrand onthou hoe Mikulski haar benader het toe sy eerste aangedui is: 'Sy het my deur die stelsel gelei.' Na 12 858 dae diens, kan Mikulski se grootste nalatenskap nie haar rekordbrekende diensperiode wees nie — maar die duurzame kultuur van beskaafdheid wat sy gehelp het skep. 'Ek sal nie altyd hier wees nie,' het sy gesê. 'Maar ek hoop hierdie gees bly.'

article_content: It’s still rolling. The red paint may be chipped, the bodywork dented, and the accelerator pressed just a little less firmly — but the juggernaut keeps moving. Before kickoff, the idea that a home draw with Dundee could be seen as a point gained by Aberdeen would have seemed absurd. Eight straight league wins without conceding tend to breed an all-or-nothing mindset. Yet by the time Ryan Jack bundled home the sixth and final goal deep into injury time, no one at Pittodrie was mourning a lost two points — except the stunned, silent sea of dark blue supporters. David Goodwillie celebrated his opening goal with Adam Rooney, but the real story unfolded later. Trailing 3-1 with just three minutes of normal time remaining, Aberdeen’s rescue mission was as astonishing as their earlier dominance. This was no ordinary afternoon. It was chaotic, surreal — a day where neither laughter nor tears felt fitting for either manager. Derek McInnes leaned toward relief; Paul Hartley, his opposite number, searched for silver linings. Dundee were brilliant in spells — particularly in the 10 minutes before halftime, when Gary Irvine and Greg Stewart finished stunning team moves to cancel Goodwillie’s opener. They were sharp, organized, and nearly deserved their 3-1 lead after Gary Harkins’ volley deflected off Ash Taylor to beat Scott Brown. But as the clock ticked, their legs turned to lead. Their defense froze in their own box. Aberdeen refused to surrender. Substitutes Willo Flood, Cammy Smith, and above all, 19-year-old Lawrence Shankland, injected urgency. With 17,000 fans roaring, they clawed back with two late goals. If this counts as a bad day by Aberdeen’s recent standards, they’ll gladly take these rollercoasters. While they won’t want to rely on Houdini-like escapes to win the title, sometimes — just sometimes — they’re necessary. Shankland, a former Queen’s Park teammate of Andrew Robertson, came off the bench with seven minutes left to replace Rooney. He didn’t score — but he did everything else. He drew the foul that led to Jonny Hayes’ 87th-minute penalty. Then, in the second minute of stoppage time, he rose to head the ball perfectly for Ryan Jack to bundle in the equalizer. The celebration was as wild as any last-gasp win. Though their lead atop the table is now just two points over Celtic, Dundee learned the hard way: Aberdeen’s understanding of ‘defeat’ is fading fast. 'We all believed,' Shankland said. 'Ten minutes is enough to score two goals — we proved that.' The script had been clear: Goodwillie’s early strike, set up by Niall McGinn stealing the ball from Irvine, seemed to signal a rout. For 20 minutes, the only question was how many Aberdeen would win by. Rooney missed a tap-in, Jack’s shot went wide, and Dundee couldn’t catch their breath — until, suddenly, they did. In 180 seconds, Aberdeen’s 757-minute clean sheet evaporated. Irvine scored with a lung-busting run; Stewart curled a sublime finish into the bottom corner. Harkins’ volley, deflected by Taylor, made it 3-1. But the tide turned when referee Alan Muir awarded a penalty. Hayes converted it, and Dundee cracked. Shay Logan’s hopeful cross was guided on by Shankland — Jack pounced. Every champion team needs moments like this. McInnes called it a ‘huge point’ but avoided speculating on its title implications. At Pittodrie, improvement remains the mantra. Shankland, who’s scored 19 goals for Aberdeen’s development side this season, is growing into a vital presence — proof that their squad depth matches their ambition. 'I just tried to get in good positions,' Shankland grinned. 'The gaffer told me to do what I could. My job’s to score — but assists count too.' He admitted he didn’t take the penalty: 'There are more experienced lads. Jonny took it well.' Despite competing with Goodwillie and Rooney for a starting spot, Shankland sees a path forward. 'We’ve got a strong squad. The strikers are scoring, so I’ve got to be patient, work hard, and make the most of my chances.' He names Jack as an example: 'He took his opportunity — that’s what I need to do.' With Ash Taylor sidelined for a month, McInnes must reshuffle his defense ahead of Friday’s trip to St Johnstone. But Aberdeen aren’t done yet.

Met Ash Taylor vir ’n maand buite, moet McInnes sy stukke herorden voor Vrydag se reis na St Johnstone. Maar Aberdeen is nog nie klaar nie.

article_content: In 1991, Seth Owusu boarded a plane from rural Ghana to the United States with no prior experience using a computer. Two decades later, he’s transformed that gap into a mission: bringing digital literacy to African children through the nonprofit he founded, Entire Village Computers Organization (EVCO). Based in Washington, D.C., EVCO collects discarded computers from donors in developed nations, repairs and upgrades them in Owusu’s cluttered garage, and ships them to underserved schools across Ghana and Nigeria. But the project doesn’t stop at hardware. Each donation comes with a three-year commitment—training for teachers, tech support, and community outreach. Schools become hubs where entire villages gather to learn, connect, and grow. Owusu, who moved to the U.S. at 24, credits a visit by missionaries to his childhood school as his turning point. They traveled far to help strangers, and that act of kindness stuck with him. 'It taught me that even if you have nothing, you can still give something powerful,' he says. Since 2004, EVCO has delivered 233 computers across 25 labs, entirely funded by Owusu, his family, and a handful of loyal supporters. Beyond fixing machines, Owusu uses his trips back home to deliver talks on HIV prevention and teenage pregnancy, urging communities to value education over early labor. He’s now working to extend EVCO to Sierra Leone, though funding shortages mean he often has to say no to other requests. Still, he remains undeterred. 'We’re not just giving computers—we’re planting seeds,' he explains. 'The kids we help today are the ones who’ll shape the world tomorrow. If we want change, we start with them.'

Maar die projek hou nie net op by hardeeware nie. Elke skenk kom met 'n driejaarige verpligting—opleiding vir opvoeders, tegniese ondersteuning en gemeenskaplike uitreiking. Skole word sentrum waar hele dorpe versamel om te leer, te koppel en te groei. Owusu, wat op 24 na die V.S. verhuis het, dank 'n besoek deur sendelinge aan sy kinderjare-skool as sy draaipunt. article_content: Many seniors struggle with overwhelming medical bills, and a congressional investigation has revealed that federal websites designed to help Medicare beneficiaries make informed health care choices are falling dangerously short. Instead of providing clear information on out-of-pocket costs and quality of care, these sites leave users confused and ill-equipped. The nonpartisan Government Accountability Office (GAO) found critical weaknesses in five consumer-information websites operated by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). These platforms—intended to compare hospitals, nursing homes, physicians, and other providers—suffer from confusing layouts, incomplete data, and a lack of personalized tools. As a result, consumers cannot reliably assess value or make sound decisions. The GAO report, obtained by The Associated Press ahead of its public release, highlights that CMS has no standardized processes for delivering useful, understandable information to patients. Even as the federal government prepares to launch new websites focused on hospice, inpatient rehab, and long-term care, current barriers remain unchanged—and unlikely to be resolved soon. Comparisons with third-party vendors showed that private sites offer far more consistent and detailed pricing and quality data—for procedures like gallbladder surgery, MRIs, and maternity care—than official government portals. Meanwhile, CMS sites often omit vital metrics, such as patient-reported outcomes after colonoscopies or hip replacements. Critics liken CMS’s star-rating system for nursing homes to appliance ratings, reducing life-altering decisions to simplistic icons. Although CMS officials say they plan to improve transparency—including expanding star ratings and estimating out-of-pocket expenses—GAO found no evidence these changes have been implemented. Resistance from medical providers, including the American Medical Association’s opposition to releasing physician billing data, has slowed progress. Yet lawmakers like Sen. Pat Toomey (PA) and Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (NH) argue that patients deserve full access to cost and quality data to drive better care and lower prices. Despite a 2011 commitment under the Affordable Care Act to deliver clear, complete health care information, the government continues to fall short. The GAO concludes that without stronger policies and measurable goals, CMS will remain ineffective in empowering Medicare beneficiaries.

In plaas van duidelike inligting oor uit-pocketkoste en kwaliteit van sorg te verskaf, laat hierdie gasse gebruikers verward en onvoorbereid. Die nie-partisane Regeringsverantwoordelikheidskantoor (GAO) het kritieke swaktes in vyf verbruiker-inligtingwebwerwe gevind wat deur die Sentrum vir Medicare en Medicaid Diens (CMS) bedryf word. Hierdie platforme—bedoel om hospitale, verpleeghuisse, dokters en ander verskaffers te vergelyk—ly aan verwarrende opsette, onvolledige data en ‘n gebrek aan gepersonaliseerde hulpmiddels. Gevolglik kan verbruikers nie betroubaar waarde bepaal of gesonde besluite neem nie. Die GAO-verslag, verkry deur The Associated Press voor sy openbare vrylating, beklemtoon dat CMS geen standaardprosesse het om bruikbare, begrypbare inligting aan pasiënte te lewer nie. Selfs terwyl die federale regering voorberei om nuwe webwerwe te lanseer wat fokus op hospiese, ingeslote herstel en langtermynsorg, bly huidige hindernisse onveranderd—en onwaarskynlik om binnekort opgelos te word. Vergelykings met derdeparty-verskaffers het getoon dat privaatwerwe baie meer konsekwente en gedetailleerde prys- en kwaliteitsdata bied—vir prosedures soos galblaassurgie, MRT’s en materniteitsorg—as amptelike regeringsportale. Tuis word CMS-webwerwe dikwels kritiese metrieke soos pasiëntgerapporteerde uitslae na kolonoskopieë of heupvervanginge weggelaat. Kritici vergelyk CMS se sterre-beoordelingstelsel vir verpleeghuisse met toestandbeoordelings, en verminder lewensveranderende besluite tot eenvoudige ikone. Alhoewel CMS-amptenare sê hulle plan om transparansie te verbeter—inclusief die uitbreiding van sterrebeoordelings en skatting van uit-pocketkoste—het die GAO geen bewyse gevind dat hierdie veranderinge geïmplementeer is nie. Weerstand van mediese verskaffers, insluitend die Amerikaanse Mediese Vereniging se teenstelling teen die vrylating van dokterrekeningdata, het die vooruitgang vertraag. Maar wetgewers soos Sen. Pat Toomey (PA) en Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (NH) argumenteer dat pasiënte volle toegang tot koste- en kwaliteitsinligting verdien om beter sorg en laer pryse te dryf. Ten spyte van ‘n 2011-verbintenis onder die Affordable Care Act om duidelike, volledige gesondheidsorginligting te verskaf, bly die regering tekort. Die GAO sluit af dat sonder sterkere beleide en meetbare doelwitte, CMS ondoeltreffend sal bly in die bemagtiging van Medicare-betrokkenes.

article_content: Anna and Ella, identical-looking twins separated at birth, were reunited on Saturday after their adoptive families discovered they were biologically related. Both pairs of parents had long noted striking similarities between the girls — including shared mannerisms and facial expressions — and became suspicious when they learned the girls shared the same birthday. Over the summer, the families agreed to a DNA test, which confirmed Anna and Ella are fraternal twins. Ella’s family, who live in Michigan, visited Anna’s home in North Carolina en route to Myrtle Beach, marking their first meeting. Initially shy, the girls quickly bonded once they stepped away from adult supervision. Neither set of adoptive parents had been informed during the adoption process that their daughter had a twin. The Cuares family was told Ella had been found in a park; the Kandls were told Anna had been left on a hospital doorstep. The families had stayed in touch through Facebook, where photos and the shared birthday sparked their suspicions. 'I’ll look at Ella, and I can just see that they’re related,' said Ella’s father, Randy Cuares. Anna’s mother, Karen Kandl, added, 'They have so many of the same facial expressions — things like that catch me off guard.' 'It’s a connection we can’t give her,' said Ella’s mother, Teresa Cuares. 'It’s something we could never provide — and now we have it.' Though Anna already has an older sister, Becky, her mother believes knowing she has a twin is invaluable. The families plan to remain closely connected as the girls grow up.

article_content: Real Madrid returned to winning form on Saturday with a 2-0 home victory over Deportivo La Coruña at the Santiago Bernabéu. Goals from Spanish midfielder Isco and French striker Karim Benzema — one before and one after halftime — sealed the win. Despite dominating possession, Real’s performance was far from fluent. Deportivo came close to equalizing early in the second half when Celso Borges struck the post, and goalkeeper Iker Casillas made a crucial save to deny Oriol Riera. The win offered relief after a 4-0 drubbing by city rivals Atlético Madrid last weekend. However, manager Carlo Ancelotti expressed concern over his team’s disjointed play and the muted display from star forward Cristiano Ronaldo, who failed to score for the third straight La Liga match — the first such stretch since 2013. Ronaldo, who set up Benzema’s goal and hit the bar himself, was criticized by fans earlier in the week for hosting his 30th birthday celebration soon after the derby loss. He missed a close-range chance just before Isco opened the scoring. Ancelotti told AFP: 'It was a difficult week, but we’ve come out with a win. The team was anxious at first, but the fans supported us and understood what we’re going through.' Real Madrid now lead La Liga by four points, though Barcelona could cut that gap to one point if they defeat Levante on Sunday. Elsewhere, West Brom beat West Ham 4-0 thanks to two goals from Brown Ideye, plus strikes from James Morrison and Saido Berahino. Liverpool overturned a deficit to beat Crystal Palace 2-1, with goals from Daniel Sturridge and Sadio Mané. In lower-league cup action, Blackburn stunned Stoke City 4-1, while Reading defeated Derby County 1-0 thanks to a Yakubu winner. In Ligue 1, Paris Saint-Germain drew 2-2 with Caen after conceding two late goals while down to nine men. PSG led through Zlatan Ibrahimović and Ezequiel Lavezzi, but injuries to Serge Aurier and Lucas forced them to play the final minutes with fewer players. Despite holding firm for most of the extra time, Emiliano Sala and Hervé Bazile netted in the 89th and 92nd minutes to snatch a draw. PSG remain third, behind Marseille and league leaders Lyon, who travel to FC Lorient on Sunday.

article_content: London bus drivers will no longer accept cash payments onboard when new measures take effect this summer. Transport for London (TfL) has announced several changes, including allowing passengers with insufficient Oyster card credit to complete a full journey before topping up. TfL cited declining cash usage as the primary reason for the shift, noting that 99% of passengers already use Oyster cards, prepaid tickets, contactless payment cards, or concessionary passes. Cash payments on London buses will be discontinued by mid-2014. Leon Daniels, Managing Director of Surface Transport at TfL, said: 'The decision to stop accepting cash fares on London buses reflects how people in our city are changing the way they pay for goods and services—including bus travel. Paying with Oyster or a contactless card is not only the most affordable option, but also speeds up boarding and reduces delays.' TfL estimates that accepting cash costs £24 million annually. Eliminating this option will generate significant savings, all of which will be reinvested into improving the transport network. The changes will be implemented by mid-2014, pending successful testing of new technology. During a recent public consultation, approximately one-third of respondents supported removing cash fares. TfL noted that 99% of its customers now use contactless or Oyster payments, and processing cash currently costs £24 million per year. Around 75% of consultation responses came from individuals who do not use cash to pay for bus fares. TfL’s new 'One More Journey' feature will permit passengers with a positive card balance—below the single fare (£1.45)—to take one additional bus trip before needing to recharge. TfL will also provide updated guidance to all 24,500 London bus drivers to ensure consistent support for vulnerable passengers. The Oyster card was publicly launched on June 30, 2003, and approximately 60 million cards have been issued since then.

article_content: Alden Ehrenreich and writer-director Chloe Domont revealed that numerous viewers have shared personal experiences closely mirroring those depicted in their film, Fair Play. The movie, which premiered at Sundance and is now streaming on Netflix, has sparked widespread conversation throughout 2023. At Deadline’s Contenders Film: Los Angeles event on Saturday, Ehrenreich recounted a poignant moment from Sundance: 'You're walking down the street, and people just come up to you. One woman approached me and said, 'My husband and I work together. I make more than he does. We’ve been secretly dating—and no one knows. This is our story.' Ehrenreich and Phoebe Dynevor portray Luke and Emily, a couple navigating intense professional rivalry and emotional strain after Emily receives a promotion Luke believed was his. Domont shared that many women have sent her lengthy emails detailing how deeply they relate to Emily’s journey. 'There’s nothing more rewarding than hearing someone say, 'I feel seen,' after watching your film,' she said. Domont also noted the film has ignited meaningful dialogue among couples. 'I’ve seen pairs leave theaters and immediately start talking—then one partner says something, and the other responds, 'Oh, that’s what you thought?' You just know the car ride home is going to be interesting.' Ehrenreich believes the film’s power lies in its emotional honesty—not as a political statement, but as a raw expression of Domont’s own experiences. 'It had that ring of humanity,' he said. 'That’s what made it exciting—and dangerous.' Domont had admired Ehrenreich’s work long before Hail, Caesar!, and felt he was perfect for the role because he never judged the character. 'I knew that was the way in,' she said. 'And I never judged him either. If we’d both come in with judgment, it wouldn’t have been compelling.' For the role of Emily, Domont was drawn to Dynevor after her breakout in Bridgerton. 'Emily is a rising star in finance,' Domont explained. 'So I wanted a rising star in film too. Dynevor had that energy from Bridgerton—but hadn’t yet exploded in features. It felt perfectly on-brand.'
translated_content: Alden Ehrenreich en skrywer-regisseur Chloe Domont het bekendgemaak dat talryke kykers persoonlike ervarings deel wat noukeurig ooreenstem met dié wat in hul rolprent, Fair Play, vertel word. Die fliek, wat op Sundance premieer het en nou op Netflix beskikbaar is, het in 2023 wye gesprekke uitgelok. Tydens die Deadline’s Contenders Film: Los Angeles-geleentheid op Saterdag het Ehrenreich ’n pynlike oomblik van Sundance vertel: 'Jy loop op die straat en mense kom net na jou toe. Een vrou het na my toe gekom en gesê, 'My man en ek werk saam. Ek verdien meer as hy. Ons het ’n geheime verhouding gehad—en niemand weet nie. Dit is ons verhaal.' Ehrenreich en Phoebe Dynevor speel Luke en Emily, ’n paar wat deur intensiese professionele konflik en emosionele spanning gaan nadat Emily ’n bevordering kry wat Luke verwag het. Domont het gesê dat baie vroue haar lang e-posse gestuur het waarin hulle beskryf hoe hulle die Emily-rol so goed kan identifiseer. 'Daar is niks belonender as om iemand te hoor sê, 'Ek voel gesien,' ná die fliek,' het sy gesê. Domont het ook opgemerk dat die fliek betekenisvolle dialoog tussen pare uitgelok het. 'Ek het pare gesien wat uit die teater kom en onmiddellik begin praat—dan sê een van hulle iets en die ander reageer, 'Oh, dit is wat jy gedink het?' Jy weet net die rit huis toe gaan interessant wees.' Ehrenreich glo die fliek se krag lê in sy emosionele eerlikheid—nie as ’n politieke verklaring nie, maar as ’n rauwe uitdrukking van Domont se eie ervarings. 'Dis het daardie menslike klank gehad,' het hy gesê. 'Dit is wat dit spannend—en gevaarlik—gemaak het.' Domont het reeds lank voor Hail, Caesar! van Ehrenreich se werk gehou en gevoel hy was perfek vir die rol omdat hy die karakter nooit beoordeel het. 'Ek het geweet dit was die pad in,' het sy gesê. 'En ek het hom ook nooit beoordeel nie. As ons albei met oordeel ingekom het, sou dit nie indrukwekkend gewees het nie.' Vir die rol van Emily was Domont aangetrokke tot Dynevor ná haar deurbraak in Bridgerton. 'Emily is ’n opklimmende ster in finansies,' het Domont verklaar. 'Dus het ek ’n opklimmende ster in rolprente wil hê. Dynevor het daardie energie van Bridgerton gehad—maar nog nie in rolprente geëksplodeer nie. Dit het perfek by Emily gepas.'

article_content: Teresa Romero, a 44-year-old Spanish nurse who survived Ebola, is devastated that authorities euthanized her dog, Excalibur, while she was hospitalized. Romero contracted the virus in October after caring for two infected priests at Madrid’s Carlos III Hospital—Manuel Garcia Viejo, who died on September 25, and Miguel Pajares, who died in August after returning from Liberia. Although Romero tested negative for Ebola weeks later, Spanish officials ordered Excalibur’s euthanasia as a precautionary measure, citing potential transmission risks. This decision ignited nationwide protests, with over 390,000 people signing a petition demanding the dog’s life be spared. Demonstrators, including healthcare workers, marched through Madrid calling for Health Minister Ana Mato to resign. Romero’s husband, Javier Limon, told El País: 'She is asking herself why they killed the dog, who wasn’t to blame for anything.' In contrast, the U.S. chose to quarantine and test Bentley, the dog of nurse Nina Pham in Dallas—both tests came back negative, and the animal was spared. Romero was treated with supportive care, including human serum containing antibodies from Ebola survivors, and the experimental antiviral favipiravir, according to El Mundo. Her recovery has fueled further criticism of Spain’s handling of the situation, as experts and activists argue Excalibur could have been safely quarantined like Bentley. Though no evidence confirmed Excalibur carried the virus, authorities acted on precaution, drawing sharp comparisons to the more measured U.S. response.

Romero het die virus opgedoen in Oktober ná dat sy twee besmette priesters versorg het by die Carlos III-siekehuis in Madrid—Manuel Garcia Viejo, wat op 25 September oorlede is, en Miguel Pajares, wat in Augustus oorlede is nadat hy teruggekeer het van Liberië. Hierdie beslissing het landwye proteste losgemaak, met meer as 390 000 mense wat 'n petisie onderteken het om die hond se lewe te red. Demonstrante, insluitend gesondheidswerkers, het deur Madrid gemarsjeer en eis dat Gesondheidsminister Ana Mato afgetree moet word. Romero is behandel met ondersteunende sorg, insluitend menslike serum wat antibliggame van Ebola-oorlewendes bevat, en die eksperimentele antivirale middel favipiravir, volgens El Mundo. Haar herstel het verdere kritiek op Spanje se hantering van die situasie veroorsaak, aangesien deskundiges en aktiviste argumenteer dat Excalibur soos Bentley veilig in kwarentyn kon gewees het. Hoewel geen bewyse bevestig het dat Excalibur die virus gedra het nie, het die owerhede op voorbereiding gehandel, wat skerp vergelykings met die meer gemete VSA-respons teweeggebring het.

article_content: Sharon Helman, director of the Phoenix Veterans Affairs Health Care System, received an $8,500 performance bonus in April 2014 — the same month the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) inspector general opened an investigation into the deaths of 40 veterans linked to falsified waitlist records. She had also received a $9,345 bonus in 2013. Public outrage erupted after Congressman David Scott (D-GA) publicly condemned the bonuses on national television, prompting the VA to rescind both awards. VA officials later stated the bonuses were issued due to an 'administrative error.' The scandal intensified as bipartisan calls mounted for VA Secretary Eric Shinseki to resign. Even as President Barack Obama defended Shinseki, citing the need to await the official inspector general report, prominent Democrats — including Rep. John Barrow (D-GA) — broke ranks to demand his removal. Rep. Jeff Miller (R-FL) criticized the VA on CNN, rejecting claims that the issue stemmed from a 'low-level administrative error.' Speaker John Boehner echoed this sentiment, declaring, 'We’ve not just let them down — we’ve let them die.' While many acknowledge Shinseki’s distinguished military service, critics argue that accountability must begin at the top. President Obama stated that if the allegations are true, the behavior is 'dishonorable and disgraceful' and will not be tolerated — but he continues to withhold judgment until the IG report is complete.

Sy het ook 'n $9 345-bonus in 2013 ontvang.
